We have an opening for a Systems Engineer in the Technical Services Department (TSD) within the Environment, Safety and Health (ES&H) Directorate. As a Systems Engineer you will support radioanalytical laboratories and radiation exposure dosimetry groups to demonstrate comprehensive compliance with radiation protection standards. This position may offer a hybrid schedule, which includes the flexibility to work from home one or more days per week, after a probationary period. The specifics of the hybrid schedule, including the exact number of days required in the office and virtual work options may vary based on the needs of the team and the organization. You will Leverage nuclear engineering domain knowledge to develop, enhance and maintain laboratory codes to monitor radiation exposure for LLNL workers. Ensure analytical results, dose evaluations/assessments, and reports are of the highest accuracy and quality. Collaborate with IT support personnel in the development, upgrade, and maintenance of the personnel dosimetry databases and their applications. Provide technical assistance to TSD and other ES&H divisions in addressing internal and external dosimetry issues. Conduct studies and prepare reports on relevant technical issues. Develop codes and tools to automate the processing, analysis, and archival of dosimetry data. Explore a variety of approaches within established practices and procedures and recommend and implement improvements or new processes as appropriate. Follow defined policies and practices in selecting methods, techniques, and evaluation criteria for obtaining results, based on in depth analysis of multiple identifiable factors. Work with dosimetry technical specialist to prepare, review, and submit reports. Perform other duties as assigned. Ability to secure and maintain a U.S. DOE Q-level security clearance which requires U.S. citizenship. Bachelor’s degree in nuclear engineering, radiation protection, a related science, engineering, or related technical field or the equivalent combination of education and related experience. Comprehensive technical understanding of external dosimetry including universal nuclear accident dosimeters. Practical experience and/or working knowledge in one or more of the following: radiation detection/counting instrumentation, statistical evaluation, Thermo-luminescent dosimeter (TLD) processing including ability to analyze information to determine proper methods and techniques. Experience working with teams developing and deploying high quality software products; specifically, gathering requirements, implementing software, debugging and remediating issues, coupled with prior coding and/or automation experience. Proficient verbal and written communication skills necessary to effectively collaborate in a team environment and to present and communicate technical information to technical staff and management. Effective organizational skills with attention to detail necessary to handle multiple moderately complex tasks in a demanding environment with conflicting priorities, tight and changing deadlines, and frequent interruptions while providing high-level customer service and good follow through. Experience working independently and in a team environment with a broad cross-section of people and organizations, and meeting schedules. Qualifications We Desire Master’s degree in a related field. Understanding of applicable Federal regulations including 10 CFR 835. Experience with the Department of Energy Laboratory Accreditation Program (DOELAP) process for internal or external dosimetry systems. Experience working in a research and development environment (e.g., DOE National Laboratory) with a broad range of radiation types, exposure geometries, and dose rates. Broad experience with programming languages, data management systems, SQL, Oracle server databases and creating SQL Queries. Pay Range $129,150- $163,764 Annually This is the lowest to highest salary we in good faith believe we would pay for this role at the time of this posting; pay will not be below any applicable local minimum wage. An employee’s position within the salary range will be based on several factors including, but not limited to, specific competencies, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, seniority, geographic location, performance, and business or organizational needs.

This is a remote position with up to 50% domestic travel required. Candidates may reside in the Southwest or Western part of the United States and should expect frequent national travel. The AbbVie Employer NAE is responsible for supporting and implementing strategic business initiatives in response to the changing healthcare environment, deployed specifically to national Employer Stakeholders via the AbbVie Employer Team with a focus on improving workforce health and productivity and maximizing strategic access to AbbVie’s therapies. The Employer NAE will be accountable for building effective stakeholder strategies and engagements that are on the forefront of emerging concerns impacting employee access, affordability, disease state awareness/management and medication value and access. This includes healthcare decision-makers (HCDMs) within national employer plan sponsors, employee benefit consultants (EBCs), and employer coalitions, as well as emerging stakeholders/influencers/vendors, national organizations, and professional/advocacy organizations. The Employer NAE provides branded and unbranded messaging to employers and employer influencers/KOLs regarding the value and differentiation of AbbVie therapies to accelerate access to treatment and the use of benefit plan designs to identify and minimize barriers to affordable and predictable Rx access. The NAE also delivers messaging relating to disease state and burden of illness to increase the awareness of treatment solutions and explore solutions and develop best practices/case studies. The Employer NAE will provide leadership to distinguish AbbVie in the employer channel, be a convener of stakeholders and regional/national KOLs and SMEs, and provide strategic insights internally in support of evolving business needs to ensure timely awareness of market changes and trends and inform internal business leads to ensure a rapid response to external disruptors and Rx management strategies which impact affordable access to AbbVie’s therapies. This role is highly collaborative and consultative and requires partnering and interfacing with numerous cross-functional teams (Market Access leadership, Payer Strategy and Cross Portfolio Strategy and Pipeline, Training, Market Analytics Business Insights, Business Evolution Strategy Development (BESD), Brand Sales/Marketing, Government Affairs and Policy, Corporate Strategy, US Medical Affairs/Value & Access and Medical Outcomes Science & Science Liaisons (MOSLs); Finance, Legal, Compliance, Communications/PR, Field Reimbursement Leadership, Brand Sales/Marketing teams and internal Centers of Excellence (CoE). The NAE must demonstrate the ability to anticipate and act proactively and effectively in uncertain situations. Additionally, the NAE requires significant collaboration with the Corporate Accounts KAM teams, providing timely insights regarding evolving contracting trends and evolving rebate models, educating client-facing teams, and providing updates regarding downstream employer clients and formulary initiatives. This position does not have direct reports but does require the ability to manage and lead without authority across cross-functional teams while also being able to work independently and productively. The Employer NAE is the lead for regional employer initiatives working in conjunction with the Regional Account Executive (RAE) teams and Regional Directors, as well as compliant collaboration with the Population Heath Account Executive (PHAE) team. This includes identifying opportunities and/or employer access issues and training/educating and executing on use of Employer Team resources and messaging to health plan, health system, PBM and employer customers. This role also is a key collaborator with other national field-based teams including the Field Reimbursement team, educating team members on market disruptors and problem-solving on employer-focused access issues. The Employer NAE serves as a key role in cataloguing key disruptors and potential patient disruption and analyzing potential financial (Gross to Net) impact, as well as working across internal stakeholders to develop and execute mitigation strategies. Major Duties and Responsibilities: Proactively engage with existing employer stakeholders and identify/influence emerging employer stakeholders across the US. Identify insights, positions and potential impact of new and emerging employer stakeholders and vendors. Build proactive share of voice with employer customers and influencers on Rx management topics. Support and contribute to internal Strategy Teams regarding emerging strategies and identification of external SMEs. Collaborate with Government Affairs/Policy/Strategy Directors to connect and convene with new and emerging stakeholders and advocates. Work in conjunction with Employer Team Director and Marketing Director (and collaboratively with Principal National MOSL, Employer Channel) relative to employer channel resource development and messaging. Develop and deliver stakeholder appropriate resources to support access for the expanding AbbVie portfolio (DSA decks, case studies, condensed employer value-prop decks, case studies and benefit plan design resources) Cultivate national employer KOLs and advocates to help shape external education and policy in collaboration with Government Affairs/Policy/Strategy teams. Monitor, inform and deliver market insights to internal business partners. Lead education initiatives in conjunction with Market Access Training on key trends impacting purchasers and AbbVie access/gross-to-net. Establish AbbVie as credible source for non-branded information and disseminate via industry meetings and electronic sites / social media (consistent with AbbVie Communications/PR guidelines). Support efforts to integrate Employer Strategy into AbbVie Business Planning process. Assist AbbVie Employer Corporate Account Team Leader with managing budget and execution of sponsorships and memberships, consistent with AbbVie Office of Ethics and Compliance (OEC) guidelines. Establish AbbVie as a national leader and key partner in the employer channel. Work with Big 3 PBM/GPO KAM teams and respective rebate analysts to ensure contract compliance. Quantify volume/sales associated with employer child accounts and access changes. Participate in internal task forces relating to member/patient access. Bachelor’s degree in Business, Life Sciences, or a related field required. Minimum of 5 years of Account Executive or Market Access experience within the healthcare industry; employee benefits consulting (EBC) experience and/or PBM experience is a plus. Proven ability to operate effectively in large, complex geographies, influence diverse stakeholders, and deliver commercial results. Demonstrated capability in negotiation, stakeholder engagement, and strategic planning/development and execution. Strong analytical skills, especially related to Rx contract terms/language and the commercial payor market. Effective communication and presentation skills (written and oral) with both technical and non-technical audiences. Experience managing complexity and collaborating with cross-functional, matrixed teams; agility and team-orientation required. Customer-centric approach and proven ability to act as primary point of contact for internal and external stakeholders. Ability to work autonomously, manage ambiguity, and identify/influence key customers. Understanding of the evolving healthcare environment—including ACA, CAA, ERISA, clinical guidelines, and formulary/utilization management. Adept at delivering product and disease state value proposition materials to a range of customers. Highest ethical standards and compliance with AbbVie Office of Ethics and Compliance (OEC) policies. Significant domestic travel required (up to 50%) for customer interactions, industry meetings and internal meetings. An essential requirement of your position is to satisfy all applicable health care industry representative (HCIR) credentialing requirements to gain and maintain entry into facilities and organizations that are in your assigned territory. You must also be in good standing and/or eligible to obtain these credentials. Driving a personal auto or company car or truck, or a powered piece of material handling equipment. Valid driver’s license: Ability to pass a pre-employment drug screening test and meet safe driving requirements. Preferred: 10+ years’ experience in pharmaceutical, Rx supply chain, employee benefit consulting, or healthcare organization. Deep understanding of commercial business models and payor markets.

Suggest, adapt, and, as appropriate, implement new or improved experimental protocols/techniques, consulting relevant literature as needed. Build and maintain strong collaborative relationships with peers and cross-functional partners. Foster a learning environment, encourage diverse ideas, and support continuous process improvement. Understand and adhere strictly to corporate standards for conduct, safety, quality, and proper handling of materials. Bachelor’s degree with at least 3 years (Associate Scientist II) or 5 years (Scientist I) relevant experience; or Master’s degree with no additional experience (Associate Scientist II) or typically +2 years of relevant experience (Scientist I). Strong technical background in Separations Science, with theoretical and practical knowledge required to independently carry out job functions. Demonstrated proficiency in developing, troubleshooting, and modifying chromatographic methods and purification protocols. Broad expertise in analytical techniques, with emphasis on chromatography, compound purification, and spectral analysis. Ability to search scientific literature and evaluate potential solutions to research problems. The Center for Global Security Research (CGSR) was established at Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL) in 1996 to bring together experts from the science, technology, and policy communities to address pressing national security challenges. For over 20 years, CGSR has engaged diverse perspectives on topics important to national security, deterrence, diplomacy, dual-use technology, arms control, nonproliferation, space, cyber, biosecurity, and energy security. We have openings in Fall 2026 for undergraduate students to engage in practical research on global security topics. Students will work with CGSR over the duration of three to four months as a research associate (RA). RAs will engage in practical research to further their educational and career goals, while also supporting the development of strategies for national security and LLNL’s mission focus areas. Examples of relevant fields of research include nuclear deterrence, arms control, nonproliferation, emerging technologies, cybersecurity, space, biological & chemical security, and energy security. CGSR’s objectives are as follows: To explore the dynamics of potential 21st century strategic conflicts (i.e., those with a potential nuclear aspect) and to formulate ideas about how to achieve U.S. deterrence and other objectives in such conflicts. To explore the sources and characteristics of strategic competition in the emerging security environment and to formulate organizing concepts to enhance the competitive position of the United States and its allies and partners over the long term. To identify whether and how technically based approaches can address new challenges to national and international security. To catalyze broader national and international thinking about the requirements of effective deterrence, assurance, and strategic stability in a changed and changing security environment. To assist in the development of new generations of experts motivated by a clear view of the changed and changing security environment. More information on CGSR, its research focus areas, and its publications can be found at https://cgsr.llnl.gov/ . This job will be closed to applicants on May 31, 2026. You will Conduct an independent research project on an agreed upon topic aligned with CGSR/LLNL research priorities under the supervision of CGSR staff. Support CGSR/LLNL through contributions to ongoing research activities. Tasks may include contributing to literature reviews, annotated bibliographies, and workshop summary reports. Attend relevant research seminars, speakers’ series, and workshops. Present research to LLNL staff at end of the assignment. Prepare end-of-assignment technical report or publication. Perform all assignments in accordance with ES&H, security, and business practice requirements and policies. Perform other duties as assigned. Must be eligible to access the Laboratory in compliance with Section 3112 of the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA). See Additional Information section below for details. Must be currently enrolled in an accredited university or have completed AA/AS degree in a field of research aligned with CGSR analytic priorities. Areas of study include international relations and/or security, political science, economics, public policy, emerging technologies, nonproliferation, energy, biosecurity, foreign language studies, or related fields. Demonstrated academic and/or professional achievement in a relevant field of research aligned with CGSR analytic priorities. Strong record of independent research and publication, or a strong proposal of research to be done while at CGSR and in future academic and professional settings. Ability to work in a team environment. Pay Range $23.26 - $31.62 Hourly This position is under a step structure. Please note that the step is determined by your academic level. Transcripts are required.

Expert delivery of anatomical/procedural information and training, including the appropriate use of anatomical terminology to train injection paradigms/postures while highlighting various anatomical and injection insights and considerations. Provide education and clinical/injection training for residents, fellows, and other key hospital personnel. Collaborate with other Account Specialist to promote the product for approved indications and execute individual, department, or group resident/fellow trainings within hospital/health system accounts. Comply with all company policies, required reports, requests and promotional compliance and effectively manages AbbVie field assets. Effectively utilize AbbVie's sales and data resources to enhance productivity and growth of AbbVie products while implementing U.S. Marketing Plan. Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in health, sciences, pharmacy or business-related field preferred or relevant and equivalent industry experience required Relevant and equivalent industry experience required in lieu of a bachelor’s degree is at least five (5) years of technical experience with three (3) or more years of experience within sales preferred and a high school diploma/GED required Documented history of strong sales performance, preferably in a clinical/technical/consultative sales role with multiple decision makers is preferred. Experience with Buy & Bill and/or Specialty Pharmacy products is preferred, in both health systems and private practice. Valid driver’s license: ability to pass a pre-employment drug screening test and meet safe driving requirements. Driving a personal auto or company car or truck, or a powered piece of material handling equipment. Valid driver’s license and ability to meet safe driving requirements. Ability to manage a complex sell, learn procedural, technical, clinical, and anatomical information quickly and communicate/present/train to a variety of audiences. Ability to lift/pull 25-100lb. training models and meet necessary hospital credentialing/vaccination requirements. Ability to travel adequately to cover territory, as well as overnight attendance at scheduled training events and sales meetings. An essential requirement of your position is to satisfy all applicable health care industry representative (HCIR) credentialing requirements to gain and maintain entry into facilities and organizations that are in your assigned territory. You must also be in good standing and/or eligible to obtain these credentials. These HCIR credentialing requirements may include, but are not limited to, background checks, drug screens, proof of immunization/vaccination for various diseases, fingerprinting and specific licenses required by individual state or cities. Please remember that you are solely responsible for ensuring that you satisfy all HCIR credentialing requirements and for any associated liability for failing to do so. AbbVie has resources available to you to help answer questions you may have.

This is a remote position with up to 50% domestic travel required. Candidates may reside in any state within the United States and should expect frequent national travel. The AbbVie Employer NAE is responsible for supporting and implementing strategic business initiatives in response to the changing healthcare environment, deployed specifically to national Employer Stakeholders via the AbbVie Employer Team with a focus on improving workforce health and productivity and maximizing strategic access to AbbVie’s therapies. The Employer NAE will be accountable for building effective stakeholder strategies and engagements that are on the forefront of emerging concerns impacting employee access, affordability, disease state awareness/management and medication value and access. This includes healthcare decision-makers (HCDMs) within national employer plan sponsors, employee benefit consultants (EBCs), and employer coalitions, as well as emerging stakeholders/influencers/vendors, national organizations, and professional/advocacy organizations. The Employer NAE provides branded and unbranded messaging to employers and employer influencers/KOLs regarding the value and differentiation of AbbVie therapies to accelerate access to treatment and the use of benefit plan designs to identify and minimize barriers to affordable and predictable Rx access. The NAE also delivers messaging relating to disease state and burden of illness to increase the awareness of treatment solutions and explore solutions and develop best practices/case studies. The Employer NAE will provide leadership to distinguish AbbVie in the employer channel, be a convener of stakeholders and regional/national KOLs and SMEs, and provide strategic insights internally in support of evolving business needs to ensure timely awareness of market changes and trends and inform internal business leads to ensure a rapid response to external disruptors and Rx management strategies which impact affordable access to AbbVie’s therapies. This role is highly collaborative and consultative and requires partnering and interfacing with numerous cross-functional teams (Market Access leadership, Payer Strategy and Cross Portfolio Strategy and Pipeline, Training, Market Analytics Business Insights, Business Evolution Strategy Development (BESD), Brand Sales/Marketing, Government Affairs and Policy, Corporate Strategy, US Medical Affairs/Value & Access and Medical Outcomes Science & Science Liaisons (MOSLs); Finance, Legal, Compliance, Communications/PR, Field Reimbursement Leadership, Brand Sales/Marketing teams and internal Centers of Excellence (CoE). The NAE must demonstrate the ability to anticipate and act proactively and effectively in uncertain situations. Additionally, the NAE requires significant collaboration with the Corporate Accounts KAM teams, providing timely insights regarding evolving contracting trends and evolving rebate models, educating client-facing teams, and providing updates regarding downstream employer clients and formulary initiatives. This position does not have direct reports but does require the ability to manage and lead without authority across cross-functional teams while also being able to work independently and productively. The Employer NAE is the lead for regional employer initiatives working in conjunction with the Regional Account Executive (RAE) teams and Regional Directors, as well as compliant collaboration with the Population Heath Account Executive (PHAE) team. This includes identifying opportunities and/or employer access issues and training/educating and executing on use of Employer Team resources and messaging to health plan, health system, PBM and employer customers. This role also is a key collaborator with other national field-based teams including the Field Reimbursement team, educating team members on market disruptors and problem-solving on employer-focused access issues. The Employer NAE serves as a key role in cataloguing key disruptors and potential patient disruption and analyzing potential financial (Gross to Net) impact, as well as working across internal stakeholders to develop and execute mitigation strategies. Major Duties and Responsibilities: Proactively engage with existing employer stakeholders and identify/influence emerging employer stakeholders across the US. Identify insights, positions and potential impact of new and emerging employer stakeholders and vendors. Build proactive share of voice with employer customers and influencers on Rx management topics. Support and contribute to internal Strategy Teams regarding emerging strategies and identification of external SMEs. Collaborate with Government Affairs/Policy/Strategy Directors to connect and convene with new and emerging stakeholders and advocates. Work in conjunction with Employer Team Director and Marketing Director (and collaboratively with Principal National MOSL, Employer Channel) relative to employer channel resource development and messaging. Develop and deliver stakeholder appropriate resources to support access for the expanding AbbVie portfolio (DSA decks, case studies, condensed employer value-prop decks, case studies and benefit plan design resources) Cultivate national employer KOLs and advocates to help shape external education and policy in collaboration with Government Affairs/Policy/Strategy teams. Monitor, inform and deliver market insights to internal business partners. Lead education initiatives in conjunction with Market Access Training on key trends impacting purchasers and AbbVie access/gross-to-net. Establish AbbVie as credible source for non-branded information and disseminate via industry meetings and electronic sites / social media (consistent with AbbVie Communications/PR guidelines). Support efforts to integrate Employer Strategy into AbbVie Business Planning process. Assist AbbVie Employer Corporate Account Team Leader with managing budget and execution of sponsorships and memberships, consistent with AbbVie Office of Ethics and Compliance (OEC) guidelines. Establish AbbVie as a national leader and key partner in the employer channel. Work with Big 3 PBM/GPO KAM teams and respective rebate analysts to ensure contract compliance. Quantify volume/sales associated with employer child accounts and access changes. Participate in internal task forces relating to member/patient access. Bachelor’s degree in Business, Life Sciences, or a related field required. Minimum of 5 years of Account Executive or Market Access experience within the healthcare industry; employee benefits consulting (EBC) experience and/or PBM experience is a plus. Proven ability to operate effectively in large, complex geographies, influence diverse stakeholders, and deliver commercial results. Demonstrated capability in negotiation, stakeholder engagement, and strategic planning/development and execution. Strong analytical skills, especially related to Rx contract terms/language and the commercial payor market. Effective communication and presentation skills (written and oral) with both technical and non-technical audiences. Experience managing complexity and collaborating with cross-functional, matrixed teams; agility and team-orientation required. Customer-centric approach and proven ability to act as primary point of contact for internal and external stakeholders. Ability to work autonomously, manage ambiguity, and identify/influence key customers. Understanding of the evolving healthcare environment—including ACA, CAA, ERISA, clinical guidelines, and formulary/utilization management. Adept at delivering product and disease state value proposition materials to a range of customers. Highest ethical standards and compliance with AbbVie Office of Ethics and Compliance (OEC) policies. Significant domestic travel required (up to 50%) for customer interactions, industry meetings and internal meetings. An essential requirement of your position is to satisfy all applicable health care industry representative (HCIR) credentialing requirements to gain and maintain entry into facilities and organizations that are in your assigned territory. You must also be in good standing and/or eligible to obtain these credentials. Driving a personal auto or company car or truck, or a powered piece of material handling equipment. Valid driver’s license: Ability to pass a pre-employment drug screening test and meet safe driving requirements. Preferred: 10+ years’ experience in pharmaceutical, Rx supply chain, employee benefit consulting, or healthcare organization. Deep understanding of commercial business models and payor markets.

SUMMARY: To provide supervision, guidance and support to all team leaders and operators and insure that all teams are operating efficiently and meeting production targets. The Muliplatform Producer works closely with correspondents to gather all editorial elements needed for stories, including social media newsgathering, research, securing interviews, and confirming information with government agencies and community organizations. The Producer must be able to manage multiple assignments simultaneously, adapt quickly to breaking news, and collaborate closely with editorial leadership and production teams. The ideal candidate has experience working in a multiplatform newsroom and demonstrates strong knowledge of social media and digital storytelling. This role requires strong editorial judgment, the ability to work under tight deadlines, and a solid understanding of national and international news, including breaking news coverage. Responsibilities include requesting graphics and other visual elements that support storytelling and enhance the presentation of stories across platforms. The Multimedia Producer may also assist in writing scripts and editorial content for newscasts and digital coverage. This position requires a strong visual sense and the ability to identify compelling video, natural sound, and other elements that strengthen the narrative and overall impact of a story. In addition, the Multiplatform Producer is responsible for booking guests on a daily basis for linear, streaming, and digital platforms. The candidate must be able to work effectively in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment, including weekends, early mornings, and flexible hours to accommodate last-minute. The position requires the ability to work flexible hours, including nights, weekends, and holidays, particularly during breaking news coverage or special assignments. This position demands the ability to work effectively under tight deadlines within a fast-paced and evolving newsroom environment. Responsibilities: • Gather editorial elements needed for stories, including social media newsgathering, research, and securing interviews. • Contribute to the day’s editorial direction by pitching story ideas, exclusive reports, and interview opportunities. • Participate in breaking news coverage and special projects. • Demonstrate proficiency in using social media platforms for newsgathering, research, and content creation. • Maintain a well-established network of contacts, including community organizations, business leaders, federal and local officials, and other media outlets. • Work effectively in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment, including weekends, early mornings, and flexible hours to accommodate last-minute scheduling changes. • Operate under the guidance of the VP of News Gathering • This position is based on-site in Miami, Florida, and requires regular in-office presence to support newsroom operations. • Contribute to a collaborative, inclusive, and accountable newsroom culture. Basic Requirements: Bachelor’s degree in journalism, Communications, or equivalent professional experience. Minimum of 3 years of on-air news reporting experience in Spanish. Experience producing digital video content in a newsroom environment is a plus. Proficiency in social media platforms and trends. Fluent in Spanish, written and spoken. Fluent in English Desired Characteristics: Accustomed to working in a team and collaborating with all levels within the organization. Proven excellent interpersonal skills combined with a strong sense of how to visually tell a compelling story. Outside of the box thinker Proficient in I-News, helpful Additional Requirements: Interested candidate must submit a resume/CV through www.nbcunicareers.com to be considered (job #: ) Must be willing to work in the greater Miami, Florida area. Must be 18 years or older. Must have a valid driver’s license. Must have unrestricted work authorization to work in the United States Must be covered by Solutions, NBCU’s Alternative Dispute Resolution Program

Specializes in working in facilities that manufacture a finished product for sale, or sale to another organization for use in an end product. Performs microbial control cleaning procedures that must comply with current Good Manufacturing Practices (cGMP) and regulatory guidelines which include documentation of work procedures frequently audited by the FDA and other regulatory agencies. The work will be accomplished under the general supervision of Lead Personnel and an area Supervisor. Responsibilities Performs cross contamination cleaning methods in areas that require microbial control. Completes cGMP documentation of training or cleaning performed on paper and electronic devices. Prepares cleaning solutions based on cGMP regulated mixing instructions. Performs microbial control cleaning techniques on walls, ceiling and floors based on cGMP regulated cleaning frequencies. Completes preventive maintenance work orders to meet cGMP cleaning requirements. Follows specific gowning procedures and performs cGMP entrance and exit procedures for controlled environments. Operates bailing and compacting equipment. Operates various types of hand held battery and electric cleaning equipment. Operates various types of battery and electric walk behind or ride-on floor cleaning equipment. Performs safety and preventive maintenance inspections on housekeeping power equipment and small tools and wears approved PPE. High School Diploma or equivalent. Must be able to read and comprehend written information to include Corporate Quality Documents, Divisional Operating Procedures, Departmental Operating Procedures and Safety Guidelines. Must be able to comply with cGMP, regulatory guidelines and able to write legibility in English and complete accurate and legible written records in compliance with cGMP when documenting work performed, on paper documents and electronic devices auditable by regulatory agencies. Must be able to operate a computer to complete required compliance & technical training. Must have the ability to learn and perform cleaning techniques to meet regulatory requirements. Must have the ability to work alone or as a team member sharing responsibility and work tasks. Must be able to perform all cleaning specialist job functions. Basic physical requirements are but are not limited to: stand for 7 hours per shift, regularly lift 35 pounds 50 times per shift, occasionally lift 50 pounds 6 times per shift, walk approximately 2000 feet per hour, climb 6 flights of stairs per shift, work on knees 30 minutes per shift, bend / Squat 200 times per shift, rotate left / right 200 times per shift.

The Real-Time Graphics Specialist is responsible for the design, development, deployment, and optimization of high-quality real-time broadcast graphics for live studio and event productions. This role blends advanced creative execution with strong technical expertise to support dynamic, on-air visual storytelling. The Specialist manages the graphics production lifecycle — from concept through live delivery — while collaborating closely with producers, directors, and technical teams. We have an opening for a Field Technician to provide technical support and customer services in the management of hazardous and radioactive waste. Under general supervision you will perform a variety of technical functions in collecting, packaging, labeling, identifying, documenting, segregating, consolidating, treating, and storing hazardous, explosive and radioactive waste generated by various LLNL programs. This position is in the Radioactive and Hazardous Waste Management (RHWM) Program and part of the Special Project Group supporting Site 200 within the Strategic Deterrence Directorate. This position requires full-time on-site presence due to the nature of the work. This position will be filled at either level based on knowledge and related experience as assessed by the hiring team. Additional job responsibilities (outlined below) will be assigned if hired at the higher level. In this role you will Perform a wide variety of waste management activities, often wearing personal protective equipment (PPE) such as anti-C’s, respirator, hearing protection, etc., to collect, package, label, identify, segregate, consolidate, treat, store, and verify hazardous, low level radioactive, mixed and/or transuranic waste. Operate wastewater retention tanks and/or systems, perform pump-outs, perform lab packing of waste chemicals and manage waste container storage areas. Perform field testing (pH, visual etc.) and sampling of waste to verify characterization and/or treatment results and operate radiation survey instruments to obtain radiological data. Operate a variety of vehicles up to and including 5-ton trucks, use material handling equipment (fork trucks, drum handling equipment, mechanical pump systems, etc.), and use hand and power tools. We have an opening for a Document Compliance Coordinator to navigate a complex matrix of federal, institutional and organizational requirements. You will collaborate with engineers and subject matter experts to initiate, develop, document and evaluate comprehensive technical procedures, documents and safety plans. This position will support the Superblock (SBK) facility within the Strategic Deterrence Directorate. This position may offer a hybrid schedule, which includes the flexibility to work from home one or more days per week, after a probationary period. The specifics of the hybrid schedule, including the exact number of days required in the office and virtual work options, may vary based on the needs of the team and the organization. In this role you will Analyze and implement documentation processes, procedures, and practices to ensure activities within the facility are performed in compliance with requirements in federal regulations, institutional procedures, and the nuclear facility safety bases. Evaluate procedures and process documents to verify facility requirements are adequately implemented, controls identified in the safety basis documents are maintained, and technical and management reviews are conducted. Manage technical information communications and interface with the LLNL programs and facilities personnel related to facility procedures; solicit feedback and facilitate comment resolution. Perform other duties as assigned. Additional job responsibilities, at the A23.3 level Develop, plan, review, assess, analyze, and implement administrative processes, procedures, and practices by applying in depth knowledge to ensure SBK activities comply with governing requirements, including federal regulations, LLNL procedures, and nuclear facility safety basis documents. Provide professional support to program/practice/policy development and implementation efforts; assists with program research and ongoing monitoring of results. Serves as a subject matter expert and trusted resource, providing informed recommendations to management on policy updates and changes. Ability to secure and maintain a U.S. DOE Q level security clearance which requires U.S. citizenship. Associate Degree in a related field or equivalent combination of education and related experience in a business, operational and/or organizational area. Experience interpreting, reviewing and analyzing administrative processes, policies, procedures and practices to determine if the activities they address are performed in compliance with complex regulations and requirements. Effective technical composition, writing and editing skills and experience effectively composing professional documentation with the ability to obtain a Procedure Professionals Association (PPA) Certification. Experience tracking, compiling and monitoring data necessary to coordinate corrective actions. Proficient verbal and written communication skills necessary to manage scientific and technical communications across multidisciplinary teams, with effective collaboration and communication skills necessary to effectively explain and present proposed changes to documents and processes. Effective organizational and interpersonal skills necessary to resolve problems and sensitive/confidential issues with tact, discretion, and mature judgment. Strong proficiency in Microsoft Word and a solid working knowledge of Excel, FileMaker Pro, Adobe Acrobat, and EDMS (such as SharePoint or Windchill) with the ability to learn new software quickly. Additional qualifications at the A23.3 level Experience researching, tracking, compiling and monitoring data necessary to conduct self-assessment activities, effectively present findings, and coordinate corrective actions. Broad and specialized knowledge of and experience in related work activities and multi-faceted internal processes. Experience training and mentoring personnel on document control within a regulated environment, ensuring compliance with applicable requirements. We are looking for a Counterintelligence Officer in the Counterintelligence Program to perform comprehensive research and analysis, conduct interviews, and present recommendations to senior management, high-level DOE personnel, and officials of intelligence agencies on relevant counterintelligence (CI) issues, ensuring the Laboratory’s compliance with Department of Energy (DOE) Order 475.1 (CI Program). Bachelor’s Degree in a related field or equivalent combination of education and related experience. Knowledge and experience working on national security issues related to the USIC. Broad knowledge of, and significant experience with, classified and unclassified databases, software applications, and other intelligence research tools to identify and assess foreign capabilities using the conventional intelligence disciplines. description_text: Job Title: Manufacturing Operator Job Description: THE ROLE: Our site in Chaska, MN is seeking a Manufacturing Operator to join our team. As a Manufacturing Operator in the Valves and Manifolds department you are an essential part in helping Entegris be part of the future of Innovation. The Valves and Manifolds cleanroom assembles a range of different valves and other components that are used by our customers to ensure they can precisely measure and dispense a variety of chemicals. In this role you will execute tasks such as setting up assembly workstations, assembling valve components and bodies, and conducting tests by following Standard Operating Procedures and high-quality standards. HOURS FOR THIS POSITION ARE 6AM-4PM MONDAY-THURSDAY WHAT YOU’LL DO: Sets up workstations with components required for valve/fitting assembly by referencing part instructions. Assembles different types of valves and fittings according to engineering drawings and assembly instructions. Utilizes different hand tools, assembly fixtures, and other equipment for precise valve and fitting assembly and alignment of components. Conducts various forms of manual and automatic testing procedures on assembled valves and other components by closely following supplied part instructions Assesses test results and logs into Camline software for record-keeping and compliance. Sets up and operates engraving laser on finished parts after the assembly process. Packages finished products in adherence to established requirements. Uses SAP and other electronic systems to find, record and generate documentation throughout the assembly or soldering process. Records all output and production data in ERP systems and maintains compliance with all online training and documentation requirements. Verifies product visually and takes corrective action when necessary. Ensures product is consistent with established specifications. Escalates quality issues as appropriate. Ensures the highest possible product quality and adherence to the Entegris quality policy, ISO and/or other standards. Ensures all products are packaged per packaging specifications. Finalizes all required paperwork thoroughly and timely (i.e. Production Reports, , Labels, Component Sheets, Rework Sheets, SAP Transactions etc.). Maintains accurate attribute/variable charts of rejected materials. Conducts variable charts on manufacturing processes and counts products as required. Integrates on all key business processes to influence customer satisfaction, waste elimination, growth, cost effectiveness and product/system quality. Promotes and implements use of continuous improvement tools to eliminate non-value activities. Participates actively in Entegris’ continuous improvement activities such as 6s, Kaizen events, etc. Maintains a clean and safe work area. Communicates potential safety hazards immediately to supervisor. Performs duties in a safe manner and observes approved safety procedures. Completes miscellaneous tasks as assigned in support of the larger organization and production goals. WHAT WE SEEK: Must be 18 years or older and have the right to work in the US without sponsorship At least one (1) year of experience working in a manufacturing and/or clean room assembly setting is preferred. Basic computer and data entry skills. Good attention to detail and commitment to maintaining high-quality standards. Proven ability to execute manufacturing processes within a tight tolerance. Understand documented processes and procedures. Excellent hand-eye coordination to perform assembly tasks precisely. Ability to use measuring devices (e. G. Caliper, measuring tape) and repetitively pinch and grasp hand/power tools. Must be able to stand and walk for 75% of the shift duration. Must be able to lift to 40 pounds. Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) is required to be used at all times while on duty. This includes safety glasses, steel-toed shoes, and high-visibility vests. This role involves repetitively pinching and grasping hand tools, as well repetitively twisting, bending and reaching to handle small screws, washers, fasteners, etc. Adherence to cleanroom attire standards is always required while on duty. This includes the use of specified protective gear and garments designed to maintain a clean and controlled work environment. WHY WORK AT ENTEGRIS? Lead, Inspire, Innovate. Define Your Future Not everyone who works for a global company shares the same background, experiences and perspectives. We leverage the differences of our employees to bring new ideas to the table. Every employee throughout the company is encouraged to share input on projects and initiatives. Our decision-making process is truly a collaborative effort as we realize there are leaders at every level of the organization. We put our values at the core of how we operate as an organization — not just when it’s convenient, but in a lasting and meaningful way. We want the time and energy you spend here to have a positive impact on your life inside and outside of the office. WHAT WE OFFER: Our total rewards package goes above and beyond just a paycheck. Whether you're looking to build your career, improve your health, or protect your wealth, we offer generous benefits to help you achieve your goals. Compensation: $21-$25 hourly range with actual pay dependent on candidate overall skills for the role. Annual Bonus Eligible 3 weeks of vacation to take the time you need to recharge Generous 401(K) plan with an impressive employer match with no delayed vesting Excellent health, dental and vision insurance packages to fit your needs Education assistance to support your learning journey Values-driven culture with colleagues that rally around People, Accountability, Creativity and Excellence The company anticipates the application window closing approximately 5 days from the date the notice was posted. However, factors such as candidate flow and business necessity may require Company to shorten or extend the application window Entegris does not provide immigration-related sponsorship for this role. Do not apply for this role if you need Entegris immigration sponsorship (e.g., H1B, TN, STEM OPT, etc.) now or in the future. At Entegris we are committed to providing equal opportunity for all employees and applicants. Our policy is to recruit, hire, train, and reward employees for their individual abilities, achievements, and experience without regard to race, color, religion, sexual orientation, age, national origin, disability, marital or military status. #LI-DM1

Job Title: Production Controller Job Category: Project and Program Management Time Type: Full time Minimum Clearance Required to Start: TS/SCI Employee Type: Regular Percentage of Travel Required: Up to 10% Type of Travel: Local * * * The Opportunity: Plan and schedule work to be performed by facility technicians, including electricians, HVAC technicians, maintenance mechanics, and grounds maintenance personnel based on facility preventive maintenance plans, priority service orders, and available man-hours for each facility trade. Receive and review work order requests and incorporate scheduling of work with the continuing maintenance requirements. Plan work to coincide with the receipt of required supplies, working closely with the facility managers and the trade discipline foremen in obtaining supplies required to perform individual jobs. Prepare weekly schedules showing total man-hours required for recurring maintenance and service orders. Ensures that trade shops are fully utilized and productive. Maintains a "look ahead" schedule to reflect work to be accomplished in each shop six weeks in the future. Compile, prepare, and generate various reports, records, statistics, listings, charts, graphs, or other Facility Preventive Maintenance (PM) related information, as requested. Conduct market research and prepare purchase requests for leadership approval, to procure supplies for the accomplishment of preventive maintenance and customer service orders. Work with shop foremen to identify material requirements. Plan procurements to ensure materials arrive in time for completion of the service orders. Accept customer service calls and create service orders. Participate in the review of incoming work requests to determine, based on established work request priority methodology, which jobs can be accomplished most effectively by the shops. Interact with customer and advise on status of work requests. Qualifications: Required: High School Diploma or equivalent and 7 years of experience; or 5+ years of experience with equivalent military production control or operations management training. Experience with and robust knowledge of policies, practices, and procedures for operating, sustaining, maintaining, constructing, and repairing government real property. Experience with and knowledge of supply and procurement procedures. -Strong customer service and communication and coordination skills. Experience with and skills developing work plans and scheduling facility work. Proficient in Microsoft Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, etc.). US Citizenship, Top Secret (TS) security clearance with Single Scope Background Investigation (SSBI) with eligibility for Sensitive Compartmented Information (SCI) indoctrination. - What You Can Expect: A culture of integrity. At CACI, we place character and innovation at the center of everything we do. As a valued team member, you’ll be part of a high-performing group dedicated to our customer’s missions and driven by a higher purpose – to ensure the safety of our nation. An environment of trust. CACI values the unique contributions that every employee brings to our company and our customers - every day. You’ll have the autonomy to take the time you need through a unique flexible time off benefit and have access to robust learning resources to make your ambitions a reality. A focus on continuous growth. Together, we will advance our nation's most critical missions, build on our lengthy track record of business success, and find opportunities to break new ground — in your career and in our legacy. Pay Range : There are a host of factors that can influence final salary including, but not limited to, geographic location, Federal Government contract labor categories and contract wage rates, relevant prior work experience, specific skills and competencies, education, and certifications. Our employees value the flexibility at CACI that allows them to balance quality work and their personal lives. We offer competitive compensation, benefits and learning and development opportunities. Our broad and competitive mix of benefits options is designed to support and protect employees and their families. At CACI, you will receive comprehensive benefits such as; healthcare, wellness, financial, retirement, family support, continuing education, and time off benefits. The proposed salary range for this position is: $78,700 - $165,200 CACI is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, pregnancy, sexual orientation, age, national origin, disability, status as a protected veteran, or any other protected characteristic.

This role requires a strong grasp of healthcare policy, payer analytics, and strategy formulation within a collaborative, cross-functional environment. Key Responsibilities: Lead the planning and execution of analytics to inform market access strategies, price reform and policy analysis, with actionable recommendations for AbbVie leadership. Identify payer opportunities/threats through deep dive analytics ('Follow the Dollar', claims analysis, and scenario modeling). Foster positive relationships and close collaboration with teams including Government Affairs, Finance, Legal, Corporate Affairs, Brand, and Market Access. AI.Accelerate Overview: Are you a technically curious and ambitious undergraduate student with a passion for Artificial Intelligence? ServiceNow invites you to explore our AI.Accelerate program where you can develop practical AI skills and gain hands-on experience in a dynamic, fast-paced, and immersive environment. This eight-week unpaid bootcamp is designed to provide a comprehensive introduction to the core concepts and techniques of AI, with a focus on practical application and real-world problem-solving. You'll learn from experienced instructors, work on challenging projects, and collaborate with a cohort of talented peers. Dates: June 15 – July 31, 2026 (Virtual) + Week 8—beginning of August (In Person) Location: Virtually via Zoom Duration: 4 hours a week (plus homework) What You'll Learn: Agentic AI Foundations: Understand what makes an AI system "agentic" — including autonomy, reasoning, and action-taking — and how LLMs are evolving from chat tools into decision-making agents. Agentic Design Patterns: Explore key architectural patterns including React, chain-of-thought, tool use, and memory, and understand the difference between single-agent and multi-agent systems and when to use each. Prompt Engineering: Learn techniques for writing reliable, production-grade prompts that drive consistent and predictable agent behavior at scale. Building Agents: Design agents that use tools, APIs, and external data sources, and learn how to structure agent memory — both short-term and long-term — for complex, multi-step tasks. Multi-Agent Orchestration: Build and manage multi-agent workflows where agents collaborate, delegate, and hand off tasks to accomplish goals that no single agent could complete alone. Evaluation Frameworks: Learn why evaluations are the most critical part of building AI systems and how to design frameworks that define what to measure and how to measure it effectively. AI Safety & Responsible Use: Understand real-world failure modes including hallucination, prompt injection, and behavioral drift, and learn how to build guardrails and safety checks into agentic pipelines. Capstone Project: Design, build, evaluate, and defend an AI agent from scratch — putting every concept from the program into practice and presenting your work to a panel of ServiceNow engineers and leaders. Innovative Learning Structure: A blend of lectures, hands-on laboratories, and collaborative projects fostering a cohort- based, hands on learning experience. The program concludes with an in-person experience where participants showcase their capstone project, explore career opportunities at ServiceNow, and connect with the broader engineering community. please note: this is an unpaid program and is not an internship To be successful in this role you: Have experience in leveraging or critically thinking about how to integrate AI into work processes, decision-making, or problem-solving. This may include using AI-powered tools, automating workflows, analyzing AI-driven insights, or exploring AI’s potential impact on the function or industry . Are an Undergraduate student majoring or minoring in Computer Science (CS), Computer Engineering (CE), or Data Analytics. or related field, with a graduation date no earlier than December 2027 Are experienced in Python programming. Are experienced with and/or have knowledge of fundamental AI concepts Have availability to attend the full duration of the boot camp from June 15, 2026 to July 31, 2026 and then available to participate onsite in the beginning of August Application Process: Interested candidates should apply by April 15, 2026 , to be considered. Applications are evaluated until the application deadline only; therefore, early submission is recommended as spots are limited! Please submit a resume, a cover letter, and any related project work or AI experience. In your cover letter please share: Why do you want to participate in this AI bootcamp? Where do you see AI helping you in the future?

This is a remote position with up to 50% domestic travel required. Candidates may reside in the Southwest or Western part of the United States and should expect frequent national travel. The AbbVie Employer NAE is responsible for supporting and implementing strategic business initiatives in response to the changing healthcare environment, deployed specifically to national Employer Stakeholders via the AbbVie Employer Team with a focus on improving workforce health and productivity and maximizing strategic access to AbbVie’s therapies. The Employer NAE will be accountable for building effective stakeholder strategies and engagements that are on the forefront of emerging concerns impacting employee access, affordability, disease state awareness/management and medication value and access. This includes healthcare decision-makers (HCDMs) within national employer plan sponsors, employee benefit consultants (EBCs), and employer coalitions, as well as emerging stakeholders/influencers/vendors, national organizations, and professional/advocacy organizations. The Employer NAE provides branded and unbranded messaging to employers and employer influencers/KOLs regarding the value and differentiation of AbbVie therapies to accelerate access to treatment and the use of benefit plan designs to identify and minimize barriers to affordable and predictable Rx access. The NAE also delivers messaging relating to disease state and burden of illness to increase the awareness of treatment solutions and explore solutions and develop best practices/case studies. The Employer NAE will provide leadership to distinguish AbbVie in the employer channel, be a convener of stakeholders and regional/national KOLs and SMEs, and provide strategic insights internally in support of evolving business needs to ensure timely awareness of market changes and trends and inform internal business leads to ensure a rapid response to external disruptors and Rx management strategies which impact affordable access to AbbVie’s therapies. This role is highly collaborative and consultative and requires partnering and interfacing with numerous cross-functional teams (Market Access leadership, Payer Strategy and Cross Portfolio Strategy and Pipeline, Training, Market Analytics Business Insights, Business Evolution Strategy Development (BESD), Brand Sales/Marketing, Government Affairs and Policy, Corporate Strategy, US Medical Affairs/Value & Access and Medical Outcomes Science & Science Liaisons (MOSLs); Finance, Legal, Compliance, Communications/PR, Field Reimbursement Leadership, Brand Sales/Marketing teams and internal Centers of Excellence (CoE). The NAE must demonstrate the ability to anticipate and act proactively and effectively in uncertain situations. Additionally, the NAE requires significant collaboration with the Corporate Accounts KAM teams, providing timely insights regarding evolving contracting trends and evolving rebate models, educating client-facing teams, and providing updates regarding downstream employer clients and formulary initiatives. This position does not have direct reports but does require the ability to manage and lead without authority across cross-functional teams while also being able to work independently and productively. The Employer NAE is the lead for regional employer initiatives working in conjunction with the Regional Account Executive (RAE) teams and Regional Directors, as well as compliant collaboration with the Population Heath Account Executive (PHAE) team. This includes identifying opportunities and/or employer access issues and training/educating and executing on use of Employer Team resources and messaging to health plan, health system, PBM and employer customers. This role also is a key collaborator with other national field-based teams including the Field Reimbursement team, educating team members on market disruptors and problem-solving on employer-focused access issues. The Employer NAE serves as a key role in cataloguing key disruptors and potential patient disruption and analyzing potential financial (Gross to Net) impact, as well as working across internal stakeholders to develop and execute mitigation strategies. Major Duties and Responsibilities: Proactively engage with existing employer stakeholders and identify/influence emerging employer stakeholders across the US. Identify insights, positions and potential impact of new and emerging employer stakeholders and vendors. Build proactive share of voice with employer customers and influencers on Rx management topics. Support and contribute to internal Strategy Teams regarding emerging strategies and identification of external SMEs. Collaborate with Government Affairs/Policy/Strategy Directors to connect and convene with new and emerging stakeholders and advocates. Work in conjunction with Employer Team Director and Marketing Director (and collaboratively with Principal National MOSL, Employer Channel) relative to employer channel resource development and messaging. Develop and deliver stakeholder appropriate resources to support access for the expanding AbbVie portfolio (DSA decks, case studies, condensed employer value-prop decks, case studies and benefit plan design resources) Cultivate national employer KOLs and advocates to help shape external education and policy in collaboration with Government Affairs/Policy/Strategy teams. Monitor, inform and deliver market insights to internal business partners. Lead education initiatives in conjunction with Market Access Training on key trends impacting purchasers and AbbVie access/gross-to-net. Establish AbbVie as credible source for non-branded information and disseminate via industry meetings and electronic sites / social media (consistent with AbbVie Communications/PR guidelines). Support efforts to integrate Employer Strategy into AbbVie Business Planning process. Assist AbbVie Employer Corporate Account Team Leader with managing budget and execution of sponsorships and memberships, consistent with AbbVie Office of Ethics and Compliance (OEC) guidelines. Establish AbbVie as a national leader and key partner in the employer channel. Work with Big 3 PBM/GPO KAM teams and respective rebate analysts to ensure contract compliance. Quantify volume/sales associated with employer child accounts and access changes. Participate in internal task forces relating to member/patient access. Bachelor’s degree in Business, Life Sciences, or a related field required. Minimum of 5 years of Account Executive or Market Access experience within the healthcare industry; employee benefits consulting (EBC) experience and/or PBM experience is a plus. Proven ability to operate effectively in large, complex geographies, influence diverse stakeholders, and deliver commercial results. Demonstrated capability in negotiation, stakeholder engagement, and strategic planning/development and execution. Strong analytical skills, especially related to Rx contract terms/language and the commercial payor market. Effective communication and presentation skills (written and oral) with both technical and non-technical audiences. Experience managing complexity and collaborating with cross-functional, matrixed teams; agility and team-orientation required. Customer-centric approach and proven ability to act as primary point of contact for internal and external stakeholders. Ability to work autonomously, manage ambiguity, and identify/influence key customers. Understanding of the evolving healthcare environment—including ACA, CAA, ERISA, clinical guidelines, and formulary/utilization management. Adept at delivering product and disease state value proposition materials to a range of customers. Highest ethical standards and compliance with AbbVie Office of Ethics and Compliance (OEC) policies. Significant domestic travel required (up to 50%) for customer interactions, industry meetings and internal meetings. An essential requirement of your position is to satisfy all applicable health care industry representative (HCIR) credentialing requirements to gain and maintain entry into facilities and organizations that are in your assigned territory. You must also be in good standing and/or eligible to obtain these credentials. Driving a personal auto or company car or truck, or a powered piece of material handling equipment. Valid driver’s license: Ability to pass a pre-employment drug screening test and meet safe driving requirements. Preferred: 10+ years’ experience in pharmaceutical, Rx supply chain, employee benefit consulting, or healthcare organization. Deep understanding of commercial business models and payor markets.

Supports roadmap execution for Workfront cleanup, rationalization, and cross system consistency. Ensures documentation is current and standardized for Workfront and/or other project related systems. Experience with Microsoft Dynamics 365, PowerBI, or similar platforms. Strong understanding of project management methodologies, business process alignment, and cross‑functional operations. Experience supporting or administering integrated systems in a matrixed environment.

The AbbVie Process Chemistry Chromatographic Separations Lab is actively seeking an Associate Scientist II or Scientist I. Our team collaborates with colleagues across multiple disciplines, offering expertise in preparative chromatography to support a broad range of AbbVie R&D programs. We maintain and utilize specialized equipment for various separation tasks, including the purification of peptides, ADC drug-linkers, and chiral compounds, as well as the isolation of low-level API impurities. Additionally, the team is responsible for pilot-scale preparative purification, developing scalable purification processes, and overseeing their implementation under cGMP guidelines at AbbVie's North Chicago Chemical Pilot Plant. This role will contribute to the development of novel/advanced separations technologies and broader efforts to develop new process technologies for advancing the AbbVie pipeline. We are seeking a motivated scientist who demonstrates initiative and technical proficiency in supporting research and development projects within a collaborative team environment. The ideal candidate will have hands-on experience developing chromatographic methods and troubleshooting complex separation challenges. Experience working with peptides is highly desirable, but not required for application. Key Responsibilities: Develop and execute purification processes supporting development of small molecule, antibody drug conjugate, and peptide clinical candidates. Demonstrate scientific initiative and creativity in planning, executing, and troubleshooting experiments, resolving key project challenges with an appropriate level of autonomy based on experience. Conduct a range of laboratory and pilot-scale tasks, analyze and interpret data, and drive project objectives, assuming responsibility for tasks in accordance with experience. Suggest, adapt, and, as appropriate, implement new or improved experimental protocols/techniques, consulting relevant literature as needed. Build and maintain strong collaborative relationships with peers and cross-functional partners. Foster a learning environment, encourage diverse ideas, and support continuous process improvement. Understand and adhere strictly to corporate standards for conduct, safety, quality, and proper handling of materials. Bachelor’s degree with at least 3 years (Associate Scientist II) or 5 years (Scientist I) relevant experience; or Master’s degree with no additional experience (Associate Scientist II) or typically +2 years of relevant experience (Scientist I). Strong technical background in Separations Science, with theoretical and practical knowledge required to independently carry out job functions. Demonstrated proficiency in developing, troubleshooting, and modifying chromatographic methods and purification protocols. Broad expertise in analytical techniques, with emphasis on chromatography, compound purification, and spectral analysis. Ability to search scientific literature and evaluate potential solutions to research problems. Effective written and oral communication skills; able to work collaboratively in multidisciplinary teams.

The Center for Global Security Research (CGSR) was established at Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL) in 1996 to bring together experts from the science, technology, and policy communities to address pressing national security challenges. For over 20 years, CGSR has engaged diverse perspectives on topics important to national security, deterrence, diplomacy, dual-use technology, arms control, nonproliferation, space, cyber, biosecurity, and energy security. We have openings in Fall 2026 for undergraduate students to engage in practical research on global security topics. Students will work with CGSR over the duration of three to four months as a research associate (RA). RAs will engage in practical research to further their educational and career goals, while also supporting the development of strategies for national security and LLNL’s mission focus areas. Examples of relevant fields of research include nuclear deterrence, arms control, nonproliferation, emerging technologies, cybersecurity, space, biological & chemical security, and energy security. CGSR’s objectives are as follows: To explore the dynamics of potential 21st century strategic conflicts (i.e., those with a potential nuclear aspect) and to formulate ideas about how to achieve U.S. deterrence and other objectives in such conflicts. To explore the sources and characteristics of strategic competition in the emerging security environment and to formulate organizing concepts to enhance the competitive position of the United States and its allies and partners over the long term. To identify whether and how technically based approaches can address new challenges to national and international security. To catalyze broader national and international thinking about the requirements of effective deterrence, assurance, and strategic stability in a changed and changing security environment. To assist in the development of new generations of experts motivated by a clear view of the changed and changing security environment. More information on CGSR, its research focus areas, and its publications can be found at https://cgsr.llnl.gov/ . This job will be closed to applicants on May 31, 2026. You will Conduct an independent research project on an agreed upon topic aligned with CGSR/LLNL research priorities under the supervision of CGSR staff. Support CGSR/LLNL through contributions to ongoing research activities. Tasks may include contributing to literature reviews, annotated bibliographies, and workshop summary reports. Attend relevant research seminars, speakers’ series, and workshops. Present research to LLNL staff at end of the assignment. Prepare end-of-assignment technical report or publication. Perform all assignments in accordance with ES&H, security, and business practice requirements and policies. Perform other duties as assigned. Must be eligible to access the Laboratory in compliance with Section 3112 of the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA). See Additional Information section below for details. Must be currently enrolled in an accredited university or have completed AA/AS degree in a field of research aligned with CGSR analytic priorities. Areas of study include international relations and/or security, political science, economics, public policy, emerging technologies, nonproliferation, energy, biosecurity, foreign language studies, or related fields. Demonstrated academic and/or professional achievement in a relevant field of research aligned with CGSR analytic priorities. Strong record of independent research and publication, or a strong proposal of research to be done while at CGSR and in future academic and professional settings. Ability to work in a team environment. Pay Range $23.26 - $31.62 Hourly This position is under a step structure. Please note that the step is determined by your academic level. Transcripts are required.
