Associate Degree in a related field or equivalent combination of education and related experience in a business, operational and/or organizational area. Experience interpreting, reviewing and analyzing administrative processes, policies, procedures and practices to determine if the activities they address are performed in compliance with complex regulations and requirements. Effective technical composition, writing and editing skills and experience effectively composing professional documentation with the ability to obtain a Procedure Professionals Association (PPA) Certification. Experience tracking, compiling and monitoring data necessary to coordinate corrective actions. Proficient verbal and written communication skills necessary to manage scientific and technical communications across multidisciplinary teams, with effective collaboration and communication skills necessary to effectively explain and present proposed changes to documents and processes. Effective organizational and interpersonal skills necessary to resolve problems and sensitive/confidential issues with tact, discretion, and mature judgment. Strong proficiency in Microsoft Word and a solid working knowledge of Excel, FileMaker Pro, Adobe Acrobat, and EDMS (such as SharePoint or Windchill) with the ability to learn new software quickly. Additional qualifications at the A23.3 level Experience researching, tracking, compiling and monitoring data necessary to conduct self-assessment activities, effectively present findings, and coordinate corrective actions. Broad and specialized knowledge of and experience in related work activities and multi-faceted internal processes. Experience training and mentoring personnel on document control within a regulated environment, ensuring compliance with applicable requirements. The Role The Tool and Die Coordinator is responsible for day-to-day coordination of tool and die activities in a high-volume automotive sheet metal stamping environment. This role ensures dies, tooling, and related resources are available, safe, and capable to support the production schedule. The Coordinator serves as the primary interface between Die Room, Press Operations, Maintenance, Engineering, and outside vendors to minimize downtime, improve die performance, and support launch and tryout events. What You’ll Do Coordinate daily die room priorities based on production schedule, press downtime, and quality concerns. Plan, sequence, and track die repair, PMs, engineering changes, and tryout work to meet program and production timing. Maintain and communicate die status (in press, in repair, in storage, at vendor, in transit) to production, maintenance, and leadership. Support press set-ups and die change activities , ensuring required dies, tooling, and components are available and verified. Coordinate weekend and off-shift work (e.g., repair, tryout, PM, launch activities) including work lists, coverage, and handoff to oncoming shifts. Partner with Engineering, Quality, and Production to address repeat die issues , dimensional concerns, and scrap/downtime drivers; help prioritize corrective actions. Ensure adherence to WSS PS12 Die Handling and all applicable GM safety standards for die storage, handling, rigging, and press operations. Help maintain accurate die storage maps, identification, and labeling ; support improvements to die flow and storage layout. Work with Materials, Purchasing, and vendors to coordinate off-site tooling work , including shipping, receipts, and timing follow-up. Use available systems (e.g., local trackers, spreadsheets, shop logs, and GM systems) to track work orders, downtime, and die performance metrics . Support launch and tryout events (T-events, blitz runs, recipe development) through die readiness, schedule coordination, and on-floor presence as needed. Participate in GMS / continuous improvement activities focused on safety, quality, throughput, and cost. Provide clear communication and shift handoff regarding die status, open issues, and next-step actions. Your Skills & Abilities (Required Qualifications) ​​ 3+ years experience in an automotive stamping, tool & die, or heavy manufacturing environment. Strong understanding of stamping dies, die repair, PM practices, and die tryout . Demonstrated ability to prioritize work , manage multiple concurrent activities, and meet aggressive timing requirements. Proven track record of safe work practices in a heavy industrial environment (overhead cranes, rigging, presses, weld, machining, etc.). Effective communication skills (written and verbal) with hourly, salary, leadership, and external partners. Journeyperson-level experience in Tool & Die, Die Maker, or closely related skilled trade; or equivalent combination of education and relevant stamping/tooling experience. 3+ years of experience in an automotive stamping, tool & die, or heavy manufacturing environment . TRAINING The Sales Trainee (ST) is a training role. Upon successful participation in the training program, the ST is eligible to interview for open Account Sales Manager (ASM) roles. Build and maintain program and project schedules that include appropriate lead times, realistic durations, major milestones, and deliverables from internal customers and vendors. Perform schedule analytics, including critical path, float, variance, slippage trends, milestone health, and key driver analysis. Develop, run, and maintain metrics and alerts that identify activity slippage and emerging risks, enabling proactive decisions before milestone impacts occur. Conduct “what-if” scenario analysis to evaluate sequencing and duration changes, quantify impacts, and support recovery planning. Ability to secure and maintain a U.S. DOE Q-level security clearance, which requires U.S. citizenship. Bachelor degree in Project Management, Engineering Technology, Computer Science, Information Systems, or an equivalent combination of education and related technical experience. Advanced interpersonal, verbal, and written communication skills necessary to effectively collaborate in a team environment and present and explain technical or operational information to regulators, reviewers, and stakeholders. Advanced experience using Primavera P6 for scheduling and schedule analysis. AbbVie’s Analytics and Performance Excellence (APEX) function is seeking a highly strategic, analytical, and collaborative Associate Director to provide analytics leadership for the Business Evolution Strategic Development (BESD) Team. This role will drive impactful business analytics and insights to help AbbVie anticipate and navigate evolving healthcare environments, especially focusing on market access and policy disruptors. The Associate Director will bridge Market Access and Patient Services (MAPS) Team within APEX and BESD (Business Evolution Strategic Development) team objectives by leading modelling, advanced insights and analytics supporting forward-looking strategies, enabling enterprise readiness, and shaping market access policies and outcomes for AbbVie’s diverse U.S. portfolio. This role requires a strong grasp of healthcare policy, payer analytics, and strategy formulation within a collaborative, cross-functional environment. Key Responsibilities: Lead the planning and execution of analytics to inform market access strategies, price reform and policy analysis, with actionable recommendations for AbbVie leadership. Identify payer opportunities/threats through deep dive analytics ('Follow the Dollar', claims analysis, and scenario modeling). Foster positive relationships and close collaboration with teams including Government Affairs, Finance, Legal, Corporate Affairs, Brand, and Market Access. Communicate complex findings and insight-driven narratives to senior leadership and cross-functional teams, enabling improved payer knowledge and strategic decision-making. Monitor external environment and translate emerging trends (political, regulatory, legislative, commercial) into strategic recommendations for AbbVie’s business evolution. Advise on analytics infrastructure enhancements to drive business impact. Skills Action and Accountability: Own responsibility for activities within relevant workstreams, and engage and inspire cross functional stakeholders to advance towards clear objectives and strategies; make quick, but informed decisions, as appropriate, to ensure best paths forward in the midst of change market and policy dynamics. Constantly engage, guide, and support cross-functional team to address roadblocks, challenges, resourcing constraints and other dynamics. Leadership and Influence: Influence and persuade across multiple external and internal stakeholders. Collaboration and Teamwork: Work effectively with internal stakeholders, external market experts and partners. Bachelor’s degree required; master’s degree (MBA or related business/science) preferred. 10+ years of progressive analytical/ insights experience in healthcare industry (pharma, consulting, government affairs, market access, public policy, etc.). 1-2 years pharmaceutical market access experience with deep understanding of Health Plans, PBMs, Hospitals, Specialty Pharmacies, and healthcare policy stakeholders. Strong insurance channel experience and understanding (i.e. Medicare, Commercial etc.) Strong business acumen, strategic and analytical thinking, and executive presence. Exceptional communication and influencing skills, with the ability to distill complex information into compelling, concise messages. Strong organizational skills, flexibility, attention to detail, and experience in collaborative, dynamic environments. Exceptional communications and executive presence, critical thinking and interpersonal skills, strong ability to influence without authority, the ability to speak and write persuasively and with clarity, strong organizational skills, flexibility, and adaptability to changing requirements, resourcefulness and creativity, strong attention to detail, a proven track record of being able to work drive towards deadlines and an ability to work collaboratively in a fluid organizational and external environment. Must be an individual who works well in a team environment and enjoys working in a collegial, collaborative and fun, yet highly demanding culture Preferred: Experience in policy shaping, price reform strategy, and enterprise-level stakeholder partnership. Proficiency with pharmaceutical data sources (formulary, claims).

AI.Accelerate Overview: Are you a technically curious and ambitious undergraduate student with a passion for Artificial Intelligence? ServiceNow invites you to explore our AI.Accelerate program where you can develop practical AI skills and gain hands-on experience in a dynamic, fast-paced, and immersive environment. This eight-week unpaid bootcamp is designed to provide a comprehensive introduction to the core concepts and techniques of AI, with a focus on practical application and real-world problem-solving. You'll learn from experienced instructors, work on challenging projects, and collaborate with a cohort of talented peers. Dates: June 15 – July 31, 2026 (Virtual) + Week 8—beginning of August (In Person) Location: Virtually via Zoom Duration: 4 hours a week (plus homework) What You'll Learn: Agentic AI Foundations: Understand what makes an AI system "agentic" — including autonomy, reasoning, and action-taking — and how LLMs are evolving from chat tools into decision-making agents. Agentic Design Patterns: Explore key architectural patterns including React, chain-of-thought, tool use, and memory, and understand the difference between single-agent and multi-agent systems and when to use each. Prompt Engineering: Learn techniques for writing reliable, production-grade prompts that drive consistent and predictable agent behavior at scale. Building Agents: Design agents that use tools, APIs, and external data sources, and learn how to structure agent memory — both short-term and long-term — for complex, multi-step tasks. Multi-Agent Orchestration: Build and manage multi-agent workflows where agents collaborate, delegate, and hand off tasks to accomplish goals that no single agent could complete alone. Evaluation Frameworks: Learn why evaluations are the most critical part of building AI systems and how to design frameworks that define what to measure and how to measure it effectively. AI Safety & Responsible Use: Understand real-world failure modes including hallucination, prompt injection, and behavioral drift, and learn how to build guardrails and safety checks into agentic pipelines. Capstone Project: Design, build, evaluate, and defend an AI agent from scratch — putting every concept from the program into practice and presenting your work to a panel of ServiceNow engineers and leaders. Innovative Learning Structure: A blend of lectures, hands-on laboratories, and collaborative projects fostering a cohort- based, hands on learning experience. The program concludes with an in-person experience where participants showcase their capstone project, explore career opportunities at ServiceNow, and connect with the broader engineering community. please note: this is an unpaid program and is not an internship To be successful in this role you: Have experience in leveraging or critically thinking about how to integrate AI into work processes, decision-making, or problem-solving. This may include using AI-powered tools, automating workflows, analyzing AI-driven insights, or exploring AI’s potential impact on the function or industry . Are an Undergraduate student majoring or minoring in Computer Science (CS), Computer Engineering (CE), or Data Analytics. or related field, with a graduation date no earlier than December 2027 Are experienced in Python programming. Are experienced with and/or have knowledge of fundamental AI concepts Have availability to attend the full duration of the boot camp from June 15, 2026 to July 31, 2026 and then available to participate onsite in the beginning of August Application Process: Interested candidates should apply by April 15, 2026 , to be considered. Applications are evaluated until the application deadline only; therefore, early submission is recommended as spots are limited! Please submit a resume, a cover letter, and any related project work or AI experience. In your cover letter please share: Why do you want to participate in this AI bootcamp? Where do you see AI helping you in the future?

Aligns, trains and motivates the site staff and principal investigator under supervision on the goals of the clinical trial program, protocol, and patient treatment principles for the trial ensuring a trusted partnership. Conducts site evaluation, site training, routine, and site closure monitoring activities under supervision, in compliance to the protocol and monitoring plans and accordance with applicable regulations, Good Clinical Practices (GCPs), ICH Guidelines, AbbVie Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), and to quality standards in conducting clinical research, ensuring safety and protection of study subjects. Customize site engagement strategy for assigned study (ies) under supervision. Gather local/site insights and utilize site engagement tools such as the Customer Relationship Management (CRM) tool, to report/track progress and measure impact of that strategy. Fundamental level of competency connecting the study protocol, scientific principles and clinical trial requirements to the day-to-day clinical trial execution activities. Evaluate and ensure effective recruitment and retention techniques/plans based on the patient disease journey. Develop solid knowledge of therapeutic area, asset and clinical landscape / patient journey to enable successful patient recruitment and overall protocol compliance. Responsible for continuous risk-assessment proactively, and in collaboration with Central Monitoring team, monitor activities conducted by clinical sites to detect early overall study performance or patient safety issues. Ability to think critically to resolve site risk signals while having robust understanding of site processes to drive study execution. Ensures preventative and corrective action plans are put into place, as needed, to mitigate risk and promote compliance using a customer centric approach. Identifies, evaluates and recommends new/potential investigators/sites under supervision and support from more experienced CRAs. Ensures quality of data submitted from study sites and assures timely submission of data, including appropriate reporting and follow-up for all safety events by site personnel. Ensures audit and regulatory inspection readiness at assigned clinical site at all times. Manages investigator payments as per executed contract obligations, as applicable. *This is a remote based position. Candidates must reside in the Northeast and be willing to travel for site visits. Clinically related experience, preferably in clinical research monitoring, coordinating or data management. Knowledge on existing and emerging local regulatory and legal requirements, ICH/GCP Guidelines and applicable policies. Able to work collaboratively and cross functionally to develop and sustain working relationships. Ability to use functional expertise with appropriate guidance, leverage critical thinking skills and apply good judgement to address clinical site issues. The Associate Director provides statistical programming support for multiple clinical projects across multiple therapeutic areas, both through individual contribution and through the work of staff. The Associate Director provides training and performance management for staff. The Associate Director demonstrates leadership competencies, builds relationships, and promotes teamwork within the Statistical Programming organization and across functions. The Associate Director is accountable for ensuring statistical programming support is delivered across multiple therapeutic areas. The Associate Director makes key recommendations and decisions related to processes, standards, and resource management. Responsibilities: SAS Programming: Demonstrates a strong understanding of SAS programming concepts and techniques used in the pharmaceutical industry and applies that knowledge to resolve non-routine problems. CRFs and Database Definitions: Provides strategic guidance on CRF and database design and reviews global standards related to these deliverables. Effectively leads meetings and presentations. Training and Mentoring: Provides guidance, training, and mentoring to staff to support development and ensure compliance with training requirements. Staff Management : Assigns responsibilities, defines scope, and reviews progress to ensure projects are delivered on time and with appropriate quality. Allocates resources to maintain the right balance of expertise across projects and collaborates with management to assess staffing needs. Sets high expectations, promotes open communication, and leads staff to meet organizational goals. Provides performance management for 4–10 statistical programmers. Minimum Qualifications: Degree in Statistics, Computer Science, or a related field 10+ years of statistical programming experience (with MS) OR 12+ years of statistical programming experience (with BS) Strong technical competence in SAS programming and macro development. Experience in pharmaceutical clinical trials. Experience with regulatory filings such as NDA, BLA, or other submissions, including ISS and ISE experience. Preferred Qualifications: Experience interacting with regulatory agencies, especially FDA and EMEA. Previous management experience. Other Required Skills: Working knowledge of ICH guidelines and relevant regulatory requirements. Strong oral and written communication skills.

This is a remote position with up to 50% domestic travel required. Candidates may reside in the Southwest or Western part of the United States and should expect frequent national travel. The AbbVie Employer NAE is responsible for supporting and implementing strategic business initiatives in response to the changing healthcare environment, deployed specifically to national Employer Stakeholders via the AbbVie Employer Team with a focus on improving workforce health and productivity and maximizing strategic access to AbbVie’s therapies. The Employer NAE will be accountable for building effective stakeholder strategies and engagements that are on the forefront of emerging concerns impacting employee access, affordability, disease state awareness/management and medication value and access. This includes healthcare decision-makers (HCDMs) within national employer plan sponsors, employee benefit consultants (EBCs), and employer coalitions, as well as emerging stakeholders/influencers/vendors, national organizations, and professional/advocacy organizations. The Employer NAE provides branded and unbranded messaging to employers and employer influencers/KOLs regarding the value and differentiation of AbbVie therapies to accelerate access to treatment and the use of benefit plan designs to identify and minimize barriers to affordable and predictable Rx access. The NAE also delivers messaging relating to disease state and burden of illness to increase the awareness of treatment solutions and explore solutions and develop best practices/case studies. The Employer NAE will provide leadership to distinguish AbbVie in the employer channel, be a convener of stakeholders and regional/national KOLs and SMEs, and provide strategic insights internally in support of evolving business needs to ensure timely awareness of market changes and trends and inform internal business leads to ensure a rapid response to external disruptors and Rx management strategies which impact affordable access to AbbVie’s therapies. This role is highly collaborative and consultative and requires partnering and interfacing with numerous cross-functional teams (Market Access leadership, Payer Strategy and Cross Portfolio Strategy and Pipeline, Training, Market Analytics Business Insights, Business Evolution Strategy Development (BESD), Brand Sales/Marketing, Government Affairs and Policy, Corporate Strategy, US Medical Affairs/Value & Access and Medical Outcomes Science & Science Liaisons (MOSLs); Finance, Legal, Compliance, Communications/PR, Field Reimbursement Leadership, Brand Sales/Marketing teams and internal Centers of Excellence (CoE). The NAE must demonstrate the ability to anticipate and act proactively and effectively in uncertain situations. Additionally, the NAE requires significant collaboration with the Corporate Accounts KAM teams, providing timely insights regarding evolving contracting trends and evolving rebate models, educating client-facing teams, and providing updates regarding downstream employer clients and formulary initiatives. This position does not have direct reports but does require the ability to manage and lead without authority across cross-functional teams while also being able to work independently and productively. The Employer NAE is the lead for regional employer initiatives working in conjunction with the Regional Account Executive (RAE) teams and Regional Directors, as well as compliant collaboration with the Population Heath Account Executive (PHAE) team. This includes identifying opportunities and/or employer access issues and training/educating and executing on use of Employer Team resources and messaging to health plan, health system, PBM and employer customers. This role also is a key collaborator with other national field-based teams including the Field Reimbursement team, educating team members on market disruptors and problem-solving on employer-focused access issues. The Employer NAE serves as a key role in cataloguing key disruptors and potential patient disruption and analyzing potential financial (Gross to Net) impact, as well as working across internal stakeholders to develop and execute mitigation strategies. Major Duties and Responsibilities: Proactively engage with existing employer stakeholders and identify/influence emerging employer stakeholders across the US. Identify insights, positions and potential impact of new and emerging employer stakeholders and vendors. Build proactive share of voice with employer customers and influencers on Rx management topics. Support and contribute to internal Strategy Teams regarding emerging strategies and identification of external SMEs. Collaborate with Government Affairs/Policy/Strategy Directors to connect and convene with new and emerging stakeholders and advocates. Work in conjunction with Employer Team Director and Marketing Director (and collaboratively with Principal National MOSL, Employer Channel) relative to employer channel resource development and messaging. Develop and deliver stakeholder appropriate resources to support access for the expanding AbbVie portfolio (DSA decks, case studies, condensed employer value-prop decks, case studies and benefit plan design resources) Cultivate national employer KOLs and advocates to help shape external education and policy in collaboration with Government Affairs/Policy/Strategy teams. Monitor, inform and deliver market insights to internal business partners. Lead education initiatives in conjunction with Market Access Training on key trends impacting purchasers and AbbVie access/gross-to-net. Establish AbbVie as credible source for non-branded information and disseminate via industry meetings and electronic sites / social media (consistent with AbbVie Communications/PR guidelines). Support efforts to integrate Employer Strategy into AbbVie Business Planning process. Assist AbbVie Employer Corporate Account Team Leader with managing budget and execution of sponsorships and memberships, consistent with AbbVie Office of Ethics and Compliance (OEC) guidelines. Establish AbbVie as a national leader and key partner in the employer channel. Work with Big 3 PBM/GPO KAM teams and respective rebate analysts to ensure contract compliance. Quantify volume/sales associated with employer child accounts and access changes. Participate in internal task forces relating to member/patient access. Bachelor’s degree in Business, Life Sciences, or a related field required. Minimum of 5 years of Account Executive or Market Access experience within the healthcare industry; employee benefits consulting (EBC) experience and/or PBM experience is a plus. Proven ability to operate effectively in large, complex geographies, influence diverse stakeholders, and deliver commercial results. Demonstrated capability in negotiation, stakeholder engagement, and strategic planning/development and execution. Strong analytical skills, especially related to Rx contract terms/language and the commercial payor market. Effective communication and presentation skills (written and oral) with both technical and non-technical audiences. Experience managing complexity and collaborating with cross-functional, matrixed teams; agility and team-orientation required. Customer-centric approach and proven ability to act as primary point of contact for internal and external stakeholders. Ability to work autonomously, manage ambiguity, and identify/influence key customers. Understanding of the evolving healthcare environment—including ACA, CAA, ERISA, clinical guidelines, and formulary/utilization management. Adept at delivering product and disease state value proposition materials to a range of customers. Highest ethical standards and compliance with AbbVie Office of Ethics and Compliance (OEC) policies. Significant domestic travel required (up to 50%) for customer interactions, industry meetings and internal meetings. An essential requirement of your position is to satisfy all applicable health care industry representative (HCIR) credentialing requirements to gain and maintain entry into facilities and organizations that are in your assigned territory. You must also be in good standing and/or eligible to obtain these credentials. Driving a personal auto or company car or truck, or a powered piece of material handling equipment. Valid driver’s license: Ability to pass a pre-employment drug screening test and meet safe driving requirements. Preferred: 10+ years’ experience in pharmaceutical, Rx supply chain, employee benefit consulting, or healthcare organization. Deep understanding of commercial business models and payor markets.

The Delivery Operations Systems Administrator is responsible for the configuration, administration, and continuous optimization of the Workfront platform as the organization’s primary project execution tool. In addition, this role supports the broader project systems ecosystem—including platforms such as Microsoft Dynamics 365, Project Operations, PowerBI, and/or other enterprise tools. The position ensures project systems remain aligned with enterprise processes, governance standards, financial reporting requirements, and evolving operational needs. This individual also supports enhancements, integrations, documentation, and user enablement across multiple systems to ensure consistent, scalable, and compliant use of project operations tools. Workfront Platform Administration (Primary Responsibility) Administers and maintains Workfront configuration, including layouts, groups, teams, access levels, workflows, portfolios, templates, and custom forms. Manages Workfront roles, permissions, governance standards, and user provisioning. Ensures Workfront data integrity, process alignment, and compliance with PMO and operational frameworks. Designs and maintains Workfront reports and dashboards to support operational and executive visibility. Ensures alignment with their manager and the Enterprise Workfront Product Owner prior to initiating any largescale enhancements or system implementations. Ensures consistency and accuracy in project, task, and timetracking data. Supports audit and quality management reporting requirements. MultiPlatform Support & Enterprise Tool Administration Represents Workfront across the organization while collaborating with peer system owners to maintain and support a connected, interoperable enterprise tool landscape. Provides configuration support across other enterprise project systems, including Microsoft Dynamics 365, Project Operations, PowerBI, and/or related platforms. Supports setup, configuration, testing, documentation, and user enablement for new systems or modules as they are introduced. Contributes to crossplatform process alignment to maintain consistency in project lifecycle workflows. Systems Integration & Data Flow Alignment Supports integrations among Workfront, Dynamics 365, Project Operations, PowerBI, and/or enterprise data hubs. Partners with Operations, PMO, Finance, and Technology teams to maintain synchronization of project, task, time entry, and financial alignment workflows. Helps refine and document current state versus future state process flows as systems evolve. Governance, Optimization & Process Standards Participates in audits of system configuration, templates, custom fields, permissions, and licenses across platforms. Supports roadmap execution for Workfront cleanup, rationalization, and cross system consistency. Ensures documentation is current and standardized for Workfront and/or other project related systems. Promotes platform best practices and encourages consistent usage across teams. Issue Resolution, Change Management & Support Troubleshoots system issues, logs enhancements, and partners with technical teams to implement solutions. Supports training, release communications, and adoption across Workfront and other project systems. Facilitates sessions to address systemic blockers in project setup, reporting, or data consistency. CrossFunctional Collaboration Acts as a connector between PMO, Operations, Finance, Data & Analytics, and IT. Provides visibility into risks, dependencies, and upcoming system changes. Supports crossfunctional alignment for ongoing process improvements and system needs. All other duties as assigned. Bachelors of Sciences or Arts is required; equivalent experience considered. Experience and/or Training Minimum 3 years of relevant experience in Workfront administration, project management operations, or enterprise system configuration. Experience with Microsoft Dynamics 365, PowerBI, or similar platforms. Strong understanding of project management methodologies, business process alignment, and cross‑functional operations. Experience supporting or administering integrated systems in a matrixed environment.

As the Supply Chain Planner , you are responsible for providing and maintaining sufficient inventory to support area of responsibility and may also develop and maintain production schedules. A primary function will be to work with customers as well as with Purchasing to identify, develop, monitor, and control resources to meet goals and objectives. Responsibilities Manage Material Requirements Plan (MRP) inventory forecasts to support Master Production Schedule (MPS). Determine raw material or commodity/code needs and proper inventory levels. Create system requisitions and monitor delivery of materials, while communicating priorities to Receiving and Incoming Quality Assurance (IQA). Communicate with all functional areas to ensure that material needs are met (Receiving, Quality, Labs, Purchasing, Transportation, Manufacturing, Finishing, and MS&T). Communicate significant changes in forecast volumes that may require changes in purchasing strategy. Communicate with test labs and quality assurance, where applicable, to establish and track delivery dates for raw materials or manufactured products on test. Establish performance reports to monitor, measure and address control, where necessary, of supplier performance to assure timely and quality performance of supplier. Prepare monthly inventory reports to summarize current obsolete and surplus items, DOH, working inventory and total inventory. Manage timely disposition of obsolete and rejected materials through Material Destruct Orders (MDO’s). Where applicable, facilitate financial coverage discussions with Brand Teams accordingly. Identify large Purchase Price Variances (PPV). Take a leadership role in compiling the monthly PPV reports. Research and implement improvement opportunities with Purchasing and Finance. Become proficient with the use of planning systems like SAP and tools like Excel. We have an opening for a NEST Readiness Coordinator to oversee and execute LLNL’s Nuclear Emergency Support Team (NEST) responder readiness program. This role requires familiarity with DOE Order 153.1 and LLNL’s compliance with these requirements. You will administer and maintain readiness and training records, execute routine readiness checks and notifications using established procedures, and prepare recurring reports for program customers and management. Additional key aspects of the program include coordination of the on-call watchbill schedule, determining which qualified responders are assigned to on-call periods based on established eligibility and coverage requirements, and verifying required training and readiness items are current prior to assignment. The position coordinates updates across institutional systems and stakeholders, resolves routine issues by interpreting applicable guidelines, and escalates discrepancies that could impact readiness or on-call coverage. This position will be in the NEST Program Element within the Global Security Principal Directorate’s Nuclear Threat Reduction (N) Program. In this role, you will Participates in the development, maintenance, and improvement of the NEST responder readiness database and associated tools. Partner with the Readiness Program Lead, assess and analyze established readiness support processes and workflows, ensuring tasks are completed accurately and on time. Respond to customer questions and resolve routine readiness administration issues by interpreting and explaining procedures, guidelines, and manuals. Maintain, review data, and summarize results to support resolution of readiness discrepancies. Maintain service area records, databases, and documentation for responder readiness and training tracking. Collect, validate, reconcile, compile, and report readiness information across systems, such as, ARMS, TRAKEN, WCD, and related tools. Prepare routine and standard reports for customer use and management decision-making, including completion status, discrepancy tracking, and readiness summaries. Monitor routine readiness checks, notifications, and follow-ups; track completion and document exceptions. Maintain an escalation contact list/tree for routing readiness issues to the appropriate points of contact. Build, publish, and maintain the LLNL Master NEST on-call watch and deployment roster, determining on-call assignments using established coverage rules, qualification criteria, and availability inputs from Deployment POCs and responder organizations. Maintain documentation of responder requirements (on-call expectations, baseline training, gear and communications requirements as applicable), updating content per established guidance. Support upkeep of the NEST Deskbook by performing updates, maintaining version control, and routing edits for review/approval per defined process. Maintain a database used to document NEST facility capabilities, resources, and configurations. Coordinate onboarding/offboarding administrative steps for contractor and subcontractor personnel that support NEST readiness, such as, access requests, account tracking, required documentation, and following established procedures. Track issuance and inventory records for communications devices, such as,pagers, cell phones, Starlink units, and coordinate updates with supporting organizations. Support tracking of vendor/contract readiness-related information by maintaining records and reporting actions to the appropriate contract or technical points of contact. Perform other duties as assigned. This position requires an Active DOE Q clearance (or active Top-Secret clearance) with ability to obtain Sensitive Compartmented Information access. Experience coordinating responder readiness activities, workflow, and processes in- service operations, customer service, operations support, logistics, or mission support environment. Ability to maintain accurate records, databases, and documentation using tools such as SharePoint lists/libraries, spreadsheets, or similar systems. Experience in collecting, validating, and reporting operational data with attention to detail and data integrity. Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to document processes and requirements clearly and explain procedures to customers. Experience in tracking and coordinating multiple, parallel tasks and following through discrepancies to closure. Experience working collaboratively with cross-functional teams and multiple stakeholders. Must have a valid California driver’s license. Qualifications We Desire Bachelor’s degree in business, accounting, finance, information management/technology, or related field, or equivalent combination of education and related experience. Experience in technical operations, logistics, mission support, or emergency/incident response environments. Familiarity with LLNL and/or NEST-associated systems and processes, such as, ARMS, TRAKEN, WCD, paging/cell systems, or similar tracking and communication tools. Experience with reporting tools, such as, SharePoint and dashboards. Experience in preparing recurring operational status reports and creating basic graphical summaries, charts, and tables. Experience supporting and improving operational processes and documentation including standard operating processes, deskbooks, and playbooks; editing, version control, routing updates; consolidating requirements; and developing new tracking methods or tools. The Center for Global Security Research (CGSR) was established at Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL) in 1996 to bring together experts from the science, technology, and policy communities to address pressing national security challenges. For over 20 years, CGSR has engaged diverse perspectives on topics important to national security, deterrence, diplomacy, dual-use technology, arms control, nonproliferation, space, cyber, biosecurity, and energy security. We have openings in Fall 2026 for undergraduate students to engage in practical research on global security topics. Students will work with CGSR over the duration of three to four months as a research associate (RA). RAs will engage in practical research to further their educational and career goals, while also supporting the development of strategies for national security and LLNL’s mission focus areas. Examples of relevant fields of research include nuclear deterrence, arms control, nonproliferation, emerging technologies, cybersecurity, space, biological & chemical security, and energy security. CGSR’s objectives are as follows: To explore the dynamics of potential 21st century strategic conflicts (i.e., those with a potential nuclear aspect) and to formulate ideas about how to achieve U.S. deterrence and other objectives in such conflicts. To explore the sources and characteristics of strategic competition in the emerging security environment and to formulate organizing concepts to enhance the competitive position of the United States and its allies and partners over the long term. To identify whether and how technically based approaches can address new challenges to national and international security. To catalyze broader national and international thinking about the requirements of effective deterrence, assurance, and strategic stability in a changed and changing security environment. To assist in the development of new generations of experts motivated by a clear view of the changed and changing security environment. More information on CGSR, its research focus areas, and its publications can be found at https://cgsr.llnl.gov/ . This job will be closed to applicants on May 31, 2026. You will Conduct an independent research project on an agreed upon topic aligned with CGSR/LLNL research priorities under the supervision of CGSR staff. Support CGSR/LLNL through contributions to ongoing research activities. Tasks may include contributing to literature reviews, annotated bibliographies, and workshop summary reports. Attend relevant research seminars, speakers’ series, and workshops. Present research to LLNL staff at end of the assignment. Prepare end-of-assignment technical report or publication. Perform all assignments in accordance with ES&H, security, and business practice requirements and policies. Perform other duties as assigned. Must be eligible to access the Laboratory in compliance with Section 3112 of the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA). See Additional Information section below for details. Must be currently enrolled in an accredited university or have completed AA/AS degree in a field of research aligned with CGSR analytic priorities. Areas of study include international relations and/or security, political science, economics, public policy, emerging technologies, nonproliferation, energy, biosecurity, foreign language studies, or related fields. Demonstrated academic and/or professional achievement in a relevant field of research aligned with CGSR analytic priorities. Strong record of independent research and publication, or a strong proposal of research to be done while at CGSR and in future academic and professional settings. Ability to work in a team environment. Pay Range $23.26 - $31.62 Hourly This position is under a step structure. Please note that the step is determined by your academic level. Transcripts are required.

This includes healthcare decision-makers (HCDMs) within national employer plan sponsors, employee benefit consultants (EBCs), and employer coalitions, as well as emerging stakeholders/influencers/vendors, national organizations, and professional/advocacy organizations. The Employer NAE provides branded and unbranded messaging to employers and employer influencers/KOLs regarding the value and differentiation of AbbVie therapies to accelerate access to treatment and the use of benefit plan designs to identify and minimize barriers to affordable and predictable Rx access. The NAE also delivers messaging relating to disease state and burden of illness to increase the awareness of treatment solutions and explore solutions and develop best practices/case studies. The Employer NAE will provide leadership to distinguish AbbVie in the employer channel, be a convener of stakeholders and regional/national KOLs and SMEs, and provide strategic insights internally in support of evolving business needs to ensure timely awareness of market changes and trends and inform internal business leads to ensure a rapid response to external disruptors and Rx management strategies which impact affordable access to AbbVie’s therapies. This role is highly collaborative and consultative and requires partnering and interfacing with numerous cross-functional teams (Market Access leadership, Payer Strategy and Cross Portfolio Strategy and Pipeline, Training, Market Analytics Business Insights, Business Evolution Strategy Development (BESD), Brand Sales/Marketing, Government Affairs and Policy, Corporate Strategy, US Medical Affairs/Value & Access and Medical Outcomes Science & Science Liaisons (MOSLs); Finance, Legal, Compliance, Communications/PR, Field Reimbursement Leadership, Brand Sales/Marketing teams and internal Centers of Excellence (CoE). The NAE must demonstrate the ability to anticipate and act proactively and effectively in uncertain situations. Additionally, the NAE requires significant collaboration with the Corporate Accounts KAM teams, providing timely insights regarding evolving contracting trends and evolving rebate models, educating client-facing teams, and providing updates regarding downstream employer clients and formulary initiatives. This position does not have direct reports but does require the ability to manage and lead without authority across cross-functional teams while also being able to work independently and productively. The Employer NAE is the lead for regional employer initiatives working in conjunction with the Regional Account Executive (RAE) teams and Regional Directors, as well as compliant collaboration with the Population Heath Account Executive (PHAE) team. This includes identifying opportunities and/or employer access issues and training/educating and executing on use of Employer Team resources and messaging to health plan, health system, PBM and employer customers. This role also is a key collaborator with other national field-based teams including the Field Reimbursement team, educating team members on market disruptors and problem-solving on employer-focused access issues. The Employer NAE serves as a key role in cataloguing key disruptors and potential patient disruption and analyzing potential financial (Gross to Net) impact, as well as working across internal stakeholders to develop and execute mitigation strategies. Major Duties and Responsibilities: Proactively engage with existing employer stakeholders and identify/influence emerging employer stakeholders across the US. Identify insights, positions and potential impact of new and emerging employer stakeholders and vendors. Build proactive share of voice with employer customers and influencers on Rx management topics. Support and contribute to internal Strategy Teams regarding emerging strategies and identification of external SMEs. Collaborate with Government Affairs/Policy/Strategy Directors to connect and convene with new and emerging stakeholders and advocates. Work in conjunction with Employer Team Director and Marketing Director (and collaboratively with Principal National MOSL, Employer Channel) relative to employer channel resource development and messaging. Develop and deliver stakeholder appropriate resources to support access for the expanding AbbVie portfolio (DSA decks, case studies, condensed employer value-prop decks, case studies and benefit plan design resources) Cultivate national employer KOLs and advocates to help shape external education and policy in collaboration with Government Affairs/Policy/Strategy teams. Monitor, inform and deliver market insights to internal business partners. Lead education initiatives in conjunction with Market Access Training on key trends impacting purchasers and AbbVie access/gross-to-net. Establish AbbVie as credible source for non-branded information and disseminate via industry meetings and electronic sites / social media (consistent with AbbVie Communications/PR guidelines). Support efforts to integrate Employer Strategy into AbbVie Business Planning process. Assist AbbVie Employer Corporate Account Team Leader with managing budget and execution of sponsorships and memberships, consistent with AbbVie Office of Ethics and Compliance (OEC) guidelines. Establish AbbVie as a national leader and key partner in the employer channel. Work with Big 3 PBM/GPO KAM teams and respective rebate analysts to ensure contract compliance. Quantify volume/sales associated with employer child accounts and access changes. Participate in internal task forces relating to member/patient access. Bachelor’s degree in Business, Life Sciences, or a related field required. Minimum of 5 years of Account Executive or Market Access experience within the healthcare industry; employee benefits consulting (EBC) experience and/or PBM experience is a plus. Proven ability to operate effectively in large, complex geographies, influence diverse stakeholders, and deliver commercial results. Demonstrated capability in negotiation, stakeholder engagement, and strategic planning/development and execution. Strong analytical skills, especially related to Rx contract terms/language and the commercial payor market. Effective communication and presentation skills (written and oral) with both technical and non-technical audiences. Experience managing complexity and collaborating with cross-functional, matrixed teams; agility and team-orientation required. Customer-centric approach and proven ability to act as primary point of contact for internal and external stakeholders. Ability to work autonomously, manage ambiguity, and identify/influence key customers. Understanding of the evolving healthcare environment—including ACA, CAA, ERISA, clinical guidelines, and formulary/utilization management. Adept at delivering product and disease state value proposition materials to a range of customers. Highest ethical standards and compliance with AbbVie Office of Ethics and Compliance (OEC) policies. Significant domestic travel required (up to 50%) for customer interactions, industry meetings and internal meetings. An essential requirement of your position is to satisfy all applicable health care industry representative (HCIR) credentialing requirements to gain and maintain entry into facilities and organizations that are in your assigned territory. You must also be in good standing and/or eligible to obtain these credentials. Driving a personal auto or company car or truck, or a powered piece of material handling equipment. Valid driver’s license: Ability to pass a pre-employment drug screening test and meet safe driving requirements. Preferred: 10+ years’ experience in pharmaceutical, Rx supply chain, employee benefit consulting, or healthcare organization. Deep understanding of commercial business models and payor markets.

Position Summary Machine/grind parts/tools to conform to blueprints/drawings Duties and responsibilities The following reflects management’s definition of essential functions for this job but does not restrict the tasks that may be assigned. Management may assign or reassign duties and responsibilities to this job at any time due to reasonable accommodation or other reasons Maintain accurate inventory levels of CNC and HMC tooling, ensuring proper organization and storage. Inspect tooling for wear and determine when resharpening is required, coordinating with the manufacturer as needed. Perform grinding and relief operations on tooling as required. Assemble tooling for CNC and HMC machines as needed. Rework HMC manifold parts as required. Calibrate torque wrenches to ensure accuracy and compliance with standards. Machine and grind fixtures and parts as needed to support production. Operate CNC machines while adhering to blueprint specifications and quality standards. Conduct stability studies on gauges to ensure reliability and precision. Perform initial inspections of parts/tools when required. Support training efforts for manual machining processes. Maintain a clean and organized work while following 5S. Adhere to all safety, sanitation, and Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) requirements. Perform additional duties as assigned by the manager. Supervisory Responsibilities None Physical Requirements While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently required to do the following: Lift and move up to 50 pounds without assistance Able to stand for long periods of time Ability to load/unload machines (requires repetitive lifting and bending) Work Environment Majority of the work time is spent in a manufacturing environment where temperatures are often warm or cool, depending upon the season, and noise level can be moderate to high PPE required as determined by company safety standards: safety glasses, ear plugs, gloves, safety shoes Highschool diploma or equivalent preferred 5 or more years of experience as a toolmaker/machinist Demonstrated ability to setup and troubleshoot tooling issues Ability to assist/develop and or improve processes on new or existing parts with a complete understanding of machining fundamentals and practices Ability to use all relevant measurement equipment Ability to follow written and verbal instructions given in English Ability to meet quality and productivity standards Ability to read blueprints thoroughly Computer skills, intermediate knowledge Microsoft Office Strong attention to detail Ability to work as a part of a team Ability to be at workstation on time, every day unless authorized

Under general supervision, follows oral and/or written instructions in performance of a wide variety of skilled technical maintenance, repair, and testing on complex digital and analog electronic components, electrical and electro-mechanical components, cable assemblies, sub-assemblies, assemblies, field replaceable units (FRU) and systems to support a wide variety of Robotic Systems. Ability to communicate effectively with technical and non-technical internal customers. Acute attention to detail; excellent organizational skills. High level of professional integrity and ethics Ability to work varying shifts. Must have ability to complete training courses. Ability to work in a team environment. Excellent hand-eye coordination. Vision abilities required include close, distance, color, depth and ability to adjust focus. Work Environment: Typical production & repairs environment. General knowledge of clean and organized work areas and practices. High urgency and stress associated with customer deadlines. Some risk of exposure to electrical shock and commonly used chemical compounds such as epoxy, denatured alcohol and acetone. Willing and able to work extended hours when necessary.

TRAINING The Sales Trainee (ST) is a training role. Upon successful participation in the training program, the ST is eligible to interview for open Account Sales Manager (ASM) roles. Upon completion of the program and certification, if no ASM or otherwise qualified role is available AND the ST is meeting performance standards, the employee may remain in the ST role up to 12-months OR until an ASM or another qualified role is available (whichever comes first). Once an ASM or another qualified role is available, the certified ST must interview for that available role. If promotion to the role of ACCOUNT SALES MANAGER (or other role) does not happen prior to the expiration of the 12-mos completion period, the SALES TRAINEE role will be vacated due to end of assignment unless an exception applies. For exception, based on continued high performance, no open roles and certification completion, a manager may extend the 12-month completion period an additional 6-months. The ST role is an at-will position, meaning that the Company or ST can terminate the employment relationship at any time, for any reason or no reason at all, with or without cause. Specializes in working in facilities that manufacture a finished product for sale, or sale to another organization for use in an end product. Performs microbial control cleaning procedures that must comply with current Good Manufacturing Practices (cGMP) and regulatory guidelines which include documentation of work procedures frequently audited by the FDA and other regulatory agencies. The work will be accomplished under the general supervision of Lead Personnel and an area Supervisor. Responsibilities Performs cross contamination cleaning methods in areas that require microbial control. Completes cGMP documentation of training or cleaning performed on paper and electronic devices. Prepares cleaning solutions based on cGMP regulated mixing instructions. Performs microbial control cleaning techniques on walls, ceiling and floors based on cGMP regulated cleaning frequencies. Completes preventive maintenance work orders to meet cGMP cleaning requirements. Follows specific gowning procedures and performs cGMP entrance and exit procedures for controlled environments. Operates bailing and compacting equipment. Operates various types of hand held battery and electric cleaning equipment. Operates various types of battery and electric walk behind or ride-on floor cleaning equipment. Performs safety and preventive maintenance inspections on housekeeping power equipment and small tools and wears approved PPE. High School Diploma or equivalent. Must be able to read and comprehend written information to include Corporate Quality Documents, Divisional Operating Procedures, Departmental Operating Procedures and Safety Guidelines. Must be able to comply with cGMP, regulatory guidelines and able to write legibility in English and complete accurate and legible written records in compliance with cGMP when documenting work performed, on paper documents and electronic devices auditable by regulatory agencies. Must be able to operate a computer to complete required compliance & technical training. Must have the ability to learn and perform cleaning techniques to meet regulatory requirements. Must have the ability to work alone or as a team member sharing responsibility and work tasks. Must be able to perform all cleaning specialist job functions. Basic physical requirements are but are not limited to: stand for 7 hours per shift, regularly lift 35 pounds 50 times per shift, occasionally lift 50 pounds 6 times per shift, walk approximately 2000 feet per hour, climb 6 flights of stairs per shift, work on knees 30 minutes per shift, bend / Squat 200 times per shift, rotate left / right 200 times per shift.

The Real-Time Graphics Specialist is responsible for the design, development, deployment, and optimization of high-quality real-time broadcast graphics for live studio and event productions. This role blends advanced creative execution with strong technical expertise to support dynamic, on-air visual storytelling. The Specialist manages the graphics production lifecycle — from concept through live delivery — while collaborating closely with producers, directors, and technical teams. This position plays a key role in maintaining broadcast standards, improving workflows, troubleshooting live graphics issues, and contributing to innovation in augmented reality (AR), virtual reality production VR, and data-driven graphics. This is a hands-on role requiring creativity, precision, technical depth, and the ability to perform under live broadcast deadlines. Key Responsibilities 1. Graphics Design & Development Create and customize templates and animations for live broadcasts, including lower thirds, over-the-shoulder graphics, data visualizations, touchscreen graphics, and virtual/augmented reality elements Develop and deploy graphics using real-time rendering engines such as Vizrt, Unreal Engine, Zero Density, Flowics, or HTML-based systems Plan, build, maintain, and update graphic directories and playout systems for studio and event workflows Translate creative direction into compelling design, animation, and layout solutions Optimize graphics for performance, stability, and compliance with broadcast standards Prepare and manage image files and assets for production use Ensure visual consistency and adherence to brand standards 2. Workflow Management & Process Optimization Manage the full graphics production pipeline from concept to on-air execution Organize and maintain a centralized graphics asset library with proper version control and archiving Establish, document, and improve efficient workflows and best practices Track and report on project deliverables and performance metrics Assist with hardware/software upgrades and studio builds 3. Collaboration & Live Production Support Collaborate with producers, directors, show teams, and technical staff to meet project goals Serve as a primary contact for troubleshooting real-time graphics issues during live broadcasts Support graphics playout in live event and studio environments Work closely with production teams to design graphics tailored to specific programs or segments Communicate clearly with to manage expectations and ensure timely delivery Independently research and resolve technical challenges 4. Innovation & Industry Advancement Stay current with emerging technologies in real-time graphics and broadcast production Explore opportunities in AR, VR, virtual studios, and data-driven storytelling Contribute innovative ideas that elevate production value and visual storytelling Continuously expand technical skillsets and share knowledge with peers Basic Qualifications Minimum 5+ years of professional experience in real-time television graphics with a strong portfolio/demo reel Advanced expertise in platforms such as Vizrt, Unreal Engine, Zero Density, Flowics, or similar systems Strong understanding of broadcast standards, live production workflows, and playout systems Advanced 2D and 3D animation skills with strong typography and layout abilities Excellent troubleshooting and problem-solving skills under live broadcast pressure Strong organizational and communication skills Ability to work flexible hours in live production environments Desired Characteristics: 8+ years of live broadcast graphics experience Familiarity with AR/VR workflows and virtual production tools Knowledge of 3D modeling and animation tools such as Cinema 4D, Blender, or Maya Experience implementing hardware/software upgrades or new studio builds Education Required: High School Diploma or equivalent Preferred: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience in design, animation, broadcast technology, or related field Work Environment In-office requirement: four days per week Must be able to work flexible schedules, including evenings and weekends

In this internship, you will conduct advanced research and engineering in 3D perception, scene understanding, and machine learning to address challenges in autonomous systems. Integrate the resulting system/software into existing Bosch platform. Summarize research findings in high-quality paper and/or patent submissions. Basic Qualifications Currently enrolled and pursing a Ph.D. or Master student in Computer Science or related fields Hands-on experience on developing computer vision and deep learning algorithms with focus on at least two of the following areas: multimodal transformers, diffusion models, NeRF/Gaussian Splatting, video generation, 3D scene understanding, autonomous driving, behavior modeling/prediction, SfM, voxel/BEV grid-based feature representation. Strong background in math and statistics. Good communication and teamwork skills.

Position Purpose: Installs and repairs all electrical work throughout the treatment distribution system. Performs electrical work to maintain, install, repair or alter electrical systems found in treatment and pumping facilities, including electrical construction, installation, maintenance, and repair. Primary Duties/Responsibilities: Troubleshoot malfunctioning equipment to determine the nature of the problem, repair small and large electrical appliances, repair electronic components of electrical equipment as required for continued operations, make emergency electrical repairs to generators and pumps, and perform related duties as required; and perform related duties as assigned. Perform electrical work to maintain, install or repair all electrical systems, facilities and pump stations. Repair or replace defective or worn electrical parts, components and controlling software in electrical systems and devices, electrical motors, generators, pumps, controllers, lighting systems, and other fixtures and equipment. Work independently and make sound decisions regarding work methods and tools; read, interpret, apply, and enforce applicable codes and standards as related to electrical installation; apply State, Federal, and local safety regulations and codes to electrical work. Work safely both independently and as a crew member on high voltages up to 600 volts AC; work safely near energized primary and secondary lines with voltages up to 600 Volts AC. Read and works from electrical blueprints and drawings. Comprehend and make inferences from written material; read and interpret blueprints, wiring diagrams, and work orders. Perform preventative maintenance on electrical systems, motors and equipment. Inspect newly installed electrical equipment and lighting to ensure safe operation as well as code compliance. Maintain accurate records of work performed, materials used, and associated costs. Perform associated work including digging, trenching, occasional concrete finishing and removal, and lifting electrical equipment, conduit and pipe. Replaces defective wiring. Control wiring experience required. Variable Frequency Drive experience recommended. Work Environment: While performing the duties of this job, the employee is routinely exposed to a variety of outside weather conditions, including very hot temperatures. The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate. This employee can work in high voltages up to 600 Volts AC. Education/Experience/Background: High School Diploma/GED is required. 5 years journey level electrical experience required. Knowledge/Skills/Abilities: Knowledge of methods, materials, tools, equipment, and procedures used in the installation, maintenance, repair, replacement and alteration of electrical equipment; components and parts used in modern electrical wiring systems such as pumps, motors, controls and lighting. Basic understanding of overhead line construction, Nation Electric Code and Federal and State OSHA standards. Read, interpret and enforce applicable State and Federal codes and requirements. Ability to communicate with all levels including team, management, clients, and vendors in a professional manner both orally and in writing. Safety procedures in electrical maintenance and operations. The employee must be able to operate electric motors fueled by gasoline, diesel, or gaseous fuels, paint, welding, and fabrication equipment, and other hand tools required. Required Certification/Licenses/Training: Valid industrial electrician’s license preferred. Physical Requirements: The employee is frequently required to stand, walk, climb stairs or ladders, sit, use hands to finger, handle or feel, reach with hands and arms, climb or balance, stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl and taste or smell. The employee may regularly lift 10-20 pounds and may occasionally lift and or move up to 50 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include the ability to distinguish color, close vision and distance vision.

Conduct security audits of security systems and procedures to ensure that consistency and accuracy are maintained. Assign and/or conduct investigations regarding theft, vandalism, drug use, employee misconduct and recommend appropriate action. High level of interpersonal skills to handle sensitive and confidential situations and documentation. Demonstrated leadership competency including decision-making skills, verbal and written communication skills, interpersonal skills, team management skills, and analytical skills

Primary Function of Position: The Inventory Analyst 2 is responsible for analyzing, improving and maintaining optimal inventory health to support efficient operations and evolving business needs across the 3PL network. This role requires strong analytics capabilities, clear communication, cross functional collaboration, sound judgement, and well-structured inventory planning & compliance. The analyst drives accuracy, prevents shortages, identifies risks and supports continuous improvement across the supply chain. Essential Job Duties: Inventory Accuracy & Root Cause Analysis Analyze recurring discrepancy patterns and implement proactive corrective actions. Perform in-depth root cause analysis for complex exceptions. Troubleshoot and resolve material master related discrepancies. Inventory Health, Monitoring & Optimization Analyze inventory data to report trends, risks and opportunities from improvement. Identify overstated quantities in the system that may impact end customers and prevent material shortages. Monitor inventory levels to support operational reliability. Identify and resolve expired or at-risk inventory. Cross-Functional Issue Resolution Investigate and resolve inventory issues related to stock transfer orders across internal & 3PL plants. Act as a liaison between Inventory Control and broader operation groups. Reporting & Communication Prepare and present inventory reports, KPIs and insights to leadership and cross-functional stakeholders. Use data to influence decision-making and optimize inventory strategies. Provide mentorship by sharing inventory knowledge and analytical insights with team members. Process Governance & System Controls Maintain Kanban systems that align with operational replenishment strategies. Participating in UAT sign-off for system or process changes. Continuous Improvement & Project Support Collaborate cross-functionally to drive continuous improvement in Inventory Accuracy and processes. Support operational readiness efforts, analytics projects and ongoing process enhancements. Perform additional duties as assigned by management. Required Skills and Experience: Minimum 5 years in warehouse, inventory control experience Analytical Skills: ability to interpret complex data, perform trend analysis, and translate insights in actionable recommendations via Excel. Communication Skills: Strong verbal and written communication skills for reporting findings, and collaborating with stakeholders Liaison Skills: Proven ability to work cross-functionally and coordinate between departments Decision-Making Skills: sound judgment in evaluating options and recommending inventory actions under varying conditions Organizational Skills: Strong attention to detail with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines Required Education and Training Bachelor’s degree or the equivalent 5 years of experience in inventory management or related area. Working Conditions Ability to lift 35 pounds Extensive walking Preferred Skills and Experience Ability to multi-task. Fanatically Organized. SAP, Agile and Tableau software experience preferred.

Data Analysis & Insights Generation Conduct deep-dive analyses on logistics operations data to identify cost drivers, service gaps, efficiency opportunities, and risk areas across transportation modes (ocean, air, ground, rail). Perform root-cause analysis on logistics exceptions, delays, and cost variances, providing leadership with clear explanations and data-backed recommendations. Build and maintain analytical models in Excel, Python, or SQL to support scenario planning, freight benchmarking, and lane-level performance analysis. Synthesize large, multi-source datasets into concise, meaningful narratives that highlight the "so what" behind the numbers for non-technical stakeholders. Monitor key logistics metrics and proactively flag anomalies, trends, or emerging issues to leadership before they become operational problems. Executive & Leadership Data Support Serve as the primary analyst supporting leadership data requests—triaging, prioritizing, and fulfilling ad hoc analytical asks from Directors, VPs, and the Chief Supply Chain Officer with speed and accuracy. Prepare executive-ready data packages, briefing decks, and slide materials for business reviews, QBRs, Board presentations, and leadership offsites. Partner directly with logistics leaders to understand their strategic questions and proactively build self-serve reporting tools that reduce dependency on ad hoc requests over time. Develop and maintain a standardized logistics metrics glossary and reporting governance framework to ensure consistency of definitions across teams and stakeholders. Facilitate data storytelling—transforming raw analytical findings into compelling narratives with appropriate visualizations, context, and recommended actions. Data Governance & Quality Own data quality monitoring for key logistics datasets, establishing validation checks, alerting processes, and remediation workflows to maintain data integrity. Document data sources, transformation logic, report definitions, and refresh schedules to ensure operational continuity and knowledge transfer. Partner with IT and data governance teams to ensure logistics data assets comply with enterprise data standards, privacy requirements, and audit controls. Cross-Functional Collaboration Collaborate with supply chain planning, procurement, finance, and operations teams to integrate logistics data with broader business analytics initiatives. Support digital transformation programs (Control Tower, Digital Twin, AI workflows) by providing analytical expertise, data validation, and reporting infrastructure. Train and enable logistics operations team members to leverage self-serve Power BI reports and reduce reliance on manual data pulls. Power BI Report Development & Management Design, build, and maintain enterprise-grade Power BI dashboards and reports that provide leadership with real-time and historical visibility into logistics KPIs—including freight spend, on-time delivery, carrier performance, transit times, and inventory flow. Develop and manage the Global Logistics reporting suite, ensuring reports are accurate, refreshed on schedule, visually intuitive, and aligned to leadership requirements. Implement best-in-class data modeling practices in Power BI, including star schema design, DAX measures, calculated columns, and row-level security (RLS) for appropriate data access. Work with IT and data engineering teams to establish reliable data pipelines feeding Power BI from source systems including EDW, TMS, carrier portals, and third-party visibility platforms. THE POSITION: Medical Information is a critically important customer-facing function that supports the safe and effective use of pharmaceutical company products by providing timely, scientifically balanced, evidence based, nonpromotional information in response to unsolicited requests from healthcare professionals, patients, caregivers, and payers. Medical Information also plays an important role in post-marketing handling of adverse events and product complaints. As part of the Medical Information Contact Center (MICC) team, this position delivers industry-leading services, which include Contact Center staffing for responding to product information requests, identifying and handling of adverse events and/or product quality issues, and medical writing as needed to generate written response for use in response to medical questions received. This position requires clinical and therapeutic knowledge, critical and analytical thinking, and customer/patient-centric approach. Medical Information Specialists typically support multiple pharmaceutical clients, multiple products, and multiple therapeutic areas. ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES: Our employees are tasked with delivering excellent business results through the efforts of their teams. These results are achieved by: MEDICAL INFORMATION SUPPORT Respond to medical information inquiries from physicians, pharmacists, nurses, and other health care professionals, consumers, and payers. Utilize medical information skills to identify, research, and critically evaluate medical literature to create responses to medical information inquiries. Utilize writing skills for adverse event and product complaint narrative during intake as well as medical inquiry custom responses. Handle requests across multiple channels and platforms (phone, email, CRM, chat, etc.) Identify adverse events and product complaints during interactions with customers. Perform intake sufficient to generate adverse event and product complaint reports in compliance with EVERSANA-MICC and client standard operating procedures. Knowledge of FDA’s postmarketing adverse event reporting regulations and safety terminology. Ability to make accurate assessments regarding what information needs to be obtained and level or depth of information to be collected. Coordinate processes necessary for responding to product quality-related complaints. This process may involve interactions with personnel in the following departments: Quality Assurance, Regulatory Affairs, and the complainant.
