This is a remote position with up to 50% domestic travel required. Candidates may reside in any state within the United States and should expect frequent national travel. The AbbVie Employer NAE is responsible for supporting and implementing strategic business initiatives in response to the changing healthcare environment, deployed specifically to national Employer Stakeholders via the AbbVie Employer Team with a focus on improving workforce health and productivity and maximizing strategic access to AbbVie’s therapies. The Employer NAE will be accountable for building effective stakeholder strategies and engagements that are on the forefront of emerging concerns impacting employee access, affordability, disease state awareness/management and medication value and access. This includes healthcare decision-makers (HCDMs) within national employer plan sponsors, employee benefit consultants (EBCs), and employer coalitions, as well as emerging stakeholders/influencers/vendors, national organizations, and professional/advocacy organizations. The Employer NAE provides branded and unbranded messaging to employers and employer influencers/KOLs regarding the value and differentiation of AbbVie therapies to accelerate access to treatment and the use of benefit plan designs to identify and minimize barriers to affordable and predictable Rx access. The NAE also delivers messaging relating to disease state and burden of illness to increase the awareness of treatment solutions and explore solutions and develop best practices/case studies. The Employer NAE will provide leadership to distinguish AbbVie in the employer channel, be a convener of stakeholders and regional/national KOLs and SMEs, and provide strategic insights internally in support of evolving business needs to ensure timely awareness of market changes and trends and inform internal business leads to ensure a rapid response to external disruptors and Rx management strategies which impact affordable access to AbbVie’s therapies. This role is highly collaborative and consultative and requires partnering and interfacing with numerous cross-functional teams (Market Access leadership, Payer Strategy and Cross Portfolio Strategy and Pipeline, Training, Market Analytics Business Insights, Business Evolution Strategy Development (BESD), Brand Sales/Marketing, Government Affairs and Policy, Corporate Strategy, US Medical Affairs/Value & Access and Medical Outcomes Science & Science Liaisons (MOSLs); Finance, Legal, Compliance, Communications/PR, Field Reimbursement Leadership, Brand Sales/Marketing teams and internal Centers of Excellence (CoE). The NAE must demonstrate the ability to anticipate and act proactively and effectively in uncertain situations. Additionally, the NAE requires significant collaboration with the Corporate Accounts KAM teams, providing timely insights regarding evolving contracting trends and evolving rebate models, educating client-facing teams, and providing updates regarding downstream employer clients and formulary initiatives. This position does not have direct reports but does require the ability to manage and lead without authority across cross-functional teams while also being able to work independently and productively. The Employer NAE is the lead for regional employer initiatives working in conjunction with the Regional Account Executive (RAE) teams and Regional Directors, as well as compliant collaboration with the Population Heath Account Executive (PHAE) team. This includes identifying opportunities and/or employer access issues and training/educating and executing on use of Employer Team resources and messaging to health plan, health system, PBM and employer customers. This role also is a key collaborator with other national field-based teams including the Field Reimbursement team, educating team members on market disruptors and problem-solving on employer-focused access issues. The Employer NAE serves as a key role in cataloguing key disruptors and potential patient disruption and analyzing potential financial (Gross to Net) impact, as well as working across internal stakeholders to develop and execute mitigation strategies. Major Duties and Responsibilities: Proactively engage with existing employer stakeholders and identify/influence emerging employer stakeholders across the US. Identify insights, positions and potential impact of new and emerging employer stakeholders and vendors. Build proactive share of voice with employer customers and influencers on Rx management topics. Support and contribute to internal Strategy Teams regarding emerging strategies and identification of external SMEs. Collaborate with Government Affairs/Policy/Strategy Directors to connect and convene with new and emerging stakeholders and advocates. Work in conjunction with Employer Team Director and Marketing Director (and collaboratively with Principal National MOSL, Employer Channel) relative to employer channel resource development and messaging. Develop and deliver stakeholder appropriate resources to support access for the expanding AbbVie portfolio (DSA decks, case studies, condensed employer value-prop decks, case studies and benefit plan design resources) Cultivate national employer KOLs and advocates to help shape external education and policy in collaboration with Government Affairs/Policy/Strategy teams. Monitor, inform and deliver market insights to internal business partners. Lead education initiatives in conjunction with Market Access Training on key trends impacting purchasers and AbbVie access/gross-to-net. Establish AbbVie as credible source for non-branded information and disseminate via industry meetings and electronic sites / social media (consistent with AbbVie Communications/PR guidelines). Support efforts to integrate Employer Strategy into AbbVie Business Planning process. Assist AbbVie Employer Corporate Account Team Leader with managing budget and execution of sponsorships and memberships, consistent with AbbVie Office of Ethics and Compliance (OEC) guidelines. Establish AbbVie as a national leader and key partner in the employer channel. Work with Big 3 PBM/GPO KAM teams and respective rebate analysts to ensure contract compliance. Quantify volume/sales associated with employer child accounts and access changes. Participate in internal task forces relating to member/patient access. Bachelor’s degree in Business, Life Sciences, or a related field required. Minimum of 5 years of Account Executive or Market Access experience within the healthcare industry; employee benefits consulting (EBC) experience and/or PBM experience is a plus. Proven ability to operate effectively in large, complex geographies, influence diverse stakeholders, and deliver commercial results. Demonstrated capability in negotiation, stakeholder engagement, and strategic planning/development and execution. Strong analytical skills, especially related to Rx contract terms/language and the commercial payor market. Effective communication and presentation skills (written and oral) with both technical and non-technical audiences. Experience managing complexity and collaborating with cross-functional, matrixed teams; agility and team-orientation required. Customer-centric approach and proven ability to act as primary point of contact for internal and external stakeholders. Ability to work autonomously, manage ambiguity, and identify/influence key customers. Understanding of the evolving healthcare environment—including ACA, CAA, ERISA, clinical guidelines, and formulary/utilization management. Adept at delivering product and disease state value proposition materials to a range of customers. Highest ethical standards and compliance with AbbVie Office of Ethics and Compliance (OEC) policies. Significant domestic travel required (up to 50%) for customer interactions, industry meetings and internal meetings. An essential requirement of your position is to satisfy all applicable health care industry representative (HCIR) credentialing requirements to gain and maintain entry into facilities and organizations that are in your assigned territory. You must also be in good standing and/or eligible to obtain these credentials. Driving a personal auto or company car or truck, or a powered piece of material handling equipment. Valid driver’s license: Ability to pass a pre-employment drug screening test and meet safe driving requirements. Preferred: 10+ years’ experience in pharmaceutical, Rx supply chain, employee benefit consulting, or healthcare organization. Deep understanding of commercial business models and payor markets.

The Muliplatform Producer works closely with correspondents to gather all editorial elements needed for stories, including social media newsgathering, research, securing interviews, and confirming information with government agencies and community organizations. The Producer must be able to manage multiple assignments simultaneously, adapt quickly to breaking news, and collaborate closely with editorial leadership and production teams. The ideal candidate has experience working in a multiplatform newsroom and demonstrates strong knowledge of social media and digital storytelling. This role requires strong editorial judgment, the ability to work under tight deadlines, and a solid understanding of national and international news, including breaking news coverage. Responsibilities include requesting graphics and other visual elements that support storytelling and enhance the presentation of stories across platforms. The Multimedia Producer may also assist in writing scripts and editorial content for newscasts and digital coverage. This position requires a strong visual sense and the ability to identify compelling video, natural sound, and other elements that strengthen the narrative and overall impact of a story. In addition, the Multiplatform Producer is responsible for booking guests on a daily basis for linear, streaming, and digital platforms. The candidate must be able to work effectively in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment, including weekends, early mornings, and flexible hours to accommodate last-minute. The position requires the ability to work flexible hours, including nights, weekends, and holidays, particularly during breaking news coverage or special assignments. This position demands the ability to work effectively under tight deadlines within a fast-paced and evolving newsroom environment. Responsibilities: • Gather editorial elements needed for stories, including social media newsgathering, research, and securing interviews. • Contribute to the day’s editorial direction by pitching story ideas, exclusive reports, and interview opportunities. • Participate in breaking news coverage and special projects. • Demonstrate proficiency in using social media platforms for newsgathering, research, and content creation. • Maintain a well-established network of contacts, including community organizations, business leaders, federal and local officials, and other media outlets. • Work effectively in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment, including weekends, early mornings, and flexible hours to accommodate last-minute scheduling changes. • Operate under the guidance of the VP of News Gathering • This position is based on-site in Miami, Florida, and requires regular in-office presence to support newsroom operations. • Contribute to a collaborative, inclusive, and accountable newsroom culture. Basic Requirements: Bachelor’s degree in journalism, Communications, or equivalent professional experience. Minimum of 3 years of on-air news reporting experience in Spanish. Experience producing digital video content in a newsroom environment is a plus. Proficiency in social media platforms and trends. Fluent in Spanish, written and spoken. Fluent in English Desired Characteristics: Accustomed to working in a team and collaborating with all levels within the organization. Proven excellent interpersonal skills combined with a strong sense of how to visually tell a compelling story. Outside of the box thinker Proficient in I-News, helpful Additional Requirements: Interested candidate must submit a resume/CV through www.nbcunicareers.com to be considered (job #: ) Must be willing to work in the greater Miami, Florida area. Must be 18 years or older. Must have a valid driver’s license. Must have unrestricted work authorization to work in the United States Must be covered by Solutions, NBCU’s Alternative Dispute Resolution Program

For exception, based on continued high performance, no open roles and certification completion, a manager may extend the 12-month completion period an additional 6-months. The ST role is an at-will position, meaning that the Company or ST can terminate the employment relationship at any time, for any reason or no reason at all, with or without cause. Specializes in working in facilities that manufacture a finished product for sale, or sale to another organization for use in an end product. Performs microbial control cleaning procedures that must comply with current Good Manufacturing Practices (cGMP) and regulatory guidelines which include documentation of work procedures frequently audited by the FDA and other regulatory agencies. The work will be accomplished under the general supervision of Lead Personnel and an area Supervisor. Responsibilities Performs cross contamination cleaning methods in areas that require microbial control. Completes cGMP documentation of training or cleaning performed on paper and electronic devices. Prepares cleaning solutions based on cGMP regulated mixing instructions. Performs microbial control cleaning techniques on walls, ceiling and floors based on cGMP regulated cleaning frequencies. Completes preventive maintenance work orders to meet cGMP cleaning requirements. Follows specific gowning procedures and performs cGMP entrance and exit procedures for controlled environments. Operates bailing and compacting equipment. Operates various types of hand held battery and electric cleaning equipment. Operates various types of battery and electric walk behind or ride-on floor cleaning equipment. Performs safety and preventive maintenance inspections on housekeeping power equipment and small tools and wears approved PPE. High School Diploma or equivalent. Must be able to read and comprehend written information to include Corporate Quality Documents, Divisional Operating Procedures, Departmental Operating Procedures and Safety Guidelines. Must be able to comply with cGMP, regulatory guidelines and able to write legibility in English and complete accurate and legible written records in compliance with cGMP when documenting work performed, on paper documents and electronic devices auditable by regulatory agencies. Must be able to operate a computer to complete required compliance & technical training. Must have the ability to learn and perform cleaning techniques to meet regulatory requirements. Must have the ability to work alone or as a team member sharing responsibility and work tasks. Must be able to perform all cleaning specialist job functions. Basic physical requirements are but are not limited to: stand for 7 hours per shift, regularly lift 35 pounds 50 times per shift, occasionally lift 50 pounds 6 times per shift, walk approximately 2000 feet per hour, climb 6 flights of stairs per shift, work on knees 30 minutes per shift, bend / Squat 200 times per shift, rotate left / right 200 times per shift.

The Real-Time Graphics Specialist is responsible for the design, development, deployment, and optimization of high-quality real-time broadcast graphics for live studio and event productions. This role blends advanced creative execution with strong technical expertise to support dynamic, on-air visual storytelling. The Specialist manages the graphics production lifecycle — from concept through live delivery — while collaborating closely with producers, directors, and technical teams. This position plays a key role in maintaining broadcast standards, improving workflows, troubleshooting live graphics issues, and contributing to innovation in augmented reality (AR), virtual reality production VR, and data-driven graphics. This is a hands-on role requiring creativity, precision, technical depth, and the ability to perform under live broadcast deadlines. Key Responsibilities 1. Graphics Design & Development Create and customize templates and animations for live broadcasts, including lower thirds, over-the-shoulder graphics, data visualizations, touchscreen graphics, and virtual/augmented reality elements Develop and deploy graphics using real-time rendering engines such as Vizrt, Unreal Engine, Zero Density, Flowics, or HTML-based systems Plan, build, maintain, and update graphic directories and playout systems for studio and event workflows Translate creative direction into compelling design, animation, and layout solutions Optimize graphics for performance, stability, and compliance with broadcast standards Prepare and manage image files and assets for production use Ensure visual consistency and adherence to brand standards 2. Workflow Management & Process Optimization Manage the full graphics production pipeline from concept to on-air execution Organize and maintain a centralized graphics asset library with proper version control and archiving Establish, document, and improve efficient workflows and best practices Track and report on project deliverables and performance metrics Assist with hardware/software upgrades and studio builds 3. We have an opening for a Field Technician to provide technical support and customer services in the management of hazardous and radioactive waste. Under general supervision you will perform a variety of technical functions in collecting, packaging, labeling, identifying, documenting, segregating, consolidating, treating, and storing hazardous, explosive and radioactive waste generated by various LLNL programs. This position is in the Radioactive and Hazardous Waste Management (RHWM) Program and part of the Special Project Group supporting Site 200 within the Strategic Deterrence Directorate. This position requires full-time on-site presence due to the nature of the work. This position will be filled at either level based on knowledge and related experience as assessed by the hiring team. Additional job responsibilities (outlined below) will be assigned if hired at the higher level. In this role you will Perform a wide variety of waste management activities, often wearing personal protective equipment (PPE) such as anti-C’s, respirator, hearing protection, etc., to collect, package, label, identify, segregate, consolidate, treat, store, and verify hazardous, low level radioactive, mixed and/or transuranic waste. Operate wastewater retention tanks and/or systems, perform pump-outs, perform lab packing of waste chemicals and manage waste container storage areas. Perform field testing (pH, visual etc.) and sampling of waste to verify characterization and/or treatment results and operate radiation survey instruments to obtain radiological data. Operate a variety of vehicles up to and including 5-ton trucks, use material handling equipment (fork trucks, drum handling equipment, mechanical pump systems, etc.), and use hand and power tools. Respond to environmental emergencies at LLNL and work with cross-organizational personnel performing decontamination of facility infrastructure and equipment. Gather, analyze, and record basic pertinent data and maintain detailed and accurate records associated with radioactive and hazardous waste to properly characterize and manage the waste. Complete and maintain training requirements per Federal, State, and LLNL requirements. Provide high-end customer service with a wide range of waste generators as the front-line interface between RHWM and waste generators. Support various scope Decontamination and Demolition (D&D) projects on behalf of LLNL. Perform all assignments in accordance with ES&H, security, and business practice requirements and policies. Perform other duties as assigned. Additional job responsibilities at the 504.3 Level Solve difficult radioactive and hazardous waste management problems using established guidelines and routine techniques and procedures. Plan and execute waste management projects including directing the activities of other technicians. Conduct On-the-Job-Training and provide mentoring and leadership for less experienced technicians. We have an opening for a Document Compliance Coordinator to navigate a complex matrix of federal, institutional and organizational requirements. You will collaborate with engineers and subject matter experts to initiate, develop, document and evaluate comprehensive technical procedures, documents and safety plans. This position will support the Superblock (SBK) facility within the Strategic Deterrence Directorate. This position may offer a hybrid schedule, which includes the flexibility to work from home one or more days per week, after a probationary period. The specifics of the hybrid schedule, including the exact number of days required in the office and virtual work options, may vary based on the needs of the team and the organization. This position will be filled at either level based on knowledge and related experience as assessed by the hiring team. Additional job responsibilities (outlined below) will be assigned if hired at the higher level. In this role you will Analyze and implement documentation processes, procedures, and practices to ensure activities within the facility are performed in compliance with requirements in federal regulations, institutional procedures, and the nuclear facility safety bases. Evaluate procedures and process documents to verify facility requirements are adequately implemented, controls identified in the safety basis documents are maintained, and technical and management reviews are conducted. Serve as a contact for SBK processes, procedures, practices, manuals, guidance documents and safety plans and provide guidance to others related to SBK administrative procedures associated with document compliance. Collaborate with subject matter experts to initiate, develop, review, revise, implement and evaluate documentation that impact SBK facilities and systems, as well as LLNL programs. Monitor document tracking and routing, and ensure revision control using electronic applications (e.g., Enterprise Lifecycle Management-Unclassified [ELM-U]/Windchill) for configuration management of documents. Assist in planning, coordinating, and conducting periodic assessments to determine conformance with regulations, LLNL requirements, and SBK plans and procedures, including management self-assessments, observations and inspections, relating to SBK processes and other operational activities; recommend and coordinate completion of corrective action plans related to deficiencies. Manage technical information communications and interface with the LLNL programs and facilities personnel related to facility procedures; solicit feedback and facilitate comment resolution. Perform other duties as assigned. Additional job responsibilities, at the A23.3 level Develop, plan, review, assess, analyze, and implement administrative processes, procedures, and practices by applying in depth knowledge to ensure SBK activities comply with governing requirements, including federal regulations, LLNL procedures, and nuclear facility safety basis documents. Provide professional support to program/practice/policy development and implementation efforts; assists with program research and ongoing monitoring of results. Serves as a subject matter expert and trusted resource, providing informed recommendations to management on policy updates and changes. Ability to secure and maintain a U.S. DOE Q level security clearance which requires U.S. citizenship. Associate Degree in a related field or equivalent combination of education and related experience in a business, operational and/or organizational area. Experience interpreting, reviewing and analyzing administrative processes, policies, procedures and practices to determine if the activities they address are performed in compliance with complex regulations and requirements. Effective technical composition, writing and editing skills and experience effectively composing professional documentation with the ability to obtain a Procedure Professionals Association (PPA) Certification. Experience tracking, compiling and monitoring data necessary to coordinate corrective actions. Proficient verbal and written communication skills necessary to manage scientific and technical communications across multidisciplinary teams, with effective collaboration and communication skills necessary to effectively explain and present proposed changes to documents and processes. Effective organizational and interpersonal skills necessary to resolve problems and sensitive/confidential issues with tact, discretion, and mature judgment. Strong proficiency in Microsoft Word and a solid working knowledge of Excel, FileMaker Pro, Adobe Acrobat, and EDMS (such as SharePoint or Windchill) with the ability to learn new software quickly. Additional qualifications at the A23.3 level Experience researching, tracking, compiling and monitoring data necessary to conduct self-assessment activities, effectively present findings, and coordinate corrective actions. Broad and specialized knowledge of and experience in related work activities and multi-faceted internal processes. Experience training and mentoring personnel on document control within a regulated environment, ensuring compliance with applicable requirements. What You Will Do All Lowe’s associates deliver quality customer service while maintaining a store that is clean, safe, and stocked with the products customers need. As a Customer Service Associate/Loader, this means: • Being friendly, professional, and engaging customers to help answer questions. • Retrieving, loading, and replenishing merchandise. • Helping customers and staff move merchandise safely. The Customer Service Associate/Loader assists customers by loading merchandise into their vehicles. The Customer Service Associate/Loader also replenishes shelves for the next customers. Safety is critical because this associate lifts and moves merchandise for staff and customers frequently throughout his/her shift. Travel Requirements: This role does not require regular travel; however, this role may need to travel on occasion to meetings, trainings, or to support neighboring stores. What You Need To Succeed Minimum Qualifications • 6 months experience using a computer, including inputting, accessing, modifying, or outputting information. • 6 months experience using common retail technology, such as smart phones and tablets. • Ability to obtain sales related licensure or registration as may be required by law. Preferred Qualifications • 6 months retail experience. • 6 months experience as a Loader at any home improvement or hardware retailer. • 6 months experience working in any department at a Lowe's retail store. • 6 months retail merchandising experience, including performing Zone Recovery, stocking, down stocking, facing/fronting product, pricing, maintaining signage, and housekeeping. • 6 months experience in any industry inspecting, carrying, loading, and unloading product or material in or out of vehicles. AI.Accelerate Overview: Are you a technically curious and ambitious undergraduate student with a passion for Artificial Intelligence? ServiceNow invites you to explore our AI.Accelerate program where you can develop practical AI skills and gain hands-on experience in a dynamic, fast-paced, and immersive environment. This eight-week unpaid bootcamp is designed to provide a comprehensive introduction to the core concepts and techniques of AI, with a focus on practical application and real-world problem-solving. You'll learn from experienced instructors, work on challenging projects, and collaborate with a cohort of talented peers. Dates: June 15 – July 31, 2026 (Virtual) + Week 8—beginning of August (In Person) Location: Virtually via Zoom Duration: 4 hours a week (plus homework) What You'll Learn: Agentic AI Foundations: Understand what makes an AI system "agentic" — including autonomy, reasoning, and action-taking — and how LLMs are evolving from chat tools into decision-making agents. Agentic Design Patterns: Explore key architectural patterns including React, chain-of-thought, tool use, and memory, and understand the difference between single-agent and multi-agent systems and when to use each. Prompt Engineering: Learn techniques for writing reliable, production-grade prompts that drive consistent and predictable agent behavior at scale. Building Agents: Design agents that use tools, APIs, and external data sources, and learn how to structure agent memory — both short-term and long-term — for complex, multi-step tasks. Multi-Agent Orchestration: Build and manage multi-agent workflows where agents collaborate, delegate, and hand off tasks to accomplish goals that no single agent could complete alone. Evaluation Frameworks: Learn why evaluations are the most critical part of building AI systems and how to design frameworks that define what to measure and how to measure it effectively. AI Safety & Responsible Use: Understand real-world failure modes including hallucination, prompt injection, and behavioral drift, and learn how to build guardrails and safety checks into agentic pipelines. Capstone Project: Design, build, evaluate, and defend an AI agent from scratch — putting every concept from the program into practice and presenting your work to a panel of ServiceNow engineers and leaders. Innovative Learning Structure: A blend of lectures, hands-on laboratories, and collaborative projects fostering a cohort- based, hands on learning experience. The program concludes with an in-person experience where participants showcase their capstone project, explore career opportunities at ServiceNow, and connect with the broader engineering community. please note: this is an unpaid program and is not an internship To be successful in this role you: Have experience in leveraging or critically thinking about how to integrate AI into work processes, decision-making, or problem-solving. This may include using AI-powered tools, automating workflows, analyzing AI-driven insights, or exploring AI’s potential impact on the function or industry . Are an Undergraduate student majoring or minoring in Computer Science (CS), Computer Engineering (CE), or Data Analytics. or related field, with a graduation date no earlier than December 2027 Are experienced in Python programming. Are experienced with and/or have knowledge of fundamental AI concepts Have availability to attend the full duration of the boot camp from June 15, 2026 to July 31, 2026 and then available to participate onsite in the beginning of August Application Process: Interested candidates should apply by April 15, 2026 , to be considered. Applications are evaluated until the application deadline only; therefore, early submission is recommended as spots are limited! Please submit a resume, a cover letter, and any related project work or AI experience. In your cover letter please share: Why do you want to participate in this AI bootcamp? Where do you see AI helping you in the future?

The AbbVie Employer NAE is responsible for supporting and implementing strategic business initiatives in response to the changing healthcare environment, deployed specifically to national Employer Stakeholders via the AbbVie Employer Team with a focus on improving workforce health and productivity and maximizing strategic access to AbbVie’s therapies. The Employer NAE will be accountable for building effective stakeholder strategies and engagements that are on the forefront of emerging concerns impacting employee access, affordability, disease state awareness/management and medication value and access. The NAE also delivers messaging relating to disease state and burden of illness to increase the awareness of treatment solutions and explore solutions and develop best practices/case studies. The Employer NAE will provide leadership to distinguish AbbVie in the employer channel, be a convener of stakeholders and regional/national KOLs and SMEs, and provide strategic insights internally in support of evolving business needs to ensure timely awareness of market changes and trends and inform internal business leads to ensure a rapid response to external disruptors and Rx management strategies which impact affordable access to AbbVie’s therapies. This role is highly collaborative and consultative and requires partnering and interfacing with numerous cross-functional teams (Market Access leadership, Payer Strategy and Cross Portfolio Strategy and Pipeline, Training, Market Analytics Business Insights, Business Evolution Strategy Development (BESD), Brand Sales/Marketing, Government Affairs and Policy, Corporate Strategy, US Medical Affairs/Value & Access and Medical Outcomes Science & Science Liaisons (MOSLs); Finance, Legal, Compliance, Communications/PR, Field Reimbursement Leadership, Brand Sales/Marketing teams and internal Centers of Excellence (CoE). The NAE must demonstrate the ability to anticipate and act proactively and effectively in uncertain situations. This position does not have direct reports but does require the ability to manage and lead without authority across cross-functional teams while also being able to work independently and productively. This role also is a key collaborator with other national field-based teams including the Field Reimbursement team, educating team members on market disruptors and problem-solving on employer-focused access issues. The Employer NAE serves as a key role in cataloguing key disruptors and potential patient disruption and analyzing potential financial (Gross to Net) impact, as well as working across internal stakeholders to develop and execute mitigation strategies. Build proactive share of voice with employer customers and influencers on Rx management topics. Support and contribute to internal Strategy Teams regarding emerging strategies and identification of external SMEs. Collaborate with Government Affairs/Policy/Strategy Directors to connect and convene with new and emerging stakeholders and advocates. Monitor, inform and deliver market insights to internal business partners. Support efforts to integrate Employer Strategy into AbbVie Business Planning process. Strong analytical skills, especially related to Rx contract terms/language and the commercial payor market. The AbbVie Process Chemistry Chromatographic Separations Lab is actively seeking an Associate Scientist II or Scientist I. Our team collaborates with colleagues across multiple disciplines, offering expertise in preparative chromatography to support a broad range of AbbVie R&D programs. We maintain and utilize specialized equipment for various separation tasks, including the purification of peptides, ADC drug-linkers, and chiral compounds, as well as the isolation of low-level API impurities. Additionally, the team is responsible for pilot-scale preparative purification, developing scalable purification processes, and overseeing their implementation under cGMP guidelines at AbbVie's North Chicago Chemical Pilot Plant. This role will contribute to the development of novel/advanced separations technologies and broader efforts to develop new process technologies for advancing the AbbVie pipeline. We are seeking a motivated scientist who demonstrates initiative and technical proficiency in supporting research and development projects within a collaborative team environment. The ideal candidate will have hands-on experience developing chromatographic methods and troubleshooting complex separation challenges. Experience working with peptides is highly desirable, but not required for application. Key Responsibilities: Develop and execute purification processes supporting development of small molecule, antibody drug conjugate, and peptide clinical candidates. Demonstrate scientific initiative and creativity in planning, executing, and troubleshooting experiments, resolving key project challenges with an appropriate level of autonomy based on experience. Conduct a range of laboratory and pilot-scale tasks, analyze and interpret data, and drive project objectives, assuming responsibility for tasks in accordance with experience. Suggest, adapt, and, as appropriate, implement new or improved experimental protocols/techniques, consulting relevant literature as needed. Build and maintain strong collaborative relationships with peers and cross-functional partners. Foster a learning environment, encourage diverse ideas, and support continuous process improvement. Understand and adhere strictly to corporate standards for conduct, safety, quality, and proper handling of materials. Bachelor’s degree with at least 3 years (Associate Scientist II) or 5 years (Scientist I) relevant experience; or Master’s degree with no additional experience (Associate Scientist II) or typically +2 years of relevant experience (Scientist I). Strong technical background in Separations Science, with theoretical and practical knowledge required to independently carry out job functions. Demonstrated proficiency in developing, troubleshooting, and modifying chromatographic methods and purification protocols. Broad expertise in analytical techniques, with emphasis on chromatography, compound purification, and spectral analysis. Ability to search scientific literature and evaluate potential solutions to research problems. Effective written and oral communication skills; able to work collaboratively in multidisciplinary teams.

We have an opening for a NEST Readiness Coordinator to oversee and execute LLNL’s Nuclear Emergency Support Team (NEST) responder readiness program. This role requires familiarity with DOE Order 153.1 and LLNL’s compliance with these requirements. You will administer and maintain readiness and training records, execute routine readiness checks and notifications using established procedures, and prepare recurring reports for program customers and management. Additional key aspects of the program include coordination of the on-call watchbill schedule, determining which qualified responders are assigned to on-call periods based on established eligibility and coverage requirements, and verifying required training and readiness items are current prior to assignment. The position coordinates updates across institutional systems and stakeholders, resolves routine issues by interpreting applicable guidelines, and escalates discrepancies that could impact readiness or on-call coverage. This position will be in the NEST Program Element within the Global Security Principal Directorate’s Nuclear Threat Reduction (N) Program. In this role, you will Participates in the development, maintenance, and improvement of the NEST responder readiness database and associated tools. Partner with the Readiness Program Lead, assess and analyze established readiness support processes and workflows, ensuring tasks are completed accurately and on time. Respond to customer questions and resolve routine readiness administration issues by interpreting and explaining procedures, guidelines, and manuals. Maintain, review data, and summarize results to support resolution of readiness discrepancies. Maintain service area records, databases, and documentation for responder readiness and training tracking. Collect, validate, reconcile, compile, and report readiness information across systems, such as, ARMS, TRAKEN, WCD, and related tools. Prepare routine and standard reports for customer use and management decision-making, including completion status, discrepancy tracking, and readiness summaries. Monitor routine readiness checks, notifications, and follow-ups; track completion and document exceptions. Maintain an escalation contact list/tree for routing readiness issues to the appropriate points of contact. Build, publish, and maintain the LLNL Master NEST on-call watch and deployment roster, determining on-call assignments using established coverage rules, qualification criteria, and availability inputs from Deployment POCs and responder organizations. Maintain documentation of responder requirements (on-call expectations, baseline training, gear and communications requirements as applicable), updating content per established guidance. Support upkeep of the NEST Deskbook by performing updates, maintaining version control, and routing edits for review/approval per defined process. Maintain a database used to document NEST facility capabilities, resources, and configurations. Coordinate onboarding/offboarding administrative steps for contractor and subcontractor personnel that support NEST readiness, such as, access requests, account tracking, required documentation, and following established procedures. Track issuance and inventory records for communications devices, such as,pagers, cell phones, Starlink units, and coordinate updates with supporting organizations. Support tracking of vendor/contract readiness-related information by maintaining records and reporting actions to the appropriate contract or technical points of contact. Perform other duties as assigned. This position requires an Active DOE Q clearance (or active Top-Secret clearance) with ability to obtain Sensitive Compartmented Information access. Experience coordinating responder readiness activities, workflow, and processes in- service operations, customer service, operations support, logistics, or mission support environment. Ability to maintain accurate records, databases, and documentation using tools such as SharePoint lists/libraries, spreadsheets, or similar systems. Experience in collecting, validating, and reporting operational data with attention to detail and data integrity. Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to document processes and requirements clearly and explain procedures to customers. Experience in tracking and coordinating multiple, parallel tasks and following through discrepancies to closure. Experience working collaboratively with cross-functional teams and multiple stakeholders. Must have a valid California driver’s license. Qualifications We Desire Bachelor’s degree in business, accounting, finance, information management/technology, or related field, or equivalent combination of education and related experience. Experience in technical operations, logistics, mission support, or emergency/incident response environments. Familiarity with LLNL and/or NEST-associated systems and processes, such as, ARMS, TRAKEN, WCD, paging/cell systems, or similar tracking and communication tools. Experience with reporting tools, such as, SharePoint and dashboards. Experience in preparing recurring operational status reports and creating basic graphical summaries, charts, and tables. Experience supporting and improving operational processes and documentation including standard operating processes, deskbooks, and playbooks; editing, version control, routing updates; consolidating requirements; and developing new tracking methods or tools. The Center for Global Security Research (CGSR) was established at Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL) in 1996 to bring together experts from the science, technology, and policy communities to address pressing national security challenges. For over 20 years, CGSR has engaged diverse perspectives on topics important to national security, deterrence, diplomacy, dual-use technology, arms control, nonproliferation, space, cyber, biosecurity, and energy security. We have openings in Fall 2026 for undergraduate students to engage in practical research on global security topics. Students will work with CGSR over the duration of three to four months as a research associate (RA). RAs will engage in practical research to further their educational and career goals, while also supporting the development of strategies for national security and LLNL’s mission focus areas. Examples of relevant fields of research include nuclear deterrence, arms control, nonproliferation, emerging technologies, cybersecurity, space, biological & chemical security, and energy security. CGSR’s objectives are as follows: To explore the dynamics of potential 21st century strategic conflicts (i.e., those with a potential nuclear aspect) and to formulate ideas about how to achieve U.S. deterrence and other objectives in such conflicts. To explore the sources and characteristics of strategic competition in the emerging security environment and to formulate organizing concepts to enhance the competitive position of the United States and its allies and partners over the long term. To identify whether and how technically based approaches can address new challenges to national and international security. To catalyze broader national and international thinking about the requirements of effective deterrence, assurance, and strategic stability in a changed and changing security environment. To assist in the development of new generations of experts motivated by a clear view of the changed and changing security environment. More information on CGSR, its research focus areas, and its publications can be found at https://cgsr.llnl.gov/ . This job will be closed to applicants on May 31, 2026. You will Conduct an independent research project on an agreed upon topic aligned with CGSR/LLNL research priorities under the supervision of CGSR staff. Support CGSR/LLNL through contributions to ongoing research activities. Tasks may include contributing to literature reviews, annotated bibliographies, and workshop summary reports. Attend relevant research seminars, speakers’ series, and workshops. Present research to LLNL staff at end of the assignment. Prepare end-of-assignment technical report or publication. Perform all assignments in accordance with ES&H, security, and business practice requirements and policies. Perform other duties as assigned. Must be eligible to access the Laboratory in compliance with Section 3112 of the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA). See Additional Information section below for details. Must be currently enrolled in an accredited university or have completed AA/AS degree in a field of research aligned with CGSR analytic priorities. Areas of study include international relations and/or security, political science, economics, public policy, emerging technologies, nonproliferation, energy, biosecurity, foreign language studies, or related fields. Demonstrated academic and/or professional achievement in a relevant field of research aligned with CGSR analytic priorities. Strong record of independent research and publication, or a strong proposal of research to be done while at CGSR and in future academic and professional settings. Ability to work in a team environment. Pay Range $23.26 - $31.62 Hourly This position is under a step structure. Please note that the step is determined by your academic level. Transcripts are required.

You will Provide advanced administrative support to senior management team members within the Engineering Principal Associate Director's Office (PADO). Serve as a member of the Engineering administrative team representing management in daily matters; take initiative to gather, clarify, and disseminate information and coordinate activities; respond on their behalf on administrative matters to all levels of management, both internal and external to the Laboratory. Manage complex calendars independently determining scheduling priorities and plan and coordinate complex meetings and events. Serve as the lead point-of-contact for the Engineering Leadership Development Program (ELDP) and Engineering Excelled Program working with division administrative representatives to plan and execute events and tours including logistics. Act as a liaison between the ELDP Management Team including tracking and coordinating all ELDP events, site and laboratory tours, and leadership training sessions and updating ELDP project intake, dashboard, and feedback systems. Perform administrative support to the senior leader for Rapid Education and Placement (REAP) grant program and assist facilitators to deliver technical workshops at Las Positas College. Compile data from multiple sources for complex reports and presentations; establish and maintain complex databases, spreadsheets, and tracking/filing systems. Generate correspondence on own initiative and compose correspondence for management signature that may be sensitive in nature. Perform other duties as assigned. Ability to secure and maintain a U.S. DOE Q-level security clearance which requires U.S. citizenship. Advanced administrative knowledge and experience including accurate editing, grammar, and proofreading skills; advanced knowledge of office procedures, techniques, and methods. Advanced organizational skills, attention to detail, accuracy, and follow-through. Experience working under minimal supervision, in a multi-task environment with rapidly changing priorities, deadlines, and frequent interruptions. Advanced communication and interpersonal skills necessary to interact effectively with a multi-facet workforce and represent the organization with all levels of management, internal and external to the Laboratory, using tact, diplomacy, and discretion. Effective problem-solving and decision-making skills to anticipate, identify, and independently recommend appropriate actions and solutions to complex administrative problems. Ability to be self-motivated and flexible, exercising a high degree of discretion and mature judgment in handling business-sensitive and/or classified information, as well as personnel interactions. Advanced computer skills and experience with the Microsoft Office Suite and database and calendaring software, and the ability to learn new software quickly. Experience coordinating complex meetings and events. Qualifications We Desire Familiarity with LLNL's policies and procedures. Knowledge of LLNL business applications and processes such as LEAP, TIME, EAM, LTRAIN, ePay, and Cliqbook. Experience in branding or marketing ideas. Ability and motivation to learn new tools and platforms (e.g., MS Forms, SharePoint), proactively seeking out resources and trainings as needed. These positions are field based / remote in the following locations: CA, WA, OR, IA, MN, IN, OH, FL. Candidates must reside in one of the these states and be willing to travel for site visits. Purpose Advance AbbVie's pipeline by striving for excellence in clinical research, turning science into medicine for our patients and leveraging new advanced capabilities to drive industry leading performance. Partners with the investigator and site staff for meaningful and effective engagements positioning AbbVie as the choice in clinical trials. Focus on site clinical research that ensures appropriate conduct of the trial while driving improvement in data integrity, compliance, overall study performance and customer experience. Responsibilities Considered as the primary point of contact for the investigative site. High level of competency or experience in providing contextual information on the clinical trials, connects stakeholder to the investigative sites and strengthens AbbVie’s positioning. Aligns, trains and motivates the site staff and principal investigator on the goals of the clinical trial program, protocol and patient treatment principles for the trial ensuring a trusted partnership. Conducts site evaluation, site training, routine, and site closure monitoring activities with compliance to the protocol and monitoring plans, in accordance with applicable regulations, Good Clinical Practices (GCPs), ICH Guidelines, AbbVie Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), and quality standards, ensuring safety and protection of study subjects. Advanced understanding of site engagement and ability to customize site engagement strategy for assigned study (ies). Gather local/site insights and utilize site engagement tools such as the Customer Relationship Management (CRM) tool, to report/track progress and measure impact of that strategy. Advanced level of competency connecting the study protocol, scientific principles and clinical trial requirements to the day-to-day clinical trial execution activities. Evaluate and ensure effective recruitment and retention techniques/plans based on the patient disease journey. Develop solid knowledge of therapeutic area, asset and clinical landscape / patient journey to enable successful patient recruitment and overall protocol compliance. Possesses experienced level of competency to mentor and train less experienced CRAs on various aspects of work and provides input into their development. May participate in global/local task forces and initiatives. Responsible for activities as assigned by manager. Responsible for continuous risk-assessment proactively, and in collaboration with Central Monitoring team, monitor activities conducted by clinical sites to detect early overall study performance or patient safety issues. Advanced ability to think critically to resolve site risk signals while having robust understanding of site processes to drive study execution. Ensures preventative and corrective action plans are put into place, as needed, to mitigate risk and promote compliance using a customer centric approach. Identifies, evaluates and recommends new/potential investigators/sites on an on going basis. Potential sites may be identified through networking or internal AbbVie requests to assist in the placement of planned clinical studies with qualified investigators. Ensures quality of data submitted from study sites and assures timely submission of data, including appropriate reporting and follow-up for all safety events by site personnel. Ensures audit and regulatory inspection readiness at assigned clinical site at all times. Manages investigator payments as per executed contract obligations, as applicable. Qualifications Education: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent degree; health related preferred (e.g. Medical, Scientific, Nursing, Pharmacy). Minimum of 1 year of clinically related experience, of which a period of 6 months is required in clinical research monitoring of investigational drug or device trials. Familiar with risk‐based monitoring approach, onsite and offsite monitoring. Knowledge of appropriate therapeutic area indications is preferred with the ability to understand and apply scientific concepts as they relate to the conduct of clinical trials. Advanced knowledge on existing and emerging local regulatory and legal requirements, ICH/GCP Guidelines and applicable policies. Demonstrate strong cross-functional collaboration skills among internal and external stakeholders. Demonstrate strong planning and organizational skills and the ability to work effectively and efficiently in a dynamic environment with competing projects and deadlines. Advanced ability to leverage technology, tools and resources to provide customer centric support based on the health of the site. Strong interpersonal skills with excellent written, verbal, active listening and presentation skills, with ability to establish and leverage site relationships and trusted partnerships through engagement, motivation, and training. Ability to use functional expertise with appropriate guidance, leverage critical thinking skills and apply good judgement to address clinical site issues. Acts with integrity in accordance with AbbVie code of business conduct and leadership values. Self-motivated individual focused on delivering timely and quality outcomes in a fast-paced environment.

We have an opening for a Cloud Operations Engineer to join our team. In this position, you will be responsible for designing, implementing, and managing cloud solutions that support the National Nuclear Security Administration’s (NNSA) business services and programmatic missions, including scientific research and mission-critical operations. This position is in the Enterprise Infrastructure Services (EIS) Division within the Computing Directorate. You will work closely with multidisciplinary teams to drive innovation, improve scalability, and ensure the secure and efficient utilization of cloud resources for NNSA initiatives. This role supports multiple sites across the country and occasional travel is required to collaborate with stakeholders and partners. This position offers the opportunity to work in a dynamic and highly technical environment, supporting critical infrastructure for enterprise-level applications. This position requires full-time on-site presence due to the nature of the work. This position will be filled at either the SES.2 or SES.3 level based on knowledge and related experience as assessed by the hiring team. Additional job responsibilities (outlined below) will be assigned if hired at the higher level. In this role you will Deploy and manage cloud infrastructure (primarily AWS) in support of scientific, engineering, and business applications. Develop automation scripts and Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) solutions for cloud resource provisioning and management. Collaborate with researchers, engineers, and IT staff to migrate workloads and optimize applications for cloud environments. Implement and manage cloud financial operations (FinOps) practices to optimize cloud spending, track usage, and collaborate with stakeholders to ensure cost-effective resource allocation. Monitor cloud performance and usage, and implement solutions for high availability, scalability, and cost efficiency. Ensure compliance with Department of Energy (DOE) and NNSA security policies and federal regulations for cloud operations. Provide technical support, documentation, and training for cloud users across the enterprise. Stay abreast of emerging cloud technologies and recommend adoption of innovative solutions. Perform other duties as assigned. Additional job responsibilities at the SES.3 Level Develop and implement advanced cloud computing environments that align with customer needs and enterprise system strategies, ensuring optimal performance and scalability. Independently configure and utilize systems and cloud management tools to monitor, maintain, and optimize infrastructure operations effectively. Identify, troubleshoot, and document complex system and network issues to ensure timely resolution and minimize disruptions. Ability to obtain and maintain a US DOE Q-level security clearance which requires U.S. Citizenship. Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of technical education and relevant experience. Broad experience in cloud platform administration and support, with proficiency in technologies such as AWS, Azure, Google Cloud Platform, or hybrid cloud environments. Broad knowledge of cloud infrastructure operations, including resource provisioning, automation, and the use of infrastructure management tools. Proficient understanding of cloud support systems, such as virtual networking, identity and access management, and monitoring solutions. Comprehensive experience with cloud architecture documentation tools, including Visio and other office productivity software. Proficient in managing and troubleshooting cloud-based resources and services, including performance monitoring and incident response. Strong interpersonal, verbal, and written communication skills, with the ability to work independently while effectively collaborating with customers and team members. Additional Qualifications at the SES.3 Level Significant experience managing enterprise cloud environments, including platforms such as AWS, Azure, and hybrid cloud networking. Advanced knowledge of troubleshooting techniques, with strong skills in resolving issues through analysis of logs, metrics, and cloud-native diagnostic tools. Significant experience with resource provisioning, automation, and infrastructure as management tools, such as Terraform, CloudFormation, Cloud Development Kit, or similar platforms. Significant experience training and mentoring team members, focusing on cloud engineering best practices and architectural design principles. Desired Qualifications Active Department of Energy (DOE) Q-level clearance or active Top-Secret clearance issued by another U.S. government agency at the time of hire. AWS Certified Solutions Architect credential or an equivalent advanced cloud certification. Deep familiarity with hybrid cloud architectures and expert-level proficiency in integrating on-premises environments with cloud platforms in air-gapped environments. Comprehensive knowledge of compliance frameworks, such as National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), FedRAMP, and related standards, with proven experience implementing and maintaining compliance within cloud environments. This is a remote position with up to 50% domestic travel required. Candidates may reside in any state within the United States and should expect frequent national travel. The AbbVie Employer NAE is responsible for supporting and implementing strategic business initiatives in response to the changing healthcare environment, deployed specifically to national Employer Stakeholders via the AbbVie Employer Team with a focus on improving workforce health and productivity and maximizing strategic access to AbbVie’s therapies. The Employer NAE will be accountable for building effective stakeholder strategies and engagements that are on the forefront of emerging concerns impacting employee access, affordability, disease state awareness/management and medication value and access. This includes healthcare decision-makers (HCDMs) within national employer plan sponsors, employee benefit consultants (EBCs), and employer coalitions, as well as emerging stakeholders/influencers/vendors, national organizations, and professional/advocacy organizations. The Employer NAE provides branded and unbranded messaging to employers and employer influencers/KOLs regarding the value and differentiation of AbbVie therapies to accelerate access to treatment and the use of benefit plan designs to identify and minimize barriers to affordable and predictable Rx access. The NAE also delivers messaging relating to disease state and burden of illness to increase the awareness of treatment solutions and explore solutions and develop best practices/case studies. The Employer NAE will provide leadership to distinguish AbbVie in the employer channel, be a convener of stakeholders and regional/national KOLs and SMEs, and provide strategic insights internally in support of evolving business needs to ensure timely awareness of market changes and trends and inform internal business leads to ensure a rapid response to external disruptors and Rx management strategies which impact affordable access to AbbVie’s therapies. This role is highly collaborative and consultative and requires partnering and interfacing with numerous cross-functional teams (Market Access leadership, Payer Strategy and Cross Portfolio Strategy and Pipeline, Training, Market Analytics Business Insights, Business Evolution Strategy Development (BESD), Brand Sales/Marketing, Government Affairs and Policy, Corporate Strategy, US Medical Affairs/Value & Access and Medical Outcomes Science & Science Liaisons (MOSLs); Finance, Legal, Compliance, Communications/PR, Field Reimbursement Leadership, Brand Sales/Marketing teams and internal Centers of Excellence (CoE). The NAE must demonstrate the ability to anticipate and act proactively and effectively in uncertain situations. Additionally, the NAE requires significant collaboration with the Corporate Accounts KAM teams, providing timely insights regarding evolving contracting trends and evolving rebate models, educating client-facing teams, and providing updates regarding downstream employer clients and formulary initiatives. This position does not have direct reports but does require the ability to manage and lead without authority across cross-functional teams while also being able to work independently and productively. The Employer NAE is the lead for regional employer initiatives working in conjunction with the Regional Account Executive (RAE) teams and Regional Directors, as well as compliant collaboration with the Population Heath Account Executive (PHAE) team. This includes identifying opportunities and/or employer access issues and training/educating and executing on use of Employer Team resources and messaging to health plan, health system, PBM and employer customers. This role also is a key collaborator with other national field-based teams including the Field Reimbursement team, educating team members on market disruptors and problem-solving on employer-focused access issues. The Employer NAE serves as a key role in cataloguing key disruptors and potential patient disruption and analyzing potential financial (Gross to Net) impact, as well as working across internal stakeholders to develop and execute mitigation strategies. Major Duties and Responsibilities: Proactively engage with existing employer stakeholders and identify/influence emerging employer stakeholders across the US. Identify insights, positions and potential impact of new and emerging employer stakeholders and vendors. Build proactive share of voice with employer customers and influencers on Rx management topics. Support and contribute to internal Strategy Teams regarding emerging strategies and identification of external SMEs. Collaborate with Government Affairs/Policy/Strategy Directors to connect and convene with new and emerging stakeholders and advocates. Work in conjunction with Employer Team Director and Marketing Director (and collaboratively with Principal National MOSL, Employer Channel) relative to employer channel resource development and messaging. Develop and deliver stakeholder appropriate resources to support access for the expanding AbbVie portfolio (DSA decks, case studies, condensed employer value-prop decks, case studies and benefit plan design resources) Cultivate national employer KOLs and advocates to help shape external education and policy in collaboration with Government Affairs/Policy/Strategy teams. Monitor, inform and deliver market insights to internal business partners. Lead education initiatives in conjunction with Market Access Training on key trends impacting purchasers and AbbVie access/gross-to-net. Establish AbbVie as credible source for non-branded information and disseminate via industry meetings and electronic sites / social media (consistent with AbbVie Communications/PR guidelines). Support efforts to integrate Employer Strategy into AbbVie Business Planning process. Assist AbbVie Employer Corporate Account Team Leader with managing budget and execution of sponsorships and memberships, consistent with AbbVie Office of Ethics and Compliance (OEC) guidelines. Establish AbbVie as a national leader and key partner in the employer channel. Work with Big 3 PBM/GPO KAM teams and respective rebate analysts to ensure contract compliance. Quantify volume/sales associated with employer child accounts and access changes. Participate in internal task forces relating to member/patient access. Bachelor’s degree in Business, Life Sciences, or a related field required. Minimum of 5 years of Account Executive or Market Access experience within the healthcare industry; employee benefits consulting (EBC) experience and/or PBM experience is a plus. Proven ability to operate effectively in large, complex geographies, influence diverse stakeholders, and deliver commercial results. Demonstrated capability in negotiation, stakeholder engagement, and strategic planning/development and execution. Strong analytical skills, especially related to Rx contract terms/language and the commercial payor market. Effective communication and presentation skills (written and oral) with both technical and non-technical audiences. Experience managing complexity and collaborating with cross-functional, matrixed teams; agility and team-orientation required. Customer-centric approach and proven ability to act as primary point of contact for internal and external stakeholders. Ability to work autonomously, manage ambiguity, and identify/influence key customers. Understanding of the evolving healthcare environment—including ACA, CAA, ERISA, clinical guidelines, and formulary/utilization management. Adept at delivering product and disease state value proposition materials to a range of customers. Highest ethical standards and compliance with AbbVie Office of Ethics and Compliance (OEC) policies. Significant domestic travel required (up to 50%) for customer interactions, industry meetings and internal meetings. An essential requirement of your position is to satisfy all applicable health care industry representative (HCIR) credentialing requirements to gain and maintain entry into facilities and organizations that are in your assigned territory. You must also be in good standing and/or eligible to obtain these credentials. Driving a personal auto or company car or truck, or a powered piece of material handling equipment. Valid driver’s license: Ability to pass a pre-employment drug screening test and meet safe driving requirements. Preferred: 10+ years’ experience in pharmaceutical, Rx supply chain, employee benefit consulting, or healthcare organization. Deep understanding of commercial business models and payor markets.

Position Summary Machine/grind parts/tools to conform to blueprints/drawings Duties and responsibilities The following reflects management’s definition of essential functions for this job but does not restrict the tasks that may be assigned. Management may assign or reassign duties and responsibilities to this job at any time due to reasonable accommodation or other reasons Maintain accurate inventory levels of CNC and HMC tooling, ensuring proper organization and storage. Inspect tooling for wear and determine when resharpening is required, coordinating with the manufacturer as needed. Perform grinding and relief operations on tooling as required. Assemble tooling for CNC and HMC machines as needed. Rework HMC manifold parts as required. Calibrate torque wrenches to ensure accuracy and compliance with standards. Machine and grind fixtures and parts as needed to support production. Operate CNC machines while adhering to blueprint specifications and quality standards. Conduct stability studies on gauges to ensure reliability and precision. Perform initial inspections of parts/tools when required. Support training efforts for manual machining processes. Maintain a clean and organized work while following 5S. Adhere to all safety, sanitation, and Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) requirements. Perform additional duties as assigned by the manager. Supervisory Responsibilities None Physical Requirements While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently required to do the following: Lift and move up to 50 pounds without assistance Able to stand for long periods of time Ability to load/unload machines (requires repetitive lifting and bending) Work Environment Majority of the work time is spent in a manufacturing environment where temperatures are often warm or cool, depending upon the season, and noise level can be moderate to high PPE required as determined by company safety standards: safety glasses, ear plugs, gloves, safety shoes Highschool diploma or equivalent preferred 5 or more years of experience as a toolmaker/machinist Demonstrated ability to setup and troubleshoot tooling issues Ability to assist/develop and or improve processes on new or existing parts with a complete understanding of machining fundamentals and practices Ability to use all relevant measurement equipment Ability to follow written and verbal instructions given in English Ability to meet quality and productivity standards Ability to read blueprints thoroughly Computer skills, intermediate knowledge Microsoft Office Strong attention to detail Ability to work as a part of a team Ability to be at workstation on time, every day unless authorized

We have an opening for a Software Engineer to support the Collaborative Authorization for the Safety-basis Total Lifecycle Environment (CASTLE-PX) Project. CASTLE-PX is Risk Level 2 Safety Software, requiring a high-level of rigor to maintain SQA compliance. CASTLE-PX is a web-based, custom Java application deployed at Pantex and is being used to manage the safety-bases for weapon systems, site facilities, as well as several business processes. Working with a dynamic multi-disciplinary team of software developers, software quality engineers, and IT staff, your primary responsibilities will be to contribute to the application development, perform production support, test new releases, and help maintain the large volume of SQA support documents. This position is in the Applications, Simulations, and Quality (ASQ) Division within the Computing Directorate, in support of the CASTLE Project within the Weapon Technologies Engineering (WTE) Program. This position offers a hybrid schedule, blending in-person and virtual presence. You may have the flexibility to work from home a maximum of 2 days per week. In this role, you will Conduct technical tasks within design, implementation, deployment, and maintenance for a web-based software system using object-oriented analysis, design, and programming techniques. Participate in the requirements definition, analysis, design, implementation, debugging, testing, and optimization of the software system. Communicate regularly with stakeholders regarding status, needs, progress, and upcoming plans. May provide leadership and support to the Application team while engaging in continuous improvement across end-to-end processes. Collaborate with a large, cross-site, multi-disciplinary team of managers, engineers, and developers to define the project’s current priorities and future direction. This role will work collaboratively across show teams, the marketing organization, and the social strategy team to ensure content is timely, brand-aligned, and tuned to platform best practices. The ideal candidate has strong creative instincts, a working knowledge of social trends, and the ability to juggle multiple projects in a fast-paced environment. Flexibility is key, as show schedules and social moments often require off-hours attention. This position reports to the Director of Social & Design under Late Night Brand Marketing & Consumer Engagement. Key Responsibilities Design & Content Creation Design social assets across NBCE late‑night properties for TikTok, Instagram, X, Facebook, and YouTube. Develop digital branding elements, maintain style guides, and uphold brand standards. Edit static and motion graphics using existing templates; create new templates as needed. Edit short-form videos, including clips, recaps, compilations, and original social-first pieces. Create platform‑native content with an understanding of comedic timing and show voice. Participate in content ideation and brainstorms across shows and platforms. Social Coordination & Publishing Help manage social project workflows, including asset intake, timelines, approvals, and delivery. Draft platform‑specific social copy in show voices. Support on-platform posting and publishing across channels where needed. Monitor social platforms for trends, moments, and opportunities relevant to late-night shows. Collaborate closely with social leads and strategists to align content with insights and goals. Maintain organized asset folders, calendars, and trackers for ongoing content needs. Cross-Team Collaboration Communicate clearly with show producers, talent teams, designers, editors, and internal partners. Partner with show production teams on custom content needs, topical moments, and quick turns. Adapt quickly to last-minute changes, breaking moments, and schedule shifts. Basic Requirements: 1+ years of experience in design, social, or related fields preferred. Proficiency in After Effects, Premiere, Photoshop, and Illustrator. Experience working on a social, digital, GFX, agency, or entertainment team a plus. Working knowledge of TikTok, Instagram, X, Facebook, and YouTube (including posting workflows & best practices). Experience with photography, video, and audio production. Familiarity with illustration or 3D design a plus. Strong understanding of designing for mobile and social platforms. Ability to write short-form, platform‑native social copy. Organized, detail‑oriented, and able to handle multiple projects at once. Comfortable capturing content or editing on mobile devices when needed. Familiar with on-set etiquette. Specializes in working in facilities that manufacture a finished product for sale, or sale to another organization for use in an end product. Performs microbial control cleaning procedures that must comply with current Good Manufacturing Practices (cGMP) and regulatory guidelines which include documentation of work procedures frequently audited by the FDA and other regulatory agencies. The work will be accomplished under the general supervision of Lead Personnel and an area Supervisor. Responsibilities Performs cross contamination cleaning methods in areas that require microbial control. Completes cGMP documentation of training or cleaning performed on paper and electronic devices. Prepares cleaning solutions based on cGMP regulated mixing instructions. Performs microbial control cleaning techniques on walls, ceiling and floors based on cGMP regulated cleaning frequencies. Completes preventive maintenance work orders to meet cGMP cleaning requirements. Follows specific gowning procedures and performs cGMP entrance and exit procedures for controlled environments. Operates bailing and compacting equipment. Operates various types of hand held battery and electric cleaning equipment. Operates various types of battery and electric walk behind or ride-on floor cleaning equipment. Performs safety and preventive maintenance inspections on housekeeping power equipment and small tools and wears approved PPE. High School Diploma or equivalent. Must be able to read and comprehend written information to include Corporate Quality Documents, Divisional Operating Procedures, Departmental Operating Procedures and Safety Guidelines. Must be able to comply with cGMP, regulatory guidelines and able to write legibility in English and complete accurate and legible written records in compliance with cGMP when documenting work performed, on paper documents and electronic devices auditable by regulatory agencies. Must be able to operate a computer to complete required compliance & technical training. Must have the ability to learn and perform cleaning techniques to meet regulatory requirements. Must have the ability to work alone or as a team member sharing responsibility and work tasks. Must be able to perform all cleaning specialist job functions. Basic physical requirements are but are not limited to: stand for 7 hours per shift, regularly lift 35 pounds 50 times per shift, occasionally lift 50 pounds 6 times per shift, walk approximately 2000 feet per hour, climb 6 flights of stairs per shift, work on knees 30 minutes per shift, bend / Squat 200 times per shift, rotate left / right 200 times per shift.
