Your Day at Lowe's As a Customer Service Associate, you will welcome customers to Lowe's and help them find the right products and services for their home improvement needs. You will interact with customers throughout the day, help them find and select products, occasionally load merchandise, and ensure all customer needs are met. While you will spend most of your time listening to customers, answering questions, and organizing merchandise, your daily responsibilities may vary by department. Customer Service Associates work in one of the following departments, based on hiring needs and skillsets: Appliances, Cabinets, Flooring, Live Nursery, Inside Garden, Hardware, Tools, Millwork, Building Materials, Plumbing, Electrical, Paint, Home Décor, Tool Rental, or Pro Services. Key Responsibilities Welcome customers to Lowe's, answer questions, and deliver friendly and professional customer service. Assist customers with locating and handling merchandise Down stock merchandise by looking for empty areas on shelves and replenishing supplies Process orders and deliveries accurately so customers receive merchandise as expected and on time Cross-functionally train in other areas of the store to help deliver the best customer service Prepare merchandise in your department based on customer needs (e.g., tint and mix paint, cut and thread pipe, cut and bundle wood, cut drywall, cut blinds) Guide customers through shopping or checkout Complete other duties as assigned Minimum Qualifications 6 Months Experience using a computer, including inputting, accessing, modifying, or outputting information 6 Months Experience using common retail technology, such as smart phones and tablets Reading, writing, and performing basic arithmetic (addition and subtraction) Able to perform duties that may require prolonged standing, sitting, and other activities necessary to perform job duties Minimally lift 25lbs unassisted or over 25lbs with or without an accommodation Preferred Qualifications 6 months of Retail and/or customer service experience Bi-lingual skills Certification in trade related to department (e.g., hardware, kitchen, plumbing, electrical, lawn and garden, and lumber/building materials) Lowe's commitment to growth and teamwork extends to the community as well. To better equip our stores and serve our communities, we strongly encourage bilingual, military, and veteran talent to apply and join our team. Travel Requirements This role does not require regular travel; however, this role may need to travel occasionally to meetings, training, or to support neighboring stores. Working Conditions Environmental factors vary by location. You may be working in both inside and outside weather conditions. Exposure to varying climates, including extreme heat or cold, wet, damp, humid, windy, or drafty conditions, is possible. You may be exposed to constant or intermittent noises in addition to moving or shaking objects and equipment. Lifting methods vary based on role, weight, and volume. Associates must follow guidelines, limiting single lifts to 75 pounds. Team lifts are used minimally starting at 75 pounds or when needed. Powered equipment should be used as required, with proper training or assistance from a trained coworker. About Lowe’s Lowe’s Companies, Inc. Global Labor Agency Contracting Category Strategist Description - Are you a dynamic, forward-thinking strategist with deep expertise in procurement, negotiations, and business transformation? Do you thrive in environments where you can influence at the executive level, shape sourcing strategies, and drive cost optimization across global operations? If so, this is your opportunity to lead, innovate, and make a lasting impact at HP! The Global Labor Agency Contracting (GLAC) Strategist opportunity involves conducting comprehensive data and industry analysis to support data-driven decision-making. The qualified candidate will utilize supply chain, business, and financial modeling tools to optimize the supply base. Moreover, the GLAC strategist opportunity involves innovating complex business models, driving strategies, and identifying areas for continuous improvement and risk mitigation. Role Overview As a senior individual contributor in the Indirect Procurement organization, you will: Architect and lead high-impact GLAC strategies that align with HP’s business objectives. Influence and engage with executive stakeholders to drive strategic sourcing decisions and optimize cost structures across HP’s business units. Serve as a senior negotiator in high-visibility supplier engagements, securing competitive advantages and fostering innovation. Partner cross-functionally with legal, finance, operations, and global category management teams to enable seamless and compliant execution. Analyze market trends and business intelligence to inform long-term sourcing strategies and uncover areas for growth, efficiency, and risk mitigation. Why HP? At HP, you’ll work with passionate, results-driven teams to deliver exceptional business outcomes. We foster innovation, empower bold thinkers, and create growth opportunities. Join us to help shape the future of procurement at one of the world’s most iconic companies. Key Responsibilities Strategic Category Leadership: Develop, lead, and refine strategies for the Agency Contracting category to support HP’s cost transformation and operational excellence goals. Drive initiatives that enable end-to-end value delivery through strategic sourcing, supply base optimization, and innovative supplier partnerships. Executive-Level Influence & Business Consulting: Establish trusted advisor relationships with senior and executive stakeholders. Leverage deep industry and business knowledge to challenge assumptions and co-create impactful solutions that support business objectives. High Spend Negotiation & Contracting: Lead complex negotiations with critical suppliers, securing favorable terms and enabling innovation, service excellence, and long-term value. Utilize advanced negotiation techniques and business acumen to influence commercial outcomes and mitigate risk. Cross-Functional Collaboration: Drive the synergies in working across key internal functions (Legal, Finance, Business Unit, Operations). Ensure alignment and compliance while enabling fast, agile decision-making. Supplier Innovation & Relationship Management: Develop strategic supplier relationships to foster co-innovation and continuous improvement. Partner with suppliers to explore new capabilities, technologies, and efficiencies. Market Intelligence & Analytics: Lead in-depth spend, supplier, and market analysis to inform strategic direction. Translate complex data into executive-level insights and recommendations to influence business decisions. Mentorship & Development: Coach and guide other category managers, supporting capability development in negotiation, strategy building, and stakeholder engagement. Education and Experience Required Bachelor’s degree required; MBA or Master’s in Supply Chain Management or related field preferred. 10+ years of progressive experience in procurement, consulting, or strategic sourcing, ideally in a global environment. Background in sales or consulting is strongly preferred Preferred Certifications Project Management Professional (PMP) Lean Six Sigma C.P.M., CPSM, CPSD, CPCM, CCCM, CSCP, CPIM, CLTD, or other related certifications Knowledge & Skills Strong knowledge of indirect categories such as Labor Agency Contracting & Freelancer Program Expert-level negotiation and business strategy capabilities Proven ability to influence and consult with executives and senior stakeholders Ability to provide innovative solutions to complex issues Deep knowledge of supply chain, financial modeling, and business strategy tools Exceptional communication, analytical thinking, and problem-solving skills Experience managing complex supplier ecosystems and delivering transformational outcomes AI Fluency Cross-Org Skills Excellent communication and influencing abilities, including at an executive level Strong analytical and data analysis skills An ability to lead cross-functional teams effectively and drive strategic initiatives Strong mentoring and leadership skills Proactive in identifying areas for improvement and risk mitigation Results Orientation Learning Agility Digital Fluency Customer Centricity Working Conditions Global role with support across multiple time zones. Occasional travel for supplier meetings, governance reviews, and leadership summits. Hybrid role – on-site 3 days/week. Impact & Scope Impacts large functions and leads large, cross-divisional functional teams or projects. Complexity Provides highly innovative solutions to complex problems within established policy. Job Function: Pharmaceutical Sales Job Sub Function: Sales – Immunology (Commission) Job Category: Professional All Job Posting Locations: Charlottesville, Virginia, United States Job Description: Johnson & Johnson Innovative Medicine is recruiting for an Immunology Sales Specialist - Gastroenterology to support clients in the Charlottesville VA region. About Immunology Our expertise in Innovative Medicine is informed and inspired by patients, whose insights fuel our science-based advancements. Visionaries like you work on teams that save lives by developing the medicines of tomorrow. Our Immunology team leads in the development of transformational medicines for immunological disorders and illnesses. You can influence where medicine is going by restoring health to millions of people living with immune diseases. Join us in developing treatments, finding cures, and pioneering the path from lab to life while championing patients every step of the way. Influence decision makers and influencers within assigned customers to support the use of the company's products in the treatment of relevant disease states by developing and applying clinical and business expertise, and effective selling skills. AbbVie’s Analytics and Performance Excellence (APEX) function is seeking a highly strategic, analytical, and collaborative Associate Director to provide analytics leadership for the Business Evolution Strategic Development (BESD) Team. This role will drive impactful business analytics and insights to help AbbVie anticipate and navigate evolving healthcare environments, especially focusing on market access and policy disruptors. The Associate Director will bridge Market Access and Patient Services (MAPS) Team within APEX and BESD (Business Evolution Strategic Development) team objectives by leading modelling, advanced insights and analytics supporting forward-looking strategies, enabling enterprise readiness, and shaping market access policies and outcomes for AbbVie’s diverse U.S. portfolio. This role requires a strong grasp of healthcare policy, payer analytics, and strategy formulation within a collaborative, cross-functional environment. Key Responsibilities: Lead the planning and execution of analytics to inform market access strategies, price reform and policy analysis, with actionable recommendations for AbbVie leadership. Identify payer opportunities/threats through deep dive analytics ('Follow the Dollar', claims analysis, and scenario modeling). Foster positive relationships and close collaboration with teams including Government Affairs, Finance, Legal, Corporate Affairs, Brand, and Market Access. Communicate complex findings and insight-driven narratives to senior leadership and cross-functional teams, enabling improved payer knowledge and strategic decision-making. Monitor external environment and translate emerging trends (political, regulatory, legislative, commercial) into strategic recommendations for AbbVie’s business evolution. Advise on analytics infrastructure enhancements to drive business impact. Skills Action and Accountability: Own responsibility for activities within relevant workstreams, and engage and inspire cross functional stakeholders to advance towards clear objectives and strategies; make quick, but informed decisions, as appropriate, to ensure best paths forward in the midst of change market and policy dynamics. Constantly engage, guide, and support cross-functional team to address roadblocks, challenges, resourcing constraints and other dynamics. Leadership and Influence: Influence and persuade across multiple external and internal stakeholders. Collaboration and Teamwork: Work effectively with internal stakeholders, external market experts and partners. Bachelor’s degree required; master’s degree (MBA or related business/science) preferred. 10+ years of progressive analytical/ insights experience in healthcare industry (pharma, consulting, government affairs, market access, public policy, etc.). 1-2 years pharmaceutical market access experience with deep understanding of Health Plans, PBMs, Hospitals, Specialty Pharmacies, and healthcare policy stakeholders. Strong insurance channel experience and understanding (i.e. Medicare, Commercial etc.) Strong business acumen, strategic and analytical thinking, and executive presence. Exceptional communication and influencing skills, with the ability to distill complex information into compelling, concise messages. Strong organizational skills, flexibility, attention to detail, and experience in collaborative, dynamic environments. Exceptional communications and executive presence, critical thinking and interpersonal skills, strong ability to influence without authority, the ability to speak and write persuasively and with clarity, strong organizational skills, flexibility, and adaptability to changing requirements, resourcefulness and creativity, strong attention to detail, a proven track record of being able to work drive towards deadlines and an ability to work collaboratively in a fluid organizational and external environment. Must be an individual who works well in a team environment and enjoys working in a collegial, collaborative and fun, yet highly demanding culture Preferred: Experience in policy shaping, price reform strategy, and enterprise-level stakeholder partnership. Proficiency with pharmaceutical data sources (formulary, claims).

AI.Accelerate Overview: Are you a technically curious and ambitious undergraduate student with a passion for Artificial Intelligence? ServiceNow invites you to explore our AI.Accelerate program where you can develop practical AI skills and gain hands-on experience in a dynamic, fast-paced, and immersive environment. This eight-week unpaid bootcamp is designed to provide a comprehensive introduction to the core concepts and techniques of AI, with a focus on practical application and real-world problem-solving. You'll learn from experienced instructors, work on challenging projects, and collaborate with a cohort of talented peers. Dates: June 15 – July 31, 2026 (Virtual) + Week 8—beginning of August (In Person) Location: Virtually via Zoom Duration: 4 hours a week (plus homework) What You'll Learn: Agentic AI Foundations: Understand what makes an AI system "agentic" — including autonomy, reasoning, and action-taking — and how LLMs are evolving from chat tools into decision-making agents. Agentic Design Patterns: Explore key architectural patterns including React, chain-of-thought, tool use, and memory, and understand the difference between single-agent and multi-agent systems and when to use each. Prompt Engineering: Learn techniques for writing reliable, production-grade prompts that drive consistent and predictable agent behavior at scale. Building Agents: Design agents that use tools, APIs, and external data sources, and learn how to structure agent memory — both short-term and long-term — for complex, multi-step tasks. Multi-Agent Orchestration: Build and manage multi-agent workflows where agents collaborate, delegate, and hand off tasks to accomplish goals that no single agent could complete alone. Evaluation Frameworks: Learn why evaluations are the most critical part of building AI systems and how to design frameworks that define what to measure and how to measure it effectively. AI Safety & Responsible Use: Understand real-world failure modes including hallucination, prompt injection, and behavioral drift, and learn how to build guardrails and safety checks into agentic pipelines. Capstone Project: Design, build, evaluate, and defend an AI agent from scratch — putting every concept from the program into practice and presenting your work to a panel of ServiceNow engineers and leaders. Innovative Learning Structure: A blend of lectures, hands-on laboratories, and collaborative projects fostering a cohort- based, hands on learning experience. The program concludes with an in-person experience where participants showcase their capstone project, explore career opportunities at ServiceNow, and connect with the broader engineering community. please note: this is an unpaid program and is not an internship To be successful in this role you: Have experience in leveraging or critically thinking about how to integrate AI into work processes, decision-making, or problem-solving. This may include using AI-powered tools, automating workflows, analyzing AI-driven insights, or exploring AI’s potential impact on the function or industry . Are an Undergraduate student majoring or minoring in Computer Science (CS), Computer Engineering (CE), or Data Analytics. or related field, with a graduation date no earlier than December 2027 Are experienced in Python programming. Are experienced with and/or have knowledge of fundamental AI concepts Have availability to attend the full duration of the boot camp from June 15, 2026 to July 31, 2026 and then available to participate onsite in the beginning of August Application Process: Interested candidates should apply by April 15, 2026 , to be considered. Applications are evaluated until the application deadline only; therefore, early submission is recommended as spots are limited! Please submit a resume, a cover letter, and any related project work or AI experience. In your cover letter please share: Why do you want to participate in this AI bootcamp? Where do you see AI helping you in the future?

The Associate Director provides statistical programming support for multiple clinical projects across multiple therapeutic areas, both through individual contribution and through the work of staff. The Associate Director provides training and performance management for staff. The Associate Director demonstrates leadership competencies, builds relationships, and promotes teamwork within the Statistical Programming organization and across functions. The Associate Director is accountable for ensuring statistical programming support is delivered across multiple therapeutic areas. The Associate Director makes key recommendations and decisions related to processes, standards, and resource management. The Associate Director is also responsible for staff management and development. Responsibilities: SAS Programming: Demonstrates a strong understanding of SAS programming concepts and techniques used in the pharmaceutical industry and applies that knowledge to resolve non-routine problems. Standards: Oversees the development and implementation of global company standards for output design and programming conventions and monitors regulatory guidance and industry best practices. CRFs and Database Definitions: Provides strategic guidance on CRF and database design and reviews global standards related to these deliverables. Derivation Programming, Submission Data Sets, and Programs: Interprets statistical analysis plans, develops analysis data set specifications, and oversees the development and implementation of global standards for derived data sets and submission programs. Cross-Functional Collaboration: Works collaboratively with stakeholders to manage priorities and resources across therapeutic areas. Demonstrates a solid understanding of drug development principles, anticipates risks, develops contingency and escalation plans, and contributes to cross-functional initiatives. Communication: Presents statistical programming concepts, risk assessments, and recommendations clearly and persuasively to statisticians, scientists, programmers, and non-scientists. Effectively leads meetings and presentations. Training and Mentoring: Provides guidance, training, and mentoring to staff to support development and ensure compliance with training requirements. Staff Management : Assigns responsibilities, defines scope, and reviews progress to ensure projects are delivered on time and with appropriate quality. Allocates resources to maintain the right balance of expertise across projects and collaborates with management to assess staffing needs. Sets high expectations, promotes open communication, and leads staff to meet organizational goals. Provides performance management for 4–10 statistical programmers. Minimum Qualifications: Degree in Statistics, Computer Science, or a related field 10+ years of statistical programming experience (with MS) OR 12+ years of statistical programming experience (with BS) Strong technical competence in SAS programming and macro development. Experience in pharmaceutical clinical trials. Experience with regulatory filings such as NDA, BLA, or other submissions, including ISS and ISE experience. Preferred Qualifications: Experience interacting with regulatory agencies, especially FDA and EMEA. Previous management experience. Other Required Skills: Working knowledge of ICH guidelines and relevant regulatory requirements. Strong oral and written communication skills.

The Delivery Operations Systems Administrator is responsible for the configuration, administration, and continuous optimization of the Workfront platform as the organization’s primary project execution tool. This individual also supports enhancements, integrations, documentation, and user enablement across multiple systems to ensure consistent, scalable, and compliant use of project operations tools. Manages Workfront roles, permissions, governance standards, and user provisioning. Ensures Workfront data integrity, process alignment, and compliance with PMO and operational frameworks. Designs and maintains Workfront reports and dashboards to support operational and executive visibility. Ensures alignment with their manager and the Enterprise Workfront Product Owner prior to initiating any largescale enhancements or system implementations. Ensures consistency and accuracy in project, task, and timetracking data. Supports audit and quality management reporting requirements. MultiPlatform Support & Enterprise Tool Administration Represents Workfront across the organization while collaborating with peer system owners to maintain and support a connected, interoperable enterprise tool landscape. Provides configuration support across other enterprise project systems, including Microsoft Dynamics 365, Project Operations, PowerBI, and/or related platforms. Supports setup, configuration, testing, documentation, and user enablement for new systems or modules as they are introduced. Contributes to crossplatform process alignment to maintain consistency in project lifecycle workflows. Systems Integration & Data Flow Alignment Supports integrations among Workfront, Dynamics 365, Project Operations, PowerBI, and/or enterprise data hubs. Partners with Operations, PMO, Finance, and Technology teams to maintain synchronization of project, task, time entry, and financial alignment workflows. Helps refine and document current state versus future state process flows as systems evolve. Governance, Optimization & Process Standards Participates in audits of system configuration, templates, custom fields, permissions, and licenses across platforms. Supports roadmap execution for Workfront cleanup, rationalization, and cross system consistency. Ensures documentation is current and standardized for Workfront and/or other project related systems. Promotes platform best practices and encourages consistent usage across teams. Issue Resolution, Change Management & Support Troubleshoots system issues, logs enhancements, and partners with technical teams to implement solutions. Supports training, release communications, and adoption across Workfront and other project systems. Facilitates sessions to address systemic blockers in project setup, reporting, or data consistency. CrossFunctional Collaboration Acts as a connector between PMO, Operations, Finance, Data & Analytics, and IT. Provides visibility into risks, dependencies, and upcoming system changes. Supports crossfunctional alignment for ongoing process improvements and system needs. All other duties as assigned. Bachelors of Sciences or Arts is required; equivalent experience considered. Experience with Microsoft Dynamics 365, PowerBI, or similar platforms. Strong understanding of project management methodologies, business process alignment, and cross‑functional operations. Experience supporting or administering integrated systems in a matrixed environment.

The AbbVie Process Chemistry Chromatographic Separations Lab is actively seeking an Associate Scientist II or Scientist I. Our team collaborates with colleagues across multiple disciplines, offering expertise in preparative chromatography to support a broad range of AbbVie R&D programs. We maintain and utilize specialized equipment for various separation tasks, including the purification of peptides, ADC drug-linkers, and chiral compounds, as well as the isolation of low-level API impurities. Additionally, the team is responsible for pilot-scale preparative purification, developing scalable purification processes, and overseeing their implementation under cGMP guidelines at AbbVie's North Chicago Chemical Pilot Plant. This role will contribute to the development of novel/advanced separations technologies and broader efforts to develop new process technologies for advancing the AbbVie pipeline. We are seeking a motivated scientist who demonstrates initiative and technical proficiency in supporting research and development projects within a collaborative team environment. The ideal candidate will have hands-on experience developing chromatographic methods and troubleshooting complex separation challenges. Experience working with peptides is highly desirable, but not required for application. Key Responsibilities: Develop and execute purification processes supporting development of small molecule, antibody drug conjugate, and peptide clinical candidates. Demonstrate scientific initiative and creativity in planning, executing, and troubleshooting experiments, resolving key project challenges with an appropriate level of autonomy based on experience. Conduct a range of laboratory and pilot-scale tasks, analyze and interpret data, and drive project objectives, assuming responsibility for tasks in accordance with experience. Suggest, adapt, and, as appropriate, implement new or improved experimental protocols/techniques, consulting relevant literature as needed. Build and maintain strong collaborative relationships with peers and cross-functional partners. Foster a learning environment, encourage diverse ideas, and support continuous process improvement. Understand and adhere strictly to corporate standards for conduct, safety, quality, and proper handling of materials. Bachelor’s degree with at least 3 years (Associate Scientist II) or 5 years (Scientist I) relevant experience; or Master’s degree with no additional experience (Associate Scientist II) or typically +2 years of relevant experience (Scientist I). Strong technical background in Separations Science, with theoretical and practical knowledge required to independently carry out job functions. Demonstrated proficiency in developing, troubleshooting, and modifying chromatographic methods and purification protocols. Broad expertise in analytical techniques, with emphasis on chromatography, compound purification, and spectral analysis. Ability to search scientific literature and evaluate potential solutions to research problems. Effective written and oral communication skills; able to work collaboratively in multidisciplinary teams.

At Visa, AI is central to our vision for the future of payments and commerce. We are committed to building enterprise-scale, responsible AI solutions that deliver measurable value for our clients, partners, and the global economy. The AI Center of Excellence (AI COE), part of the Global Data Office, is at the forefront of this mission—developing reusable AI/ML frameworks, enabling agentic AI workflows, and accelerating innovation across Visa’s data science community. The AI COE operates as both an enterprise capability builder and an AI SWAT team, tackling high-impact projects that address complex business challenges and create scalable, reusable solutions. From evaluating cutting-edge AI methods to deploying reusable frameworks in production, our mission is to improve efficiency, adoption, and business outcomes across Visa’s global Data & AI ecosystem. We are seeking an AI COE Analyst to contribute to technically complex AI initiatives—from research and prototyping through deployment—while advancing reusable AI capabilities and accelerating adoption across Visa. The AI COE Analyst will: Design, develop, and deploy advanced AI/ML methods and agentic AI workflows that address high-value challenges across Visa. Contribute to the creation of reusable AI frameworks, components, and internal open-source assets for enterprise-wide adoption. Evaluate emerging AI/ML techniques, benchmark performance, and validate business impact using real Visa datasets and use cases. Support the end-to-end delivery of AI COE projects, including: Identifying and refining problem statements with stakeholders Prototyping advanced models, pipelines, and automation workflows Building high-quality, reusable code assets Ensuring production readiness and integration with enterprise systems Develop technical documentation, metadata, and best practices for validated AI methods. Contribute to quality assurance through code reviews, prompt engineering support, model evaluation frameworks, and benchmark design. Ensure compliance with governance, security, and Responsible AI standards in all AI COE outputs. Quantify and communicate impact using KPIs such as model accuracy, workflow efficiency gains, adoption metrics, and business value delivered. Collaborate with data scientists, ML engineers, product teams, and global partners to embed AI COE solutions into enterprise workflows and maximize adoption. Stay current on the latest AI frameworks, agentic AI patterns, and LLM ecosystems, rapidly evaluating and prototyping new methods for potential enterprise use. This is a hybrid position. Expectation of days in office will be confirmed by your hiring manager. Basic Qualifications: 2 or more years of work experience with a Bachelor’s Degree or an Advanced Degree (e.g. Masters, MBA, JD, MD, or PhD) Preferred Qualifications: 3 or more years of work experience with a Bachelor’s Degree or more than 2 years of work experience with an Advanced Degree (e.g. Masters, MBA, JD, MD) 2+ years of hands-on experience in AI/ML, data science, workflow automation, or applied machine learning research. Advanced degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Statistics, Business Analytics, Engineering, or a related quantitative field. Demonstrated experience delivering AI/ML models or agentic AI workflows in production or enterprise environments. Hands-on expertise with PyTorch, TensorFlow, scikit-learn, Hugging Face Transformers, or similar frameworks. Experience with agentic AI tooling (e.g., LangChain, LlamaIndex) and multi-step workflow automation. Strong data engineering foundations, including Python, SQL, Spark, Databricks, Airflow, Kafka, or ETL/ELT pipelines. Familiarity with enterprise data systems, APIs, and MLOps (CI/CD, model monitoring, containerization). Ability to translate complex AI concepts into clear, actionable insights for technical and non-technical stakeholders. Understanding of AI governance, model evaluation, and Responsible AI practices. Experience working cross-functionally in a large, global organization.

The Center for Global Security Research (CGSR) was established at Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL) in 1996 to bring together experts from the science, technology, and policy communities to address pressing national security challenges. For over 20 years, CGSR has engaged diverse perspectives on topics important to national security, deterrence, diplomacy, dual-use technology, arms control, nonproliferation, space, cyber, biosecurity, and energy security. We have openings in Fall 2026 for undergraduate students to engage in practical research on global security topics. Students will work with CGSR over the duration of three to four months as a research associate (RA). RAs will engage in practical research to further their educational and career goals, while also supporting the development of strategies for national security and LLNL’s mission focus areas. Examples of relevant fields of research include nuclear deterrence, arms control, nonproliferation, emerging technologies, cybersecurity, space, biological & chemical security, and energy security. CGSR’s objectives are as follows: To explore the dynamics of potential 21st century strategic conflicts (i.e., those with a potential nuclear aspect) and to formulate ideas about how to achieve U.S. deterrence and other objectives in such conflicts. To explore the sources and characteristics of strategic competition in the emerging security environment and to formulate organizing concepts to enhance the competitive position of the United States and its allies and partners over the long term. To identify whether and how technically based approaches can address new challenges to national and international security. To catalyze broader national and international thinking about the requirements of effective deterrence, assurance, and strategic stability in a changed and changing security environment. To assist in the development of new generations of experts motivated by a clear view of the changed and changing security environment. More information on CGSR, its research focus areas, and its publications can be found at https://cgsr.llnl.gov/ . This job will be closed to applicants on May 31, 2026. You will Conduct an independent research project on an agreed upon topic aligned with CGSR/LLNL research priorities under the supervision of CGSR staff. Support CGSR/LLNL through contributions to ongoing research activities. Tasks may include contributing to literature reviews, annotated bibliographies, and workshop summary reports. Attend relevant research seminars, speakers’ series, and workshops. Present research to LLNL staff at end of the assignment. Prepare end-of-assignment technical report or publication. Perform all assignments in accordance with ES&H, security, and business practice requirements and policies. Perform other duties as assigned. Must be eligible to access the Laboratory in compliance with Section 3112 of the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA). See Additional Information section below for details. Must be currently enrolled in an accredited university or have completed AA/AS degree in a field of research aligned with CGSR analytic priorities. Areas of study include international relations and/or security, political science, economics, public policy, emerging technologies, nonproliferation, energy, biosecurity, foreign language studies, or related fields. Demonstrated academic and/or professional achievement in a relevant field of research aligned with CGSR analytic priorities. Strong record of independent research and publication, or a strong proposal of research to be done while at CGSR and in future academic and professional settings. Ability to work in a team environment. Pay Range $23.26 - $31.62 Hourly This position is under a step structure. Please note that the step is determined by your academic level. Transcripts are required.

We have an opening for a Cloud Operations Engineer to join our team. In this position, you will be responsible for designing, implementing, and managing cloud solutions that support the National Nuclear Security Administration’s (NNSA) business services and programmatic missions, including scientific research and mission-critical operations. This position is in the Enterprise Infrastructure Services (EIS) Division within the Computing Directorate. You will work closely with multidisciplinary teams to drive innovation, improve scalability, and ensure the secure and efficient utilization of cloud resources for NNSA initiatives. This role supports multiple sites across the country and occasional travel is required to collaborate with stakeholders and partners. This position offers the opportunity to work in a dynamic and highly technical environment, supporting critical infrastructure for enterprise-level applications. This position requires full-time on-site presence due to the nature of the work. This position will be filled at either the SES.2 or SES.3 level based on knowledge and related experience as assessed by the hiring team. In this role you will Deploy and manage cloud infrastructure (primarily AWS) in support of scientific, engineering, and business applications. Develop automation scripts and Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) solutions for cloud resource provisioning and management. Collaborate with researchers, engineers, and IT staff to migrate workloads and optimize applications for cloud environments. Implement and manage cloud financial operations (FinOps) practices to optimize cloud spending, track usage, and collaborate with stakeholders to ensure cost-effective resource allocation. Monitor cloud performance and usage, and implement solutions for high availability, scalability, and cost efficiency. Ensure compliance with Department of Energy (DOE) and NNSA security policies and federal regulations for cloud operations. Provide technical support, documentation, and training for cloud users across the enterprise. Stay abreast of emerging cloud technologies and recommend adoption of innovative solutions. Perform other duties as assigned. Independently configure and utilize systems and cloud management tools to monitor, maintain, and optimize infrastructure operations effectively. Broad experience in cloud platform administration and support, with proficiency in technologies such as AWS, Azure, Google Cloud Platform, or hybrid cloud environments. Broad knowledge of cloud infrastructure operations, including resource provisioning, automation, and the use of infrastructure management tools. Proficient understanding of cloud support systems, such as virtual networking, identity and access management, and monitoring solutions. Comprehensive experience with cloud architecture documentation tools, including Visio and other office productivity software. Proficient in managing and troubleshooting cloud-based resources and services, including performance monitoring and incident response. Strong interpersonal, verbal, and written communication skills, with the ability to work independently while effectively collaborating with customers and team members. Advanced knowledge of troubleshooting techniques, with strong skills in resolving issues through analysis of logs, metrics, and cloud-native diagnostic tools. Significant experience training and mentoring team members, focusing on cloud engineering best practices and architectural design principles. AWS Certified Solutions Architect credential or an equivalent advanced cloud certification. This is a remote position with up to 50% domestic travel required. Candidates may reside in any state within the United States and should expect frequent national travel. The AbbVie Employer NAE is responsible for supporting and implementing strategic business initiatives in response to the changing healthcare environment, deployed specifically to national Employer Stakeholders via the AbbVie Employer Team with a focus on improving workforce health and productivity and maximizing strategic access to AbbVie’s therapies. The Employer NAE will be accountable for building effective stakeholder strategies and engagements that are on the forefront of emerging concerns impacting employee access, affordability, disease state awareness/management and medication value and access. This includes healthcare decision-makers (HCDMs) within national employer plan sponsors, employee benefit consultants (EBCs), and employer coalitions, as well as emerging stakeholders/influencers/vendors, national organizations, and professional/advocacy organizations. The Employer NAE provides branded and unbranded messaging to employers and employer influencers/KOLs regarding the value and differentiation of AbbVie therapies to accelerate access to treatment and the use of benefit plan designs to identify and minimize barriers to affordable and predictable Rx access. The NAE also delivers messaging relating to disease state and burden of illness to increase the awareness of treatment solutions and explore solutions and develop best practices/case studies. The Employer NAE will provide leadership to distinguish AbbVie in the employer channel, be a convener of stakeholders and regional/national KOLs and SMEs, and provide strategic insights internally in support of evolving business needs to ensure timely awareness of market changes and trends and inform internal business leads to ensure a rapid response to external disruptors and Rx management strategies which impact affordable access to AbbVie’s therapies. This role is highly collaborative and consultative and requires partnering and interfacing with numerous cross-functional teams (Market Access leadership, Payer Strategy and Cross Portfolio Strategy and Pipeline, Training, Market Analytics Business Insights, Business Evolution Strategy Development (BESD), Brand Sales/Marketing, Government Affairs and Policy, Corporate Strategy, US Medical Affairs/Value & Access and Medical Outcomes Science & Science Liaisons (MOSLs); Finance, Legal, Compliance, Communications/PR, Field Reimbursement Leadership, Brand Sales/Marketing teams and internal Centers of Excellence (CoE). The NAE must demonstrate the ability to anticipate and act proactively and effectively in uncertain situations. Additionally, the NAE requires significant collaboration with the Corporate Accounts KAM teams, providing timely insights regarding evolving contracting trends and evolving rebate models, educating client-facing teams, and providing updates regarding downstream employer clients and formulary initiatives. This position does not have direct reports but does require the ability to manage and lead without authority across cross-functional teams while also being able to work independently and productively. The Employer NAE is the lead for regional employer initiatives working in conjunction with the Regional Account Executive (RAE) teams and Regional Directors, as well as compliant collaboration with the Population Heath Account Executive (PHAE) team. This includes identifying opportunities and/or employer access issues and training/educating and executing on use of Employer Team resources and messaging to health plan, health system, PBM and employer customers. This role also is a key collaborator with other national field-based teams including the Field Reimbursement team, educating team members on market disruptors and problem-solving on employer-focused access issues. The Employer NAE serves as a key role in cataloguing key disruptors and potential patient disruption and analyzing potential financial (Gross to Net) impact, as well as working across internal stakeholders to develop and execute mitigation strategies. Major Duties and Responsibilities: Proactively engage with existing employer stakeholders and identify/influence emerging employer stakeholders across the US. Identify insights, positions and potential impact of new and emerging employer stakeholders and vendors. Build proactive share of voice with employer customers and influencers on Rx management topics. Support and contribute to internal Strategy Teams regarding emerging strategies and identification of external SMEs. Collaborate with Government Affairs/Policy/Strategy Directors to connect and convene with new and emerging stakeholders and advocates. Work in conjunction with Employer Team Director and Marketing Director (and collaboratively with Principal National MOSL, Employer Channel) relative to employer channel resource development and messaging. Develop and deliver stakeholder appropriate resources to support access for the expanding AbbVie portfolio (DSA decks, case studies, condensed employer value-prop decks, case studies and benefit plan design resources) Cultivate national employer KOLs and advocates to help shape external education and policy in collaboration with Government Affairs/Policy/Strategy teams. Monitor, inform and deliver market insights to internal business partners. Lead education initiatives in conjunction with Market Access Training on key trends impacting purchasers and AbbVie access/gross-to-net. Establish AbbVie as credible source for non-branded information and disseminate via industry meetings and electronic sites / social media (consistent with AbbVie Communications/PR guidelines). Support efforts to integrate Employer Strategy into AbbVie Business Planning process. Assist AbbVie Employer Corporate Account Team Leader with managing budget and execution of sponsorships and memberships, consistent with AbbVie Office of Ethics and Compliance (OEC) guidelines. Establish AbbVie as a national leader and key partner in the employer channel. Work with Big 3 PBM/GPO KAM teams and respective rebate analysts to ensure contract compliance. Quantify volume/sales associated with employer child accounts and access changes. Participate in internal task forces relating to member/patient access. Bachelor’s degree in Business, Life Sciences, or a related field required. Minimum of 5 years of Account Executive or Market Access experience within the healthcare industry; employee benefits consulting (EBC) experience and/or PBM experience is a plus. Proven ability to operate effectively in large, complex geographies, influence diverse stakeholders, and deliver commercial results. Demonstrated capability in negotiation, stakeholder engagement, and strategic planning/development and execution. Strong analytical skills, especially related to Rx contract terms/language and the commercial payor market. Effective communication and presentation skills (written and oral) with both technical and non-technical audiences. Experience managing complexity and collaborating with cross-functional, matrixed teams; agility and team-orientation required. Customer-centric approach and proven ability to act as primary point of contact for internal and external stakeholders. Ability to work autonomously, manage ambiguity, and identify/influence key customers. Understanding of the evolving healthcare environment—including ACA, CAA, ERISA, clinical guidelines, and formulary/utilization management. Adept at delivering product and disease state value proposition materials to a range of customers. Highest ethical standards and compliance with AbbVie Office of Ethics and Compliance (OEC) policies. Significant domestic travel required (up to 50%) for customer interactions, industry meetings and internal meetings. An essential requirement of your position is to satisfy all applicable health care industry representative (HCIR) credentialing requirements to gain and maintain entry into facilities and organizations that are in your assigned territory. You must also be in good standing and/or eligible to obtain these credentials. Driving a personal auto or company car or truck, or a powered piece of material handling equipment. Valid driver’s license: Ability to pass a pre-employment drug screening test and meet safe driving requirements. Preferred: 10+ years’ experience in pharmaceutical, Rx supply chain, employee benefit consulting, or healthcare organization. Deep understanding of commercial business models and payor markets.

This role is highly collaborative and consultative and requires partnering and interfacing with numerous cross-functional teams (Market Access leadership, Payer Strategy and Cross Portfolio Strategy and Pipeline, Training, Market Analytics Business Insights, Business Evolution Strategy Development (BESD), Brand Sales/Marketing, Government Affairs and Policy, Corporate Strategy, US Medical Affairs/Value & Access and Medical Outcomes Science & Science Liaisons (MOSLs); Finance, Legal, Compliance, Communications/PR, Field Reimbursement Leadership, Brand Sales/Marketing teams and internal Centers of Excellence (CoE). The NAE must demonstrate the ability to anticipate and act proactively and effectively in uncertain situations. Additionally, the NAE requires significant collaboration with the Corporate Accounts KAM teams, providing timely insights regarding evolving contracting trends and evolving rebate models, educating client-facing teams, and providing updates regarding downstream employer clients and formulary initiatives. This position does not have direct reports but does require the ability to manage and lead without authority across cross-functional teams while also being able to work independently and productively. This role also is a key collaborator with other national field-based teams including the Field Reimbursement team, educating team members on market disruptors and problem-solving on employer-focused access issues. The Employer NAE serves as a key role in cataloguing key disruptors and potential patient disruption and analyzing potential financial (Gross to Net) impact, as well as working across internal stakeholders to develop and execute mitigation strategies. Support and contribute to internal Strategy Teams regarding emerging strategies and identification of external SMEs. Strong analytical skills, especially related to Rx contract terms/language and the commercial payor market. Preferred: 10+ years’ experience in pharmaceutical, Rx supply chain, employee benefit consulting, or healthcare organization. Deep understanding of commercial business models and payor markets.

Position Summary Machine/grind parts/tools to conform to blueprints/drawings Duties and responsibilities The following reflects management’s definition of essential functions for this job but does not restrict the tasks that may be assigned. We have an opening for a Software Engineer to support the Collaborative Authorization for the Safety-basis Total Lifecycle Environment (CASTLE-PX) Project. CASTLE-PX is Risk Level 2 Safety Software, requiring a high-level of rigor to maintain SQA compliance. CASTLE-PX is a web-based, custom Java application deployed at Pantex and is being used to manage the safety-bases for weapon systems, site facilities, as well as several business processes. Working with a dynamic multi-disciplinary team of software developers, software quality engineers, and IT staff, your primary responsibilities will be to contribute to the application development, perform production support, test new releases, and help maintain the large volume of SQA support documents. This position is in the Applications, Simulations, and Quality (ASQ) Division within the Computing Directorate, in support of the CASTLE Project within the Weapon Technologies Engineering (WTE) Program. This position offers a hybrid schedule, blending in-person and virtual presence. You may have the flexibility to work from home a maximum of 2 days per week. In this role, you will Conduct technical tasks within design, implementation, deployment, and maintenance for a web-based software system using object-oriented analysis, design, and programming techniques. Participate in the requirements definition, analysis, design, implementation, debugging, testing, and optimization of the software system. Communicate regularly with stakeholders regarding status, needs, progress, and upcoming plans. May provide leadership and support to the Application team while engaging in continuous improvement across end-to-end processes. Collaborate with a large, cross-site, multi-disciplinary team of managers, engineers, and developers to define the project’s current priorities and future direction. Contribute to the development and maintenance of Software Quality Assurance (SQA) documentation, while ensuring it is reviewed and updated as needed for each new production release. Provide advanced technical knowledge in the use of version control systems, including Git, and branch management. Ensure application compatibility and support complex application interactions in partnership with other software development teams. Provides solutions to complex problems that require in-depth analysis of tangible and intangible factors and the creative use of established and/or innovative methods. Perform other duties as assigned Ability to obtain and maintain a US DOE Q-level security clearance which requires U.S. Citizenship. Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or equivalent combination of education and relevant previous experience in a related technical field. Advanced experience in JavaScript, JSF and/or ORM frameworks. Advanced experience with Oracle databases including writing complex SQL scripts. Advanced knowledge and experience with web services, including REST. Demonstrated ability to manage multiple concurrent technical tasks, balance competing priorities, and meet deadlines critical to project success. Advanced level experience using software configuration management tools, preferably Atlassian Suite products such as JIRA and Confluence, with a strong emphasis on issue tracking. Advanced communication, facilitation, collaboration and interpersonal skills necessary to interact with all levels of personnel, collaborate effectively in a multi-disciplinary environment, present and explain technical information and provide advice to management. Qualifications We Desire Exceptional relationship building, collaboration and communication skills with a proven ability to translate customer requestions into clear system requirements. Expert knowledge of web services, such as REST, and XML data formats. Experience developing web application user-interfaces and user-experiences, with a strong understanding of best practices. Purpose The Associate Director, Category Management partners with VP-level business or functional stakeholder(s) to develop global procurement strategies, contributing to a cross-functional team that informs strategy through analysis, market expertise, and understanding of broader business objectives. This role builds an annual strategic plan and leads a team of managers to achieve ambitious performance targets aligned with organizational goals. Responsibilities Partner with VP-level business or functional stakeholders to develop global procurement strategies for an individual procurement category, acting as a Business Partner where necessary. Build a comprehensive annual strategic plan for the relevant category, incorporating category strategies that align with overall business goals. Contribute to a cross-functional team that informs strategic decision-making by leveraging market intelligence, staying abreast of industry trends, emerging technologies, and market dynamics. Define and develop strategic value drivers with key category suppliers to secure collaborative partnerships that challenge the status quo to achieve cost savings, optimize processes, and enhance overall procurement value. Integrate sustainability and environmental, social, and governance (ESG) measures into category strategies, collaborating with suppliers to enhance sustainable and responsible sourcing practices. Lead Supplier Relationship Management (SRM) strategies, driving innovation with key category suppliers and collaborating to enact creative and cutting-edge solutions that deliver on long-term business needs. Develop and activate mitigation strategies to proactively define and manage procurement risk across the relevant category, , ensuring compliance. Ensure effective project management from initiation to completion, directing and guiding cross-functional teams to deliver strategic category-related projects. Identify opportunities for process optimization and efficiency gains, leveraging data analytics to develop long-term continuous improvement programs that achieve strategic objectives. Drive the end-to-end procurement process from sourcing strategy to contract negotiation and execution, leading negotiations with key category suppliers and strengthening decisions with strong analytical insight and strategic perspective. Lead & coach a team of Managers, setting ambitious performance targets, providing tailored coaching, and evaluating team performance. Assist in planning to address skillsets, workforce requirements, capability needs, and long-term organizational staffing goals. Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Supply Chain Mgmt or related field. Master’s degree is preferred Minimum of 10 years of experience in procurement, supply chain, or related business or operations function. Previous experience leading category teams, partnering with major suppliers, and reporting to senior leaders. Strong proficiency in developing high-impact executive-level deliverables. Knowledge of the pharmaceutical industry is strongly preferred. Comprehensive expertise in category management, including market analysis, cost and financial assessment, ensuring strategic and informed procurement decisions. Fluency in negotiation and bidding, adept in overseeing complex projects with a focus on effective change management. Strong capabilities in internal stakeholder management and influence, aligning procurement strategies with business needs and fostering collaborative supplier relationships. Strategic thinking and accountability, anticipating future trends, and taking responsibility for impactful procurement outcomes that challenge the status quo. Innovative problem-solving skills combined with a significant executive presence, enabling creative solutions and influential communication at all organizational levels. High cross-functional leadership abilities, conflict resolution skills, effectively navigating & harmonizing diverse team dynamics. Exceptional interpersonal skills and emotional intelligence, facilitating empathetic interactions, effective communication, and robust relationship-building across a matrixed organization. High resilience under pressure and autonomous work ethic, maintaining performance in challenging situations and making independent decisions.

The Muliplatform Producer works closely with correspondents to gather all editorial elements needed for stories, including social media newsgathering, research, securing interviews, and confirming information with government agencies and community organizations. The Producer must be able to manage multiple assignments simultaneously, adapt quickly to breaking news, and collaborate closely with editorial leadership and production teams. This role requires strong editorial judgment, the ability to work under tight deadlines, and a solid understanding of national and international news, including breaking news coverage. Responsibilities include requesting graphics and other visual elements that support storytelling and enhance the presentation of stories across platforms. The Multimedia Producer may also assist in writing scripts and editorial content for newscasts and digital coverage. This position requires a strong visual sense and the ability to identify compelling video, natural sound, and other elements that strengthen the narrative and overall impact of a story. In addition, the Multiplatform Producer is responsible for booking guests on a daily basis for linear, streaming, and digital platforms. The candidate must be able to work effectively in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment, including weekends, early mornings, and flexible hours to accommodate last-minute. The position requires the ability to work flexible hours, including nights, weekends, and holidays, particularly during breaking news coverage or special assignments. This position demands the ability to work effectively under tight deadlines within a fast-paced and evolving newsroom environment. Responsibilities: • Gather editorial elements needed for stories, including social media newsgathering, research, and securing interviews. • Contribute to the day’s editorial direction by pitching story ideas, exclusive reports, and interview opportunities. • Participate in breaking news coverage and special projects. • Demonstrate proficiency in using social media platforms for newsgathering, research, and content creation. • Maintain a well-established network of contacts, including community organizations, business leaders, federal and local officials, and other media outlets. • Work effectively in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment, including weekends, early mornings, and flexible hours to accommodate last-minute scheduling changes. • Operate under the guidance of the VP of News Gathering • This position is based on-site in Miami, Florida, and requires regular in-office presence to support newsroom operations. • Contribute to a collaborative, inclusive, and accountable newsroom culture. Basic Requirements: Bachelor’s degree in journalism, Communications, or equivalent professional experience. Minimum of 3 years of on-air news reporting experience in Spanish. Experience producing digital video content in a newsroom environment is a plus. Proficiency in social media platforms and trends. Fluent in Spanish, written and spoken. Fluent in English Desired Characteristics: Accustomed to working in a team and collaborating with all levels within the organization. Proven excellent interpersonal skills combined with a strong sense of how to visually tell a compelling story. Outside of the box thinker Proficient in I-News, helpful Additional Requirements: Interested candidate must submit a resume/CV through www.nbcunicareers.com to be considered (job #: ) Must be willing to work in the greater Miami, Florida area. Must be 18 years or older. Must have a valid driver’s license. Must have unrestricted work authorization to work in the United States Must be covered by Solutions, NBCU’s Alternative Dispute Resolution Program

THE POSITION: Medical Information is a critically important customer-facing function that supports the safe and effective use of pharmaceutical company products by providing timely, scientifically balanced, evidence based, nonpromotional information in response to unsolicited requests from healthcare professionals, patients, caregivers, and payers. Medical Information also plays an important role in post-marketing handling of adverse events and product complaints. As part of the Medical Information Contact Center (MICC) team, this position delivers industry-leading services, which include Contact Center staffing for responding to product information requests, identifying and handling of adverse events and/or product quality issues, and medical writing as needed to generate written response for use in response to medical questions received. This position requires clinical and therapeutic knowledge, critical and analytical thinking, and customer/patient-centric approach. Medical Information Specialists typically support multiple pharmaceutical clients, multiple products, and multiple therapeutic areas. ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES: Our employees are tasked with delivering excellent business results through the efforts of their teams. These results are achieved by: MEDICAL INFORMATION SUPPORT Respond to medical information inquiries from physicians, pharmacists, nurses, and other health care professionals, consumers, and payers. Utilize medical information skills to identify, research, and critically evaluate medical literature to create responses to medical information inquiries. Utilize writing skills for adverse event and product complaint narrative during intake as well as medical inquiry custom responses. Handle requests across multiple channels and platforms (phone, email, CRM, chat, etc.) Identify adverse events and product complaints during interactions with customers. Perform intake sufficient to generate adverse event and product complaint reports in compliance with EVERSANA-MICC and client standard operating procedures. Knowledge of FDA’s postmarketing adverse event reporting regulations and safety terminology. Ability to make accurate assessments regarding what information needs to be obtained and level or depth of information to be collected. Coordinate processes necessary for responding to product quality-related complaints. This process may involve interactions with personnel in the following departments: Quality Assurance, Regulatory Affairs, and the complainant. Maintain product, therapeutic area, and client specific requirements knowledge. Ensure good documentation, high quality, and excellent customer service. Medical writing and Medical Information content development. Provide medical writing to assist in drafting of Medical Information response documents [FAQs, Scientific Response Documents (SRDs), Custom Response Documents (CRDs)] and/or work collaboratively with medical writing team to develop these materials.  Staffing at scientific medical affairs booths. On-call responsibilities on an as assigned basis. Miscellaneous projects such as market and competitive product research, operational and process improvements, field team training and field liaison support.  All other duties as assigned. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of this position. EXPECT AT IONS OF THE JOB: Metrics: Maintain and contribute toward process improvement which positively impacts metrics associated with activities of the Medical Communications l Contact Center; metrics are subject to change annually or more often as deemed necessary. Customer Services: Maintain and improve customer services associated with activity of the Medical Communications Contact Center. Hours: Able to work full time and be flexible with work scheduling as required by clients and management. Travel: In general, this position does not travel; however, the incumbent will need to be able to travel up to 10%. We have an opening for a Field Technician to provide technical support and customer services in the management of hazardous and radioactive waste. Under general supervision you will perform a variety of technical functions in collecting, packaging, labeling, identifying, documenting, segregating, consolidating, treating, and storing hazardous, explosive and radioactive waste generated by various LLNL programs. This position is in the Radioactive and Hazardous Waste Management (RHWM) Program and part of the Special Project Group supporting Site 200 within the Strategic Deterrence Directorate. This position requires full-time on-site presence due to the nature of the work. This position will be filled at either level based on knowledge and related experience as assessed by the hiring team. Additional job responsibilities (outlined below) will be assigned if hired at the higher level. In this role you will Perform a wide variety of waste management activities, often wearing personal protective equipment (PPE) such as anti-C’s, respirator, hearing protection, etc., to collect, package, label, identify, segregate, consolidate, treat, store, and verify hazardous, low level radioactive, mixed and/or transuranic waste. Operate wastewater retention tanks and/or systems, perform pump-outs, perform lab packing of waste chemicals and manage waste container storage areas. Perform field testing (pH, visual etc.) and sampling of waste to verify characterization and/or treatment results and operate radiation survey instruments to obtain radiological data. Operate a variety of vehicles up to and including 5-ton trucks, use material handling equipment (fork trucks, drum handling equipment, mechanical pump systems, etc.), and use hand and power tools. Respond to environmental emergencies at LLNL and work with cross-organizational personnel performing decontamination of facility infrastructure and equipment. Gather, analyze, and record basic pertinent data and maintain detailed and accurate records associated with radioactive and hazardous waste to properly characterize and manage the waste. Complete and maintain training requirements per Federal, State, and LLNL requirements. Provide high-end customer service with a wide range of waste generators as the front-line interface between RHWM and waste generators. Support various scope Decontamination and Demolition (D&D) projects on behalf of LLNL. Perform all assignments in accordance with ES&H, security, and business practice requirements and policies. Perform other duties as assigned. Additional job responsibilities at the 504.3 Level Solve difficult radioactive and hazardous waste management problems using established guidelines and routine techniques and procedures. Plan and execute waste management projects including directing the activities of other technicians. Conduct On-the-Job-Training and provide mentoring and leadership for less experienced technicians. Act as Responsible Individual (RI) on Work Control Documents. Ability to secure and maintain a U.S. DOE Q-level security clearance which requires U.S. citizenship. Associate degree in environmental or related scientific field, or equivalent combination of education and experience. Intermediate knowledge of State and Federal regulations as they apply to hazardous and radioactive waste management, with emphasis on managing waste in satellite accumulation areas (SAAs) and 90-day consolidated accumulation areas (CAAs) or experience working within nuclear or high-hazard facilities. Intermediate knowledge of field instrumentation, such as radiation survey instruments, pH meters, etc., with an emphasis on their application to radioactive and hazardous waste processes. Elementary understanding of chemistry principles, including compatibility, and/or general understanding of radioactive contamination control methods. Ability to meet medical qualification to wear respiratory protection equipment, climb ladders and meet other physical requirements specified in the job demands worksheet and to successfully complete all Federal, State, LLNL and Department of Transportation (DOT) training requirements. Effective communication and interpersonal skills in order to build and maintain working relationships with coworkers, waste generators, programmatic support personnel and management. Strong organizational skills with the ability to generate and maintain high-quality, accurate records and correspondence using PC and/or Apple workstations and associated applications. Effective customer service skills needed to provide waste management support to a wide range of waste generators. Additional qualifications at the 504.3 Level Experience managing projects with minimal direction needed. High level understanding and knowledge of State and Federal regulations (RCRA, DOE, DOT) applicable to waste management, with demonstrated experience in their application or extensive experience working within nuclear facilities with a proven track record of accomplishing tasks while following strict controls. Experience with contaminated facility D&D. Experience providing training and mentoring to less experienced personnel. Pay Range $43.55 - $63.97 Hourly $43.55 - $53.36 Hourly for the 504.2 level $52.23 - $63.97 Hourly for the 504.3 level This is the lowest to highest salary we in good faith believe we would pay for this role at the time of this posting. An employee’s position within the salary range will be based on several factors including, but not limited to, specific competencies, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, seniority, geographic location, performance, and business or organizational needs.

We have an opening for a Document Compliance Coordinator to navigate a complex matrix of federal, institutional and organizational requirements. You will collaborate with engineers and subject matter experts to initiate, develop, document and evaluate comprehensive technical procedures, documents and safety plans. This position will support the Superblock (SBK) facility within the Strategic Deterrence Directorate. This position may offer a hybrid schedule, which includes the flexibility to work from home one or more days per week, after a probationary period. The specifics of the hybrid schedule, including the exact number of days required in the office and virtual work options, may vary based on the needs of the team and the organization. This position will be filled at either level based on knowledge and related experience as assessed by the hiring team. Additional job responsibilities (outlined below) will be assigned if hired at the higher level. In this role you will Analyze and implement documentation processes, procedures, and practices to ensure activities within the facility are performed in compliance with requirements in federal regulations, institutional procedures, and the nuclear facility safety bases. Evaluate procedures and process documents to verify facility requirements are adequately implemented, controls identified in the safety basis documents are maintained, and technical and management reviews are conducted. Serve as a contact for SBK processes, procedures, practices, manuals, guidance documents and safety plans and provide guidance to others related to SBK administrative procedures associated with document compliance. Collaborate with subject matter experts to initiate, develop, review, revise, implement and evaluate documentation that impact SBK facilities and systems, as well as LLNL programs. Monitor document tracking and routing, and ensure revision control using electronic applications (e.g., Enterprise Lifecycle Management-Unclassified [ELM-U]/Windchill) for configuration management of documents. Assist in planning, coordinating, and conducting periodic assessments to determine conformance with regulations, LLNL requirements, and SBK plans and procedures, including management self-assessments, observations and inspections, relating to SBK processes and other operational activities; recommend and coordinate completion of corrective action plans related to deficiencies. Manage technical information communications and interface with the LLNL programs and facilities personnel related to facility procedures; solicit feedback and facilitate comment resolution. Perform other duties as assigned. Additional job responsibilities, at the A23.3 level Develop, plan, review, assess, analyze, and implement administrative processes, procedures, and practices by applying in depth knowledge to ensure SBK activities comply with governing requirements, including federal regulations, LLNL procedures, and nuclear facility safety basis documents. Provide professional support to program/practice/policy development and implementation efforts; assists with program research and ongoing monitoring of results. Serves as a subject matter expert and trusted resource, providing informed recommendations to management on policy updates and changes. Ability to secure and maintain a U.S. DOE Q level security clearance which requires U.S. citizenship. Associate Degree in a related field or equivalent combination of education and related experience in a business, operational and/or organizational area. Experience interpreting, reviewing and analyzing administrative processes, policies, procedures and practices to determine if the activities they address are performed in compliance with complex regulations and requirements. Effective technical composition, writing and editing skills and experience effectively composing professional documentation with the ability to obtain a Procedure Professionals Association (PPA) Certification. Experience tracking, compiling and monitoring data necessary to coordinate corrective actions. Proficient verbal and written communication skills necessary to manage scientific and technical communications across multidisciplinary teams, with effective collaboration and communication skills necessary to effectively explain and present proposed changes to documents and processes. Effective organizational and interpersonal skills necessary to resolve problems and sensitive/confidential issues with tact, discretion, and mature judgment. Strong proficiency in Microsoft Word and a solid working knowledge of Excel, FileMaker Pro, Adobe Acrobat, and EDMS (such as SharePoint or Windchill) with the ability to learn new software quickly. Additional qualifications at the A23.3 level Experience researching, tracking, compiling and monitoring data necessary to conduct self-assessment activities, effectively present findings, and coordinate corrective actions. Broad and specialized knowledge of and experience in related work activities and multi-faceted internal processes. Experience training and mentoring personnel on document control within a regulated environment, ensuring compliance with applicable requirements. Knowledge and proficiency in systems, particularly MS Excel and SAP, is critical. Experience with SAP costing required. Previous supervisory experience preferred.

Johnson Controls, a leading provider of HVAC and building automation solutions, is seeking a skilled and experienced Operations and Maintenance Specialist to join our team. We are excited to announce a fantastic opportunity at the newly constructed electric vehicle battery manufacturing plant. The objective is to maintain a seamless environment by assuring that equipment is performing to specifications to facilitate uninterrupted manufacturing and administrative functions. What you will do: We are looking for a skilled specialist who has worked in commercial, industrial, and/or institutional markets to join our team. The specialist must be a skilled craftsman in their trade, and we prefer a minimum of five (5) years’ actual, practical working experience in the HVAC plumbing, pipefitting and/or mechanical equipment service industry.
